field: Reversible cellular automata and physical lattices: Margolus block CA, the billiard-ball CA, Critters, partitioned CA (Morita), lattice gases (HPP/FHP), conservation laws, physical universality, and the Brownian/ballistic physics they sit on

sources.title: Conservative Logic (Fredkin, Toffoli 1982)
sources.quote: the essential function of this register is to provide the computation with spare room rather than tokens
sources.mechanism: Two primitives. The unit wire moves one bit one time step; storage and transmission are one primitive (p.4-5). The Fredkin gate is a 3-in, 3-out controlled swap: a bijection, its own inverse, and it conserves the number of 1s. Composition is one-to-one only ("we shall restrict the meaning of the term function composition to one-to-one composition", p.5), so fan-out must happen inside an explicit gate (p.5). Fan-out is a Fredkin gate fed constants (Fig. 6c: a with 0 and 1 gives a, a, not-a). A general circuit takes constants in and puts garbage out. The garbage-free scheme (sec. 7, Figs. 23-24) runs network F, reads the result with 'spy' devices fed a 0 and a 1 (p.20), then runs the inverse network. The argument comes back unchanged, the scratchpad comes back clean, and a preloaded result register of 2n slots (top half empty, bottom half full) is rearranged into y and not-y. The scratchpad can be all 0s (a proof due to Margolus), hence 'room rather than tokens'. It cannot be dropped: "the reversibility constraint makes a computing gearbox so tight that certain functions cannot be computed at all unless some 'play' is provided" (p.22). Dissipation can also happen without energy transfer: "by our losing knowledge (and thus control) of a mechanical mode's current state" (p.18), which moves the whole mode from mechanical to thermal. The physical model is the billiard-ball model: balls plus fixed mirrors, where a possible-collision site is the interaction gate (outputs pq, not-p q, p not-q, pq).
sources.relevance: (a) Analogy: disp's duplicator can be read as Fredkin fan-out. A node is copied only by consuming constants, and un-copying returns them. Note that Fredkin fan-out also emits not-a as a byproduct. (b) 'Room, not tokens' reframes the history tc needs as borrowed blank space that running the inverse returns clean, instead of records keyed by ids. (c) F; spy; F-inverse is the spatial form of iso.rs's `bennett` (evaluators/rust-ic-strands/crate/src/iso.rs:373), with every gate running at once. (d) Dissipation is a matter of what the system can still track. A dropped K argument the system could rebuild need not be counted as heat yet.

sources.title: Physics-like models of computation (Margolus 1984)
sources.quote: only 2 states per cell in a 4 cell neighbourhood, is reversible, and conserves the number of ones
sources.mechanism: Introduces the 2x2 block partition (now called the Margolus neighbourhood). One block rule maps a block's 4 bits to 4 bits, and the blocking alternates between 'solid' and 'dotted' each step (p.5). In the BBMCA (billiard-ball cellular automaton) rule, a lone 1 moves to the opposite corner, so it travels in a straight diagonal line. Two 1s on a diagonal switch to the other diagonal, which gives the billiard-ball collision. The other cases do not change. "Since each distinct initial state of a block is mapped onto a distinct final state, this rule is reversible" (p.6). The two moving cases are involutions, so the rule is its own inverse (Margolus 1999 states this explicitly for the BBMCA), and the run reverses by reapplying it with the blockings in reverse order. A 2x2 square of 1s straddling two blocks is stable, and a mirror is two adjacent stable squares (p.8). Collisions cost a slight delay. Universality comes from translating any BBM circuit. Side results on p.6: a rule can conserve 1s without being reversible, so 'the existence of an interesting local conservation law does not depend on the rule being reversible'. For a non-bijective block rule you can count each result block's possible predecessors, so "we can count exactly how much information is lost at each step". In the BBM, kinetic energy is conserved but momentum is not, because mirrors are fixed (p.7).
sources.relevance: The strand lattice already confines every move to a 2x2x2 block. The BBMCA shows the move itself can be a permutation of the block's contents. Reversibility then needs no records, bonds or acceptance probability, and the inverse is the same table run with the blockings reversed, at exactly forward cost. The repo's phys=1 substrate takes 10-12x the forward clocks to go back (evaluators/rust-ic-strands/README.md:1529). For lossy tree-calculus steps (K drop, triage, erase), the per-block predecessor count gives an exact information-loss meter for that step.

sources.title: Invertible cellular automata: A review (Toffoli, Margolus 1990)
sources.quote: a pair of consecutive configurations suffice to determine in a unique way also the backward trajectory
sources.mechanism: A catalogue of ways to build invertible CA, organised around a 'landscape': a site's update is a permutation of its own state, chosen by its neighbourhood. That landscape must be recognisable going backward (p.9). (5.3) Conserved-landscape permutations: the landscapes that trigger a change are themselves never created or destroyed. The example is Patt's 1D rule, found by search. (5.4) Second-order rule: q(t+1) = f(neighbourhood of q(t)) - q(t-1) mod r. Solving for q(t-1) gives the inverse for ANY f, so every CA yields an invertible one on the pair (q(t-1), q(t)). "In general, second-order relations give rise to noninvertible dynamics" (p.11); only this subtractive form is safe. Q2R, a microcanonical Ising model (flip a spin iff 2 of its 4 neighbours are up, i.e. iff bond energy is unchanged), is given here as a second-order example. (5.5) Partitioning: cut space into blocks, apply a block permutation, alternate the blocking. (5.6) Lattice gases. Toffoli 1977 showed any CA can be embedded in an invertible one "having one more dimension" (p.5). Kari, Theorem 4.5: no effective procedure decides whether an arbitrary TWO-dimensional CA, given by its local map, is invertible (p.8). A reversible design also needs circuitry "analogous to energy supply and heat removal in ordinary computers" (p.6).
sources.relevance: (a) Write disp's core as block or landscape permutations, never as an arbitrary local map. Reversibility is then checked per table entry, instead of being undecidable in general (2D and up). (b) The second-order rule is the cleanest known case of 'history as a resource'. Any rule, including lossy K and triage, becomes reversible if each site keeps its previous value and the new value is combined with it instead of appended. Whether this extends to growing trees is open. (c) Landscape permutations fit strand moves: a wire end moves only in a way chosen by neighbours held fixed during that block step.

sources.title: Crystalline Computation (Margolus 1999)
sources.quote: This heatbath CA is perfectly invertible, since applying the dynamics twice to the same sublattice leaves both the spins and the heatbath unchanged
sources.mechanism: A survey of physics-like CA. Critters (p.12) is a 2x2 Margolus rule, rotationally symmetric, mapping each of the 16 block states to a distinct state, so it is invertible. The number of 1s before equals the number of 0s after, so counting 1s as particles on even steps and 0s on odd steps conserves particles. Parity along each diagonal of each block is also conserved. The exact table is in Fig. 1.5b; the usual statement is that two-1 blocks are unchanged, all others are complemented, and the three-1 case is also rotated 180 degrees. Critters is universal: glider collisions act as BBMCA collisions, and "Mirrors can be implemented by two single Critters particles" (p.18). "All invertible CA's can be reexpressed isomorphically in a partitioning format—where conservations and invertibility are manifest" (p.12). The HPP gas in block form is its own inverse, so a pressure wave runs back exactly to its starting square: "a messy state can always be cleaned up if you undo exactly the sequence of actions that produced the mess" (p.20). Ising CA (p.4): flip a spin iff exactly 2 of its 4 neighbours are 1s (bond energy unchanged), updating one sublattice at a time. Creutz heat-bath CA (p.7): each site of a 3D Ising CA gets a few heatbath bits read as an energy. A flip that changes bond energy is allowed iff the heatbath can absorb or supply the difference. Temperature is controlled by resetting heatbath values, and the dynamics stays exactly invertible. Warnings: force-carrying field particles fill space and "cannot be erased because of local invertibility" (p.30). In discrete systems, Fredkin argues, conservation, not symmetry, is fundamental (p.30 footnote). For quantum CA, "replace invertible transformations on groups of bits with unitary transformations" (p.32).
sources.relevance: A Creutz-style demon could replace the repo's global drive (Metropolis acceptance, evaluators/rust-ic-strands/README.md:113). Each site carries a small energy counter. A move that releases energy deposits it there, one that needs energy draws from it, and an erase deposits its cost locally. The move stays a bijection on (agents + counters). Critters says to build routing out of the same particles as data. The field-particle warning applies to mediator agents: if mediators are emitted and never reabsorbed, a reversible lattice clogs.

sources.title: Universal Cellular Automata Based on the Collisions of Soft Spheres (Margolus 2002/2008)
sources.quote: These constants are passed back and forth between adjacent Fredkin gates, and so don’t have to be supplied from outside of the array
sources.mechanism: A soft-sphere model (SSM) run as a lattice gas. Each site holds up to 8 particles (4 diagonal and 4 axis directions). A step moves every particle one site along its direction, then applies an independent per-site interaction (p.4). "when two diagonal particles collide at right angles, they turn into a single particle moving in the direction of the net momentum" (p.5), which turns back into two diagonal particles at the next site, displaced inward. Read relativistically (p.19), two 'photons' make a slower massive particle that decays back into two photons after one step. Without fixed mirrors, so with exact momentum conservation, signals are deflected by 'mirror streams' of constant 1s, "which brings in energy but no information" (p.9), while garbage streams carry energy and entropy away. Plain signals deflected this way get copied into the mirror stream; dual-rail (complementary) signals reflect cleanly (p.8). Rest particles let signals cross. If streams are used once, they must cross a surface around the circuit, so throughput scales with surface, not volume (p.9). The fix is a regular array of Fredkin and upside-down Fredkin gates that passes constants between neighbours (p.12), on which a universal CA such as the BBMCA is run. The 'proto-SSM' (Fig. 17) separates logic value from momentum: zeros and ones are both particles, and a third, wavy particle formed from two colliding ones deflects both values without contaminating the mirror stream. The general advice is to use "some other degree of freedom (other than presence or absence of a particle) to encode the logic state" (p.20). Conclusion: "it is possible to avoid entropy generation associated with routing signals" (p.21). An energy-conserving lattice gas of energy E changes at most 2E spots per step, matching the quantum bound.
sources.relevance: The user's 'bosons' correspond to these mirror streams: they carry energy or momentum but no information. The paper gives two rules such mediators must follow. (i) They must not read the data they steer (dual rail, or both values as particles), or they leave as garbage. (ii) They must be handed back to neighbours for reuse, or throughput is capped by the computer's surface. The fusion-decay collision also suggests running an interaction-net active pair as one composite agent for one step, which then decays into the products, keeping each step a bijection.

sources.title: Reversible computing and cellular automata - A survey (Morita 2008, preprint of TCS 395)
sources.quote: its state can be regarded as a kind of stationary signal that is always at the element’s position
sources.mechanism: Covers reversible gates and garbage-free circuits: connect the circuit and its inverse in series, and "garbage signals are erased reversibly, and we get again constants, which can be recycled" (p.6, after copying the true outputs). Also covers reversible logic elements with memory (RLEM) and reversible CA. The rotary element (RE) has a bar in one of two states (horizontal or vertical) and 4 input and 4 output lines. A particle arriving parallel to the bar goes straight. "If a particle comes from a direction orthogonal to the bar, then it makes a right turn" and rotates the bar 90 degrees (p.10). Any reversible sequential machine has a 'completely garbageless' RE circuit, with no lines other than the true inputs and outputs (Thm 2.5, p.11-12). Reversible Turing machines can likewise be built from REs (p.21). Bennett: any TM can be simulated by a reversible one that "leaves no garbage information on its tape when it halts" (p.2). Partitioned CA (PCA): each cell is split into parts, one per neighbour, and the new cell is f(parts arriving from the neighbours). "f is one-to-one iff F is one-to-one" (Prop. 4.1, p.29). Universal reversible CA include a 1D PCA simulating a reversible TM (Morita-Harao), the 16-state PCAs S1 and S2, the 8-state triangular T1, and an 81-state PCA P3 running reversible counter machines from REs, in which "computation is carried out by a single signal that interacts with REs and position markers" (p.39). Self-reproduction exists in 2D and 3D reversible PCAs (p.44).
sources.relevance: (a) PCA is the formal model of a strand-lattice site with its switchboard. Each site's state splits into per-neighbour ports, a step swaps ports with neighbours and applies one table per site, and checking that table is injective is the whole reversibility check. (b) The RE token machine is the CA counterpart of iso.rs's walking-token machine (removed in 2a32736, history in eca0073). It is garbage-free and reusable, but it has one token per program, so one program runs sequentially; parallel work needs many tokens or many copies. (c) Elements with memory need no clock: the resting state waits for the moving token.

sources.title: Representing Reversible Cellular Automata with Reversible Block Cellular Automata (Durand-Lose 2001)
sources.quote: We built a simulation in linear time of reversible cellular automata by reversible block cellular automata
sources.mechanism: A block permutation applies one permutation of a finite block's contents across a regular partition of the lattice. Main result: any d-dimensional reversible CA is the composition of d+1 block permutations. This proves the Toffoli-Margolus 1990 conjecture for all d; Kari 1996 had proved it for d = 1, 2 with a count exponential in d. The construction works by progressively erasing previous states and adding next states. Intermediate cells hold both their previous and next state (alphabet S ∪ S²), the d+1 partitions are offset from each other by (3r, ..., 3r), and block width grows with the radius r of the CA and its inverse. Reversible block CA also simulate any reversible CA in linear time, on finite and infinite configurations. The paper notes that reversibility of a general CA is undecidable in dimension above 1 but easy to check for block CA, and that block CA are not Morita's partitioned CA.
sources.relevance: This supports restricting disp's physical core to block permutations without losing any reversible local dynamics, but at a cost: the general construction needs blocks sized to the rule's radius and a temporarily doubled alphabet (each cell holding old and new state). It does NOT show that a fixed 2x2x2 table on the original alphabet with 4 alternating offsets is enough. Related: Arrighi-Nesme (arXiv 1201.5529) note that in 2D an exact block representation needs three layers and cannot be done with two (Kari 1999).

sources.title: Reversible quantum cellular automata (Schumacher, Werner 2004)
sources.quote: any quantum cellular automaton is structurally reversible, i.e., that it can be obtained by applying two blockwise unitary operations
sources.mechanism: A quantum CA (QCA) is translation-invariant, causal unitary dynamics on a quantum lattice. Structure theorem: every QCA is two layers of block unitaries in a generalised Margolus partition. Unlike the classical case, the inverse of a nearest-neighbour QCA is again nearest-neighbour (Cor. 7). Constructions include: quantising reversible classical CA, whose configuration permutation becomes a permutation unitary (this needs the classical inverse to be local too; the rule c(x) + c(x-1) + c(x+1) mod 2 has no quantum version); Clifford QCAs; and number-conserving quantum lattice gases, whose single-particle sector is a quantum walk.
sources.relevance: A block-permutation core is trivially a partitioned QCA run in the classical basis, so it has a direct unitary reading. Every step that is not a bijection (Metropolis acceptance, erase, forget) is exactly the part that would need an explicit environment (heat sink) on a quantum substrate. That pins down where the physics has to be added.

sources.title: Lattice Gas Hydrodynamics in Two and Three Dimensions (Frisch, d'Humières, Hasslacher, Lallemand, Pomeau, Rivet 1987)
sources.quote: the four-bit states (1, 0, 1, 0) and (0, 1, 0, 1) are exchanged; all other states are left unchanged
sources.mechanism: Each node has one Boolean cell per lattice direction, with an exclusion principle of at most one particle per node per direction. An update is collision (local, per node) then propagation (each particle hops one link). HPP (square lattice): the only nontrivial collision turns a head-on pair onto the other axis, conserving mass and momentum. But "momentum is conserved along each horizontal and vertical line, resulting in far too many conserved quantities for physical modeling" (p.6), and the model is not isotropic. FHP moves to the triangular lattice for the larger symmetry group. Its head-on collisions have two outcomes, picked with equal probability or pseudo-randomly (for example by the parity of a time or space index). Head-on-only collisions there still conserve a spurious quantity, the particle difference in each opposite pair, which triple collisions remove (FHP-I, p.7). FHP-II/III add rest particles and 'spectator' collisions. Semi-detailed balance (the summed transition probability into each state is 1) "is trivially satisfied when the collision rule is deterministic and one-to-one" (p.12).
sources.relevance: Collide-then-propagate is a clean step shape for the strand lattice: (1) at each site, a bijection on what sits there (the tree-calculus rewrite table); (2) shift wire ends along their strands. The exclusion principle corresponds to one wire end per port. Two cautions. Designed rules can carry spurious invariants that change the large-scale behaviour, so check what each disp table conserves besides the intended quantities. And one-to-one collision rules satisfy semi-detailed balance, so they keep the uniform distribution stationary. That random scheduling of bijective moves adds no hidden bias is an extrapolation from this, not something the paper shows.

sources.title: A Physically Universal Cellular Automaton (Schaeffer 2014)
sources.quote: implement any transformation on a finite region of the CA by initializing the complement of the region
sources.mechanism: A Margolus 2x2 CA in which a lone particle moves to the opposite corner each step, so it travels diagonally. The rule must be symmetric under rotation and reflection, conserve particles, and be bijective ("A Margolus neighbourhood CA is reversible if and only if the update rule, ρ, is bijective", p.4). Up to symmetry there are four collision kinds, and eight CAs meet the conditions (p.5). In the chosen one, two-particle blocks (opposing or at right angles) behave as if the particles pass through, and the three-particle case is the only real interaction. Swapping it too would give 'no particle interactions'; changing the opposing-pair rule instead gives HPP (p.6). The exact table is in Fig. 1. The paper proves physical universality (Janzing's notion): any function on a finite region's contents can be carried out by preparing only the surroundings and letting the system evolve, in time polynomial in the region and circuit size. BBMCA fails this test: "It is possible to construct immovable, impenetrable walls in Margolus's CA" (p.2).
sources.relevance: A design test for disp's core: nothing may be immovable. Routing, 'mirrors', wires and the program itself must be ordinary matter that other matter can take apart and rebuild. Physical universality is the formal version of 'no privileged infrastructure'.

sources.title: The Thermodynamics of Computation - a Review (Bennett 1982)
sources.quote: would cause the Brownian computer to spend most of its time bogged down in extraneous predecessors of states on the intended path
sources.mechanism: Two physical regimes. Ballistic (billiard balls): no dissipation at finite speed, but sensitive to small perturbations (p.6). Brownian: thermal noise makes the computer random-walk along its computation graph under a small drive, and "the drift velocity is proportional to the driving force, and hence the energy dissipated approaches zero only in the limit of zero speed" (p.1). Logically irreversible steps (merges) give states extra predecessors, so the walk wanders into them unless about kT ln 2 is paid per merge (p.2). Fig. 10 (p.19) separates three cases. In an unbranched graph a tiny drive works. In a slightly branched graph a small drive still works, but the computation is slower because of detours. In an exponentially branched graph, holding the walk on the intended path needs a dissipation per step of about kT times the log of the mean number of immediate predecessors. A one-time 'latching energy' at the last step keeps the machine in its final state (p.17). A history tape makes any machine reversible, but the machine has then "only postponed the problem of throwing away unwanted information by using the extra tape as a garbage dump" (p.18). Compute-copy-uncompute cleans it up.
sources.relevance: The phys=1 substrate is already a Brownian computer with one drive for every rewrite. Bennett suggests the drive should differ by rule. Bijective moves need only an arbitrarily small bias. A lossy rule (K drop, triage, erase) should carry about kT ln(number of predecessors it creates) where its backward branching compounds; otherwise the walk spends its time in extraneous predecessors. Price each rule by the information it loses, and add a latching cost at the final answer. It is a hypothesis, not a measured fact, that this branching explains the substrate's slow reversal.

sources.title: Brownian Circuits: Designs (Lee, Peper, et al. 2016)
sources.quote: they use fluctuations to make tokens backtrack their way out of deadlocks
sources.mechanism: A Brownian circuit is "a token-based circuit, in which tokens are allowed to fluctuate forwards and backwards on lines and across operators" (p.3). It extends conservative delay-insensitive (CDI) circuits, which tolerate any signal delay and conserve tokens ("the number of input tokens to a module equals the number of output tokens", p.4). Three primitives (p.4-6). Hub: 3 bidirectional lines, at most one token, which may move onto any of them. CJoin: one token on each of two inputs passes, as a pair, to the two outputs, and the operation can be reversed. Ratchet: lets a token pass one way but blocks it coming back, so it 'imposes a direction' on a line. Ratchets are placed selectively, for example at inputs to lock tokens in (p.20). From these the Merge and 2x2-CJoin, a universal set for CDI circuits, are built. Fluctuation lets tokens back out of deadlocks, so the circuits need less deadlock-avoidance machinery than earlier designs. Hardware discussed: single-electron tunnelling (SET). Lee and Peper's Brownian CA (ref. 12) lay such circuits on an asynchronous CA.
sources.relevance: The closest model to the repo's random-proposal lattice. It suggests making rewrites unbiased (reversible, unrecorded) and placing 'ratchets' only where commitment is wanted: after a lossy rule, and at the final answer (compare Bennett's latching). Random back-and-forth then undoes stuck states instead of a drive on every rewrite.

key_ideas: Make the core a permutation table on block contents applied on alternating partitions (Margolus 1984; Toffoli-Margolus 1990). Reversibility is then checked per table entry, while for an arbitrary local map in 2D or more it is undecidable (Kari, via the 1990 review). Every reversible CA is d+1 block permutations (Durand-Lose 2001), but only with blocks sized to the rule's radius and a temporarily doubled alphabet. A fixed 2x2x2 table on the original alphabet is a real restriction. Block permutations are permutation unitaries, so the core has a direct quantum reading (Schumacher-Werner 2004). For a self-inverse block rule like the BBMCA, reversal costs exactly forward time with no records, versus 10-12x forward in the current phys=1 substrate.

Split the step into collide-then-propagate (HPP/FHP, Frisch et al. 1987): a bijective rewrite table on what sits at a site (or block), then a shift of wire ends along strands. One wire end per port plays the role of the exclusion principle. Check each table for unintended extra conserved quantities (HPP conserves momentum on every row and column), which change large-scale behaviour. One-to-one collision rules keep the uniform distribution stationary (semi-detailed balance).

Treat a site as a partitioned-CA cell (Morita 2008): its state splits into per-neighbour ports, and correctness reduces to 'the site table is injective' (f one-to-one iff F one-to-one). This fits the strand switchboard directly. Note that Morita PCA and Margolus block CA are different classes.

Copying is Fredkin fan-out (Fredkin-Toffoli 1982): a with constants 0 and 1 becomes (a, a, not-a), and un-copying is the inverse gate, which gives the constants back. Composition is one-to-one, so linearity is structural and fan-out lives only in explicit gates.

Make the vacuum countable: Critters counts 0s as particles on odd steps, and the proto-SSM makes zeros and ones both particles (Margolus 1999, 2002). Fuel is then blank particles: copying draws them and un-copying refunds them, and particle number (matter + blanks) can be checked per block.

History is borrowed room, not a log (Fredkin-Toffoli 1982): the garbage-free scheme needs a scratchpad that provides 'spare room rather than tokens' and comes back clean when the inverse network runs (F; spy; F-inverse, the spatial form of iso.rs `bennett` with all gates running at once). Some functions cannot be computed reversibly without that room.

Second-order rule (Toffoli-Margolus 1990): q(t+1) = f(q(t)) - q(t-1) mod r makes ANY local rule invertible by keeping exactly one step of history and using it up every step. It is the cleanest known case of history as a resource that is consumed, not appended.

Local energy accounting with Creutz heat-bath bits (Margolus 1999): each site holds a small energy counter, and a flip happens iff the counter can absorb or supply the energy change. The dynamics stays exactly invertible on (spins + counters), and temperature is set by the counters' energy. This could replace the global Metropolis drive with a local, conserved quantity.

Price each rule by the information it loses (Bennett 1982; Margolus 1984 per-block predecessor count). Bijective moves need almost no bias. Where lossy steps (K drop, triage, erase) cause compounding backward branching, the bias must be about kT ln(mean number of predecessors). Put 'ratchets' only at commitment points and at the final answer (Bennett's latching energy; ratchets in Brownian circuits, Lee et al. 2016), and elsewhere let unbiased fluctuation get out of stuck states.

Mediators ('bosons') are mirror streams (Margolus SSM): they carry energy or momentum but no information. They must not read the data they steer (dual rail, or both bit values as particles), or they leave as garbage. They must be handed back to neighbours for reuse, or the computer's throughput scales with its surface instead of its volume. Mediators emitted and never reabsorbed clog a reversible lattice (Margolus 1999).

Run an interaction as a short-lived composite particle (SSM: two diagonal particles colliding at right angles become one particle along the net momentum, which then turns back into two). An active pair can be one agent for one step, then decay into the products, keeping each step a bijection.

Garbage policy as geometry (SSM, Fredkin-Toffoli): garbage either stays as local matter and is reclaimed by the inverse, or streams out through the boundary. Because boundary flux bounds throughput, local uncompute is a physical necessity at scale. Losing track of a mode, even with no energy transfer, is what makes it heat (Fredkin-Toffoli p.18), so a dropped K argument the system can still rebuild need not count as heat.

Element with memory (Morita's rotary element): a site's resting state plus one moving token gives a garbage-free, reusable, clock-free machine. This is the CA counterpart of iso.rs's removed token machine, and it shows that machine's limit: one token means one program runs sequentially. Parallel work needs many tokens or self-reproducing copies (which exist in 2D and 3D reversible PCA).

No immovable infrastructure (Schaeffer 2014; Critters vs. BBMCA): BBMCA's fixed mirrors are walls that rule out physical universality, while Critters builds mirrors from ordinary particles. In disp, routing and wiring should be the same matter as the program, so other matter can rebuild or reclaim them.

Very small universal reversible 2D CA exist. Morita's elementary triangular partitioned CA (cells split into three one-bit parts) are each described 'by only four local rules' ([Morita 2017](https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~kyodo/kokyuroku/contents/pdf/2040-02.pdf#page=1)), and the non-conservative T0347 is universal using gliders as signals. This is an existence example, not a lower bound, but it shows a disp core with dozens of agent kinds and rules is far from the simplest known universal reversible substrate.

Time symmetry as a precise form of 'conceptually reversible': 'a CA G is time-symmetric if G is its own inverse up to a simple recoding H of the cells', G-inverse = HGH with H self-inverse ([Arrighi-Nesme 2012](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1201.5529#page=1)). With a cell-wise involution such as flipping each agent's direction bit, running backward needs no second rule set. The direction-bit example is a design suggestion, not from the paper.

field: Reversible logic elements with memory (RLEMs: Morita's rotary element and the 2-state elements), delay-insensitive and token-based asynchronous circuits (Keller; Patra and Fussell's conservative circuits), Brownian circuits and Brownian cellular automata (Lee, Peper and colleagues), plus their physical versions (fluxon swap gates, skyrmion and quantum-dot tokens) and how much energy they cost. Focus: elements whose state returns after use, tokens moving locally, parallelism, and noise as the driver.

sources.title: Towards a Theory of Universal Speed-Independent Modules
sources.quote: No set of serial modules can be universal for the set of all modules
sources.mechanism: Modules are finite-state machines (Q is a finite set of states) whose inputs and outputs are signal events on lines. There is no clock, and lines can have any delay. Condition 2: a module ['once having created a signal on a line, cannot'](https://web.archive.org/web/20240502171700id_/https://scholarship.claremont.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1288&context=hmc_fac_pub#page=3) withdraw it before the receiver takes it. A serial module is one where every input signal ['must be followed by exactly one output signal on some line before another input can be applied'](https://web.archive.org/web/20240502171700id_/https://scholarship.claremont.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1288&context=hmc_fac_pub#page=4). Theorem 2.1: Merge plus Select (two internal states; set by S, reset by R, tested by T, and the test signal leaves on one of two outputs by state) is universal for serial modules. Theorem 3.1 (the quote): serial modules can never build a parallel module (examples: Join, Fork). Theorem 3.2: {Merge, Select, Fork, Arbitrating Test-and-Set} is universal for all modules. The construction funnels the parallel module's inputs one at a time through a lock-unlock module (built from Fork, Merge, ATS, with a busy-waiting circulating signal), runs a serial core, then fans outputs back out with Forks and Merges. So general universality needs a fork plus an arbiter, not necessarily a Join. No notion of reversibility; Merge loses which input fired.
sources.relevance: The theorem behind 'how parallel was the old token machine': a program built only from one-token-in, one-token-out elements is a serial module, so one token walking a laid-out program (the removed iso Machine) was sequential by construction. Keller's own route to full universality is a serial core plus fork and an arbiter, which says parallelism needs two extra ingredients: something that emits two tokens and something that decides which of two simultaneous tokens goes first. Keller's no-withdraw condition is exactly what Brownian circuits drop on purpose, and dropping it is what lets noise replace the arbiter (see Peper et al. 2013).

sources.title: The Thermodynamics of Computation — a Review
sources.quote: the energy dissipated approaches zero only in the limit of zero speed
sources.mechanism: A Brownian computer makes transitions only through thermal agitation: it random-walks back and forth along its logically reversible computation path, with a drift from a weak driving force; drift velocity is proportional to the force, so dissipation per step vanishes only as speed does. Bennett states the per-step cost directly: with reactants 10% off equilibrium RNA polymerase makes ['11 forward steps for each 10 backward steps'](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/863.18/notes/computation/Bennett-1982.pdf#page=10), dissipating kT ln(11/10) ≈ 0.1 kT per net forward step. Real copying enzymes are ['nature's closest approach to a Brownian computer, dissipating 20-100kT per step'](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/863.18/notes/computation/Bennett-1982.pdf#page=1). A logically irreversible computation bogs down in extraneous predecessor states ['unless an extra driving force of kTln2 were applied (and dissipated) at each merge point'](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/863.18/notes/computation/Bennett-1982.pdf#page=2); for branching backward trees the needed dissipation is ['about k T times the logarithm of the mean number of immediate predecessors'](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/863.18/notes/computation/Bennett-1982.pdf#page=19). Models: an enzymatic Turing machine; history is handled by Bennett's 1973 history tape (run, copy output, run backward).
sources.relevance: The cost model for a noise-driven disp: forward progress is paid by the bias, kT ln(forward rate / backward rate) per net step, not by a walker. Every rule that merges states (K dropping its argument, triage dropping untaken arms) either needs extra drive of about kT times log(number of predecessors) or lets the walk wander into a growing tree of predecessor states. So make every rule injective first and drive with a small uniform bias.

sources.title: A Framework for Conservative and Delay-insensitive Computing (UT Austin tech report TR95-10)
sources.quote: An event is pushed into the stack if otherwise it would be destroyed
sources.mechanism: Each signal event is an object ['distinguishable only by the associated I/O channel']. [Merge and Mutex are conservative but not invertible](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/ftp/techreports/tr95-10.pdf#page=7); Joins, Fork and Tria are invertible but not conservative; Toggle is conservative. The [Cjoin](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/ftp/techreports/tr95-10.pdf#page=8) doubles each output terminal of a Join, so a pair of input events yields two output events. {Merge, Ctria, Mutex} is universal for conservative DI circuits; note the arbiter (Mutex) is still a primitive. Any Keller-class DI spec can be built as a 'marginally conservative' circuit (Sinks and extra outputs allowed only up to the external output count). For a spec that is itself conservative, a Storage Stack removes the Sinks: push takes two events and returns an acknowledgement, pop takes one and returns two, operations are strictly serial, capacity at most 2d (d = largest input/output gap in any trace), pre-loaded with stored events when outputs can run ahead of inputs. Claim: DI systems can be asymptotically non-dissipating ['without the need for explicit uncomputation of results'](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/ftp/techreports/tr95-10.pdf#page=1).
sources.relevance: The origin of the CJoin and a concrete token ledger: take extra outputs from a reservoir of stored tokens and push would-be-destroyed tokens back into it. It applies to disp only if each program's token count balances overall; otherwise the ledger leaks. On a lattice the central serial stack would have to become a local gas of blank tokens (inference), with heat paid only when a token carrying unknown information is reset.

sources.title: A Simple Universal Logic Element and Cellular Automata for Reversible Computing (MCU 2001, LNCS 2055)
sources.quote: it makes a right turn, and rotates the bar by 90 degrees counterclockwise
sources.mechanism: Rotary element (RE): 2 states, H or V, 4 input and 4 output lines, at most one particle at a time. Parallel to the bar it passes straight with no state change; orthogonal to the bar it turns right and rotates the bar 90°. Formally a reversible sequential machine with injective move function. RE circuits forbid fan-out. Any reversible Turing machine is built from REs: a tape-cell module (two RE columns) stores the symbol s AND whether the head is on that square (h), and a finite-state control module is a matrix of REs; the single signal shuttles between control and tape cells as commands and completions. Because a signal meets only one element at a time, ['there is no need to provide a clock signal'](https://www.cs.auckland.ac.nz/~cristian/UMCreadings/revcomputCA.pdf#page=12). The RE is also embedded in P3, a rotation-symmetric reversible partitioned CA with 3^4 states per cell and 13 rule schemes (81 rules), where a single dot acts as the signal.
sources.relevance: The smallest 'matter + messenger' interaction: a resting element with 1 bit, a moving token, and one injective scattering table. This is the shape the removed iso token machine had. disp could make leaf/stem/fork stationary elements and apply/evaluate the tokens, but a single token keeps it sequential (Keller).

sources.title: On Reversible Computation in Asynchronous Systems (with the 2002 UMC paper 'Reversible Computation in Asynchronous Cellular Automata')
sources.quote: reversibility is not closed under circuit composition
sources.mechanism: The RE (one signal at a time) is embedded in a self-timed CA whose cells update at independent random times. In the 2002 paper each cell has 4 bits, a transition reads its own 4 bits plus one bit of each of its 4 neighbours, and embedding a universal reversible TM ['requires merely four rotation-symmetric transition rules, which are bit-conserving and locally reversible'](https://www2.nict.go.jp/nano/results/abstract/14_48.html); the model is shown globally reversible. The later paper also proposes a new delay-insensitive reversible element with 3 inputs, 3 outputs and 2 states and proves it universal by building an RE. Then for circuits with more than one signal, ['a simple reordering of signal arrival times may (or may not) destroy their reversibility'](https://www2.nict.go.jp/nano/results/abstract/17_217.html); they analyse an irreversible multi-signal circuit built from reversible elements and only 'speculate' about reasons and repairs.
sources.relevance: (a) Four bit-conserving, locally reversible rules suffice on an asynchronous lattice, so the strand lattice's block moves could be that small. (b) The warning: with several tokens at once, reversible elements no longer compose into a backward-deterministic circuit, because arrival order becomes hidden information. disp must either keep some record where tokens meet (inference; the paper leaves this open) or settle for statistical reversibility (Brownian).

sources.title: Efficient Computation in Brownian Cellular Automata
sources.quote: any update of cells using these rules can always be followed by a reversed update undoing it
sources.mechanism: An asynchronous CA in which signal configurations propagate randomly, like Brownian motion. Three kinds of rules: two are locally reversible and rotation-symmetric, so their updates can always be undone; ['The third transition rule is not reversible and is merely used for diffusive purposes'](https://www2.nict.go.jp/nano/results/abstract/peper/peper090923.html), letting signals fluctuate forward and backward on wires. These three rules embed arbitrary asynchronous circuits, so the CA is universal. Arbitration and choice come from active backtracking of cell updates. Speed-ups: confine the Brownian motion inside primitive-element configurations so wires need no backward propagation, and add ratchets on input and output lines.
sources.relevance: The closest relative of the strand lattice's Metropolis moves, except its circuit is fixed. It shows noise plus reversible local rules plus a few ratchets gives arbitration for free, which suggests replacing priority rules and walker logic with diffusion plus reversible meeting rules.

sources.title: Brownian Circuits: Fundamentals (ACM JETC 9(1))
sources.quote: The T-element requires one token as input on its base line and one token on one of its choice lines
sources.mechanism: Token-pass circuits modelled as Petri nets. The T-element has two choice lines and a base line; one transition moves a base token and a choice token through together (2 in, 2 out); if both choice lines hold tokens the choice is arbitrary. {Merge, Fork, Tria} is universal for token-based DI circuits, so {TP-Merge, TP-Fork, TP-Tria} is universal for token-pass circuits. Corollary 4.5: a deadlock-free TP-Tria cannot be built from T-elements, but with fluctuations the circuit backtracks out of deadlocks, so ['signal fluctuations are essential for this primitive to be universal'](https://www.cs.upc.edu/~jordicf/Research/gavina/BIB/files/BrownianCircuits_JETC2013.pdf#page=2). Ratchets (one-way devices on lines) speed circuits up; they must go only where no backtracking is needed (e.g. output lines, outside the TP-Trias of a memory), and ratchets consume energy (citing Feynman).
sources.relevance: One primitive is universal once noise is allowed, and noise also replaces the arbiter that Keller and Patra-Fussell needed as a separate primitive. Its rule (two tokens meet and move on together) has the shape of an interaction-net active pair (inference). Placement rule for disp: make a move irreversible and energy-spending only where backtracking is never needed, e.g. after a result is committed or read out.

sources.title: Reversible Logic Elements with Memory and Their Universality (MCU 2013, EPTCS 128)
sources.quote: non-degenerate RLEMs are "all" universal besides only four exceptions
sources.mechanism: An RLEM is a reversible sequential machine with equal numbers of input and output symbols and an injective move function. There are 4, 14 and 55 non-degenerate 2-state k-symbol RLEMs for k = 2, 3, 4. Theorem 2: every non-degenerate 2-state RLEM with k > 2 is universal: each 3-symbol one can build RLEMs 2-3 and 2-4, which build 3-10, which builds the RE, and any k-symbol one reduces to a (k-1)-symbol one by feedback. Of the 2-symbol ones, 2-2, 2-3, 2-4 are non-universal and 2-17 was open, but ['any two combination among RLEMs 2-3, 2-4, and 2-17 is universal'](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1309.1264#page=11). RSM construction from REs: one RE column per state; the current state's column has its bottom RE in H, all others V. An incoming particle sets that bottom RE to V and emerges on the crossing line (state, input), which is wired to the next-state column, whose bottom RE it sets to H, then leaves on the output line; ['fan-out of an output is not allowed'](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1309.1264#page=4). In the billiard-ball model an RE ['consists of one stationary ball called a state ball'](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1309.1264#page=3) plus reflectors; any m-state k-symbol RLEM is BBM-realizable when k ≤ 4.
sources.relevance: A fully mapped design space: any non-degenerate 1-bit, 3-port element is universal, so a disp node agent can be that small. The RSM construction is a linear read: reading clears the state, the token's path carries the value, writing sets the new state, and all scratch elements are back to default afterwards, so a circuit is reused by routing tokens through it rather than copying it.

sources.title: Computation time and thermodynamic uncertainty relation of Brownian circuits
sources.quote: The CJoin is the only circuit element producing environment entropy
sources.mechanism: Three primitives (Hub, CJoin, Ratchet) with dual-rail encoding (the wire a token sits on is the bit). Hub: a junction where a token hops between branches and can come back. Ratchet: a unidirectional transition standing for readout, i.e. detecting a token. CJoin: synchronizes through two-token scattering, with forward and backward rates γ+ and γ−; it pushes computation forward (γ+ > γ−) at the cost of environment entropy. Computation time is the first-passage time to the finished state (adders simulated). Result: ['The computation can be completed in finite time without environment entropy production'](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.10735#page=1); the cost is paid by error-free output detection and the resets between cycles, and plays a minor role, unlike a logically reversible Brownian TM whose entropy production grows logarithmically with state-space size. Skyrmion version: the CJoin ['only allows for a token passage in pairs of two'](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.02097#page=3) (Brems, Kläui, Virnau 2021).
sources.relevance: An exact energy ledger: environment entropy comes only from biased CJoins; readout and reset carry the rest. For disp: bias only the meeting rules (active pairs) and the commit/readout step, leave wire motion and hub choices unbiased, and heat is booked where it is actually made.

sources.title: Asynchronous Reversible Computing Unveiled Using Ballistic Shift Registers (Phys. Rev. Applied 19, 054034)
sources.quote: Its operation consists of the elastic swapping of flux between the stored and the moving bit
sources.mechanism: Simulated superconducting ballistic shift register (BSR): a storage loop holds a flux quantum whose polarity is the stored bit; a fluxon moving along a long Josephson junction line is the moving bit, and the two swap elastically. Operation is powered by the input bits alone. A storage loop gives the asynchronous property: inputs may arrive at any time as long as their order is preserved. ['two BSRs operate in sequence without power added, giving a 2-bit sequential memory'](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.12999#page=1). A BSR with two input and two output ports lets a bit be set from one port and read out on either; the authors call it the first asynchronous reversible 2-input gate. Frank and Shukla's ballistic asynchronous reversible computing has the same picture: ['fluxons are conserved and interact asynchronously with stored flux quanta'](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.00065#page=43) at stateful elements.
sources.relevance: Proposes the swap as the base move: reading a cell takes what it holds and leaves what you brought, so nothing is copied, deleted or logged. A tree-walking token that swaps with the nodes it passes would keep its return path in the slots it emptied (inference, close to pointer-reversal tree walking), a local replacement for the old iso Machine's return stack. Note the order-preservation requirement: the BSR is asynchronous only in timing, not in input order.

sources.title: Join gate with memory in token-conserving Brownian circuits and the thermodynamic cost
sources.quote: a double quantum dot that functions as a one-bit memory, storing the direction of two-particle transfer
sources.mechanism: Repelling particles (electrons, skyrmions) make a local CJoin hard to design. The proposal synchronizes two moving particles indirectly, through their interaction with a localized particle in a double quantum dot; that dot is a one-bit internal state recording which way the last two-particle transfer went. A bit-wise periodic reset protocol makes the CJoin emit in one chosen direction. Under periodic resets the cost is ['the work done for resets minus the entropy reduction due to resets'](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.12390#page=1), with a lower bound within a few kT. The particle emission rate is bounded above by the subsystem's irreversible entropy-production rate and dynamical activity rate.
sources.relevance: A concrete device-level CJoin whose internal bit records the direction of the last pair transfer, with the bill (a few kT) paid when that bit is reset to drive the gate forward. Template for disp's active pair (inference): a rewrite could leave one bit at the meeting site, undoing uses it, and resetting it to push computation forward is where the heat goes.

sources.title: Phase transitions in time complexity of Brownian circuits
sources.quote: achieving efficient polynomial-time computation generally requires a finite forward bias corresponding to a nonzero energy input
sources.mechanism: Brownian circuits built from CJoins; computation time is the first-passage time to the completed state. For adders, varying the forward rate switches mean time against circuit size from linear to exponential, an easy-hard transition. Because a deterministic circuit funnels many initial states into one completed state, intermediate states typically have one forward and several backward transitions, a 'generic structural bias toward backward motion' that the forward rate must compensate; for a tree with branch number m the threshold is γ+ = mγ−. Counterexample: any logic reduces to an effective one-dimensional process that is easy even at zero bias, but ['achieving such a one-dimensional normal form unavoidably leads to an exponential increase in circuit size'](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.24728#page=1). Result: a trade-off between time, circuit size and energy.
sources.relevance: No free lunch for a noise-driven disp: polynomial time needs a finite bias per step, sized by the backward branching (γ+ > m γ−), unless the state graph is a single chain. A one-token RLEM circuit has a chain-shaped state graph, so it is cheap at zero bias but sequential; many tokens give parallelism but need bias (inference linking to Keller).

key_ideas: Matter and messengers as RLEMs: stationary elements hold 1 bit and conserved tokens move. Every interaction is one injective table (state, entry port) -> (state', exit port), with no fan-out and no copy or delete primitive ([Morita 2001](https://www.cs.auckland.ac.nz/~cristian/UMCreadings/revcomputCA.pdf#page=2); [Morita 2013](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1309.1264#page=1)). Any non-degenerate 1-bit element with 3 or more ports is universal, so leaf/stem/fork agents can be that small.

Swap as the linear read: an arriving token and the stored value trade places, so nothing is copied, deleted or logged ([Osborn and Wustmann 2022](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.12999#page=1); [Frank and Shukla 2021](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.00065#page=43)). A tree-walking token that swaps keeps its return path in the slots it emptied (inference), which would make the old iso Machine's return stack local. Caveat: the fluxon gate is asynchronous in timing but needs input order preserved.

Reusable circuits through destructive read plus position-encoded state: the token reads by clearing, carries the value as which line it is on, writes the new state, and every scratch element is back to default when it leaves, so a shared circuit is reused by routing tokens through it instead of copying it ([Morita 2013 RSM construction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1309.1264#page=4)).

Where parallelism lives: serial (one-in, one-out) elements can never build a parallel module ([Keller 1974, Thm 3.1](https://web.archive.org/web/20240502171700id_/https://scholarship.claremont.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1288&context=hmc_fac_pub#page=8)). Deterministic DI universality needs two extra ingredients, a fork/synchronizer and an arbiter (Keller's {Merge, Select, Fork, ATS}; Patra and Fussell's conservative set {Merge, Ctria, Mutex} built around the [Cjoin](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/ftp/techreports/tr95-10.pdf#page=8)). With noise the arbiter disappears: the single T-element (two tokens in, two out) is universal ([Peper et al. 2013](https://www.cs.upc.edu/~jordicf/Research/gavina/BIB/files/BrownianCircuits_JETC2013.pdf#page=2)). An interaction-net active pair has the same 2-in shape (inference), so in a noise-driven disp the rewrite rules could be the only synchronizers.

Concurrency breaks backward determinism: with several tokens, arrival order becomes hidden information and reversibility does not survive composition ([Lee et al. ~2005](https://www2.nict.go.jp/nano/results/abstract/17_217.html)); the paper leaves the fix open. A real CJoin design carries a 1-bit internal memory of which way its pair went, and the only cost is a few kT when that bit is reset to drive it forward ([Utsumi 2025](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.12390#page=1)). Inference for disp: each rewrite could leave a 1-bit receipt at its site, un-rewriting uses it up, and resetting it is where heat is paid.

Token-count ledger: primitives are classed as conservative or invertible, and for a specification whose token count balances, extra outputs are popped from a reservoir of stored tokens and would-be-destroyed tokens are pushed back instead of erased ([Patra and Fussell 1995](https://www.cs.utexas.edu/ftp/techreports/tr95-10.pdf#page=15)). This is 'copy draws fuel, un-copy refunds' for balanced computations only; unbalanced ones are merely 'marginally conservative'. On a lattice the serial stack would have to become a local gas of blank tokens (inference).

Noise as the driver, bias only where it pays: tokens random-walk, and arbitration and deadlock escape come free by backtracking ([Peper et al. 2013](https://www.cs.upc.edu/~jordicf/Research/gavina/BIB/files/BrownianCircuits_JETC2013.pdf#page=2); [Lee and Peper 2009](https://www2.nict.go.jp/nano/results/abstract/peper/peper090923.html)). Only biased CJoins produce environment entropy, with readout and reset carrying the rest ([Utsumi et al. 2022](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.10735#page=9)). Ratchets consume energy and go only where backtracking is never needed. This could replace the strand lattice's priority rules and demand machinery with diffusion plus a few ratchets.

Energy-time law: polynomial time needs a finite forward bias, and for backward branching m the threshold is γ+ = m γ− ([Okajima and Hukushima 2025](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.24728#page=1)). Dissipation per net step is kT ln(forward/backward) ([Bennett 1982](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/863.18/notes/computation/Bennett-1982.pdf#page=10)) and merges cost about kT times log of the predecessor count ([Bennett 1982](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/863.18/notes/computation/Bennett-1982.pdf#page=19)). So make every rule injective first, then pay a per-step bias sized by how branchy the state graph is.

A tiny reversible lattice: four rotation-symmetric, bit-conserving, locally reversible rules on an asynchronous 4-bit-per-cell CA run a universal reversible TM, and the whole CA is globally reversible ([Lee et al. 2002](https://www2.nict.go.jp/nano/results/abstract/14_48.html)). That sets the scale to aim for in the strand lattice's 2x2x2 block moves: make each block move a bijection on block states and accept it with symmetric Metropolis (inference).

Two meanings of 'reversible' to pick between: backward-deterministic, where every configuration has one predecessor (Morita), which breaks under concurrency unless something records arrival order; and stochastically reversible, where every move has a reverse move and bias sets the direction (Brownian), which composes with parallelism. disp's 'needs energy to reverse' matches the second.

Schedule-independent asynchrony: flip automata networks fire a node only when all its edge indicators point at it, and firing may flip any of them, so that ['the update schedule does not affect the update history of individual nodes'](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.05989#page=5) (Baburin, Cook et al. 2025, adjacent field). Interaction nets already have this property (strong confluence), which confirms disp needs no central sequencer.

field: Conservative logic and ballistic/adiabatic reversible computing: Fredkin-Toffoli conservative logic and the billiard-ball model, Margolus's block-partitioned and soft-sphere lattices, Bennett and Landauer on what erasure costs, Frank's asynchronous ballistic logic and conditional reversibility, plus Morita's rotary element. The focus is on what each model conserves, how it makes garbage, how it recycles or returns that garbage, and how it accounts for energy.

sources.title: Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process (Landauer 1961)
sources.quote: This dissipation serves the purpose of standardizing signals and making them independent of their exact logical history
sources.mechanism: A device is logically irreversible when its output does not determine its input. RESTORE TO ONE (erasure) maps 2 states to 1 and must dissipate about kT ln 2 per bit. What matters is a single well-defined initial state, not that the bits agree (p.5). A reversible 3-in/3-out embedding of AND needs 'a separate ZERO for every AND operation' supplied in the initial programming (p.4), and its extra outputs clutter memory. Landauer concludes the irreversibility is only moved: 'only at the expense of added comparable irreversibility during the loading of the program' (p.5). He also argues losses are 'essential for the standardization of signals' (p.4), i.e. noise immunity. He believed logical irreversibility essential to computing (p.4), which Bennett 1973 refuted.
sources.relevance: Fixes the unit of the heat ledger (kT ln 2 per bit whose value the system does not already know) and says that pre-blanked constants (blank agents) cost irreversibility where they are made. The further suggestions (fuel should stream in from the lattice edge; the substrate's drive also does Landauer's 'standardizing' job and should be booked apart from erasure heat) are design inferences, not claims of the paper.

sources.title: Logical Reversibility of Computation (Bennett 1973)
sources.quote: the history tape is not random - there exists a subtle mutual redundancy between it and the machine that produced it
sources.mechanism: Any deterministic Turing machine is simulated by a 3-tape reversible one built from quadruples (each a read/write or a shift, which makes every step one-to-one). Stage 1 runs forward and writes the index of each transition onto a history tape. Stage 2 copies the output onto a blank tape. Stage 3 runs the inverse quadruples, consuming the history and restoring the input. End state: (input, output, blank history): 'Even though no history remains. the computation is reversible and deterministic.' History grows one record per step; 'by performing a job in many stages rather than just three, the required amount of temporary storage can often be' reduced, which is the seed of later pebbling. Physical section (#PhysicalReversibility): 'Tape copying is a logically reversible operation', with RNA polymerase as the example; a dissipation e < kT per step buys a drift velocity of Ge/kT steps per second.
sources.relevance: Per-rewrite records run backward are Bennett's history tape. Compute, copy onto blanks, uncompute turns 'forget' (heat) into uncompute (time) and returns code and arguments intact. 'Mutual redundancy' says a record need not store what the rule already determines, matching the README's note that most of the ~2.3 used-up agents per event are implied by the rule. Note this is not a new proposal for the repo: the README already describes a `bennett` option (run, copy the answer, run back) for the trace machinery (evaluators/rust-ic-strands/README.md around line 1449); what is open is doing it inside the substrate (phys=1) lattice.

sources.title: Conservative Logic (Fredkin and Toffoli 1982)
sources.quote: all signal processing is ultimately reduced to conditional routing of signals
sources.mechanism: Two primitives: the unit wire (storage and transmission are the same process seen in different reference frames, p.4-5) and the Fredkin gate (u,x1,x2) -> (u, u?x1:x2, u?x2:x1), invertible and conservative (number of 1s preserved). No implicit fan-out; FAN-OUT is a gate with constant inputs. Signals are 'moved around ... but never created or destroyed' (p.6). A non-invertible f is realized 'using source and sink' (p.8): constants in, garbage out; e.g. AND is a Fredkin gate with x2=0, garbage a and (not a)b. Billiard-ball model: elastic collisions form the interaction gate, fixed mirrors route. Garbageless scheme (section 7): run the network, observe the result with a 'spy' gate fed 0 and 1, then run the inverse network. The argument register returns unchanged; an all-zero scratchpad returns clean ('spare room rather than tokens', p.21, via a proof by Margolus); a result register of capacity 2n, preloaded with n tokens, ends holding y and not-y. The circuit itself makes no garbage; the only possible 'dissipation' is the user discarding the m-bit argument, which is unrelated to gate count (p.21-22). Scratchpad size trades against time, from about exp(m) down to about m (7.2). Section 7.3: if f is both invertible and conservative, the result can be produced by rearranging the argument tokens in the same register, and 'any invertible, conservative function ... can be realized without garbage by means of the Fredkin gate' (p.24, proved by B. Silver). Closing such circuits into loops gives general-purpose conservative computers (Ressler 1981). Section 8: billiard-ball energy is proportional to the number of balls, so there is 'no necessary connection between the energy involved in a computation and its length or complexity'.
sources.relevance: Makes 'just moves things around' exact. (a) Each tree-calculus rule can be a bijection with explicit source and sink wires: K's dropped argument and triage's untaken arms plus the branch taken leave as garbage matter; duplicator outputs arrive as blanks. (b) Compute, copy onto blanks, mirror-uncompute reuses the circuit instead of copying the code. (c) Token count is an exactly checkable local invariant. (d) Silver's theorem applies only to functions that are BOTH invertible and conservative: (a,b) -> (a,a+b) in plain binary is invertible but not conservative (a=1,b=0 maps 1 one-bit to 2), so it needs dual-rail encoding (each bit stored with its complement, which makes any bijection weight-preserving) or a scratchpad before Silver's result applies.

sources.title: Physics-like Models of Computation (Margolus 1984)
sources.quote: the existence of an interesting local conservation law does not depend on the rule being reversible
sources.mechanism: A partitioning CA (the Margolus neighbourhood): the grid is split into 2x2 blocks, alternating between a solid and a dotted blocking each step, and each block is updated by a 4-in/4-out rule. In the billiard-ball CA (BBMCA) rule, a lone 1 moves to the opposite corner and two diagonal 1s become the other diagonal (a collision). The rule is bijective, conserves 1s and is universal; stable 2x2 squares of 1s straddling block boundaries act as mirrors. Unlike the BBM, collisions introduce a delay that must be accounted for when synchronizing signals. A 1-conserving rule need not be injective: it would 'forget all sorts of details' yet keep the counts. Footnote: for each block one can tell 'how many possible predecessors the result-block has', so the information lost per step is counted exactly (p.6). Unwanted intermediates are 'mostly erased' by 'copying the answer once you have it, and then running the computation backwards' (p.8). BBM computations can be pipelined.
sources.relevance: Strand-lattice moves already happen inside 2x2x2 blocks, and Margolus shows a whole dynamics can be one bijective block table, making reversibility a property of the table rather than of stored records. The footnote gives an exact per-block count of information lost, i.e. a local heat ledger. The idea of turning erasure into a conserved 'heat particle' that diffuses to the boundary (the README's open 'fuel and heat as fields' item) follows from the conservation-without-injectivity remark but is a design proposal, not something the paper builds.

sources.title: The Thermodynamics of Computation - a Review (Bennett 1982)
sources.quote: would cause the Brownian computer to spend most of its time bogged down in extraneous predecessors of states on the intended path
sources.mechanism: Compares ballistic (Fredkin-Toffoli) computers, which dissipate nothing but need perfect isolation and precision, with Brownian computers, which random-walk through a 'low-energy labyrinth' isomorphic to the computation under a weak drive. A drive of ε per step gives a forward/backward ratio e^(ε/kT); RNA polymerase example: '11 forward steps for each 10 backward steps' at about 0.1 kT per net step (p.10). Merging paths makes a Brownian computer bog down in extraneous predecessors 'unless an extra driving force of kT ln2 were applied (and dissipated) at each merge point' (p.2). Fig. 11B: a seven-stage reversible computation of a 1:1 function phi with no extra output, using irreversible algorithms for phi and phi^-1; the phi^-1 history 'serves in stage 7 to destroy itself and the remaining copy of the input' (p.21). Gate garbage is disposed of 'by feeding them into a mirror image of the reversible logic net' (p.22). Fuel: a tape of N zeros can do N kT ln 2 of work; a computable tape such as the digits of pi can too, via a reversible computer that maps it to zeros first; a typical random tape cannot be exploited by any simple apparatus. Of seven identical random tapes, six can be reversibly cancelled into blanks (p.31).
sources.relevance: (a) Every merge in a Brownian lattice's state graph costs an extra kT ln 2 of drive or the walk bogs down; a rule set that emits garbage instead of merging keeps the reachable states a chain. Caution: the README attributes the substrate's 10-12x slower way back to undo pieces needing to come back together in space (535,718 undo tries found them apart for add 1 1), not to merges, so this paper does not explain that measurement. (b) Fig. 11B is the general recipe for an injective function to leave no history; the README already has this as `bijection f g x` ('Bennett's second step'). For (a,b)->(a,a+b) specifically it is overkill, since in-place y := y + a is already reversible. (c) Identical copies cancel back into blanks while one original remains, so a duplicator's fuel is refundable.

sources.title: Parallel Quantum Computation (Margolus 1990)
sources.quote: add a single bit of update-count to each cell, we can run the system asynchronously while retaining a perfectly synchronous causality
sources.mechanism: Feynman's model is H = F + F-dagger with a single cursor moving along a chain of gates. With only neighbour interactions, parallelism forces 'asynchronous (no global time) computing schemes' (p.7). Scheme: a 1D pairing (partitioning) CA. Each cell carries the lowest bit of its update count; adjacent cells can never get more than one step apart, so a pair can be updated whenever both are at the same step, in any order. Starting from a synchronous configuration, every cell updated n times holds the state it would have after n synchronous steps ('hills and valleys of time'); backward steps are allowed. Quantum form: F = sum of local block-update terms on clock spins. A uniform rate needs [F, F-dagger] = 0, which holds iff blocks ready to go forward equal blocks ready to go back: true in 1D with periodic boundaries, false for the earlier 2D model. Feynman's serial cursor maps to a 'staircase' configuration with two active blocks (one forward, one back), which is NOT on the orbit of any synchronous parallel computation. In 2D, only one dimension of parallelism is achieved, by sweeping a 1D active region across the plane. 'Achieving full parallelism in more than one dimension remains an open problem' (p.1).
sources.relevance: The strand lattice's random block proposals are an asynchronous partitioned CA. Margolus's 1D result says one phase bit per cell, starting from a synchronous state, makes random local firing reproduce a synchronous block CA exactly, runnable backward with no central sequencing. Carrying this to 2x2x2 blocks in 3D is plausible but is not shown here (the earlier 2D 'guard bits' version is in a prior paper, not verified). The serial walker is a staircase configuration off the synchronous orbit, which is a precise way to say a single cursor is a different regime from block-parallel evaluation. The uniform-rate parallel unitary beyond 1D stays open; a driven Brownian lattice is the classical stand-in.

sources.title: Reversibility and Adiabatic Computation: Trading Time and Space for Energy (Li and Vitanyi 1997)
sources.quote: put a free pebble on node i or remove a pebble from node i, provided node i - 1 is pebbled at the time
sources.mechanism: Bennett's 1989 reversible simulation as a pebble game on a chain: a pebble (a checkpoint of S bits) may be placed on or removed from node i only if node i-1 is pebbled; win by pebbling the last node then clearing the rest. With n pebbles Bennett's strategy simulates 2^n - 1 steps (about 3^n moves), and among pebble-game simulations it is optimal in space: no such simulation reaches that many steps with n-1 pebbles. Saving kS space costs (2^(k+2) - 1)S irreversible bit erasures, so 'there can be an advantage in adding limited irreversibility' (p.4). Cost model: reversible steps free, each irreversibly supplied or erased bit costs one unit. Fundamental theorem (up to logarithmic terms, for a reversible computation that does not retain its program): E(x,y) = C(x|y) + C(y|x), counting 'the number of extra bits (apart from x) that must be irreversibly supplied at the beginning, plus the number of garbage bits' (p.15); 'the cost is less if we compact the garbage before we throw it away' (p.15).
sources.relevance: Gives a local, reversible way to thin a CHAIN of history: a checkpoint may be dropped or re-made only while its predecessor is present, so forgetting costs time, not heat. It also gives a theoretical floor C(x|y) + C(y|x) for the heat ledger and says to compress garbage before erasing. That floor is in Kolmogorov complexity, which is uncomputable, so it bounds the ledger but cannot be computed by it. The substrate's rewrites form a DAG, not a chain, so the pebble rule does not transfer directly.

sources.title: A Simple Universal Logic Element and Cellular Automata for Reversible Computing (Morita 2001)
sources.quote: there is only one incoming signal to each element, which interacts with rotating bar of the element
sources.mechanism: A reversible sequential machine has a one-to-one move function delta: Q x Sigma -> Q x Gamma. The rotary element (RE) has two states (bar horizontal or vertical) and four input and four output lines. A particle arriving parallel to the bar passes straight through. A particle arriving across the bar turns right and rotates the bar 90 degrees. The RE conserves particles ('a particle is neither annihilated nor newly created', p.3), and RE circuits forbid fan-out. Since one signal at a time interacts with the element, no clock is needed (p.12). Any reversible Turing machine can be built from REs alone. An RE also embeds in the 3^4-state reversible partitioned CA P3, whose 81 rules are given by 13 rule schemes.
sources.relevance: The minimal matter-mediator interaction: the element's state is matter, the particle is the mediator, each step is a bijection on (state, incoming direction), and two mediators never meet, so nothing needs synchronizing. Disp's mediator-value rules (apply, triage and the duplicator meeting leaf, stem and fork) have this shape. That suggests a criterion: each mediator x value rule should be injective on (value, mediator) -> (value', mediator(s)'), with garbage leaving as an extra mediator. Caution: an RE circuit simulating a Turing machine runs with one particle, which is a walker; parallelism needs many particles in flight.

sources.title: Universal Cellular Automata Based on the Collisions of Soft Spheres (Margolus 2002, arXiv 2008)
sources.quote: Two particles colliding at right angles turn into a single new particle of twice the mass for one step
sources.mechanism: Soft (compressible) balls take a finite time to bounce, which makes the model a lattice gas: every particle moves along its velocity, then each site interacts independently. Two diagonal particles meeting at right angles fuse into one double-mass particle for one step, then split; mirrors deflect. Mass and energy are conserved, and momentum too except at mirrors. 3D versions use cube face and body diagonals; in two of the three 3D schemes the slow fused particle carries a collision-plane bit, while in the body-plus-face-diagonal scheme it does not, and there mirrors can potentially be replaced by signals ('using only signals to deflect signals', p.6). Dual-rail signalling lets signals be reflected cleanly. In a regular array of Fredkin gates and upside-down Fredkin gates, constant streams of 1s 'are passed back and forth between adjacent Fredkin gates' (p.12) and need not be supplied from outside. 'The main difficulty here turns out to be reusing signal-routing resources' (p.2). Reversibility and energy conservation let such CAs 'accurately model thermodynamic limits on computation' (p.2).
sources.relevance: A lattice built only of particles, where even routing 'hardware' is made of reusable particle streams, parallels disp's code-as-matter steering mediators. The one-step fused particle is a model of a mediator meeting matter as a short-lived composite that then splits into outputs. Passing constant streams between neighbouring gates is a model for handing fuel blanks from un-copies to nearby copies instead of settling them through a lattice-wide ledger.

sources.title: Notes on Landauer's Principle, Reversible Computation, and Maxwell's Demon (Bennett 2003)
sources.quote: copying unknown data onto a blank (ie initially zero) register, and the reverse process, namely erasure of one of two copies of data known to be identical
sources.mechanism: Landauer's principle: logically irreversible operations (erasure, merging of computation paths) must raise the entropy of non-information-bearing degrees of freedom. Copy is y := y + x (needs y = 0); un-copy is y := y - x (needs y = x); each undoes the other, so both are logically reversible and in principle thermodynamically free (p.2). Erasing random data is thermodynamically reversible (an entropy transfer), but when 'the logically irreversible operation is applied to known data, the operation is thermodynamically irreversible' (p.1), because the environment's entropy rise is not offset. Merging of control flow is itself logical irreversibility (p.3). Any computation that keeps a copy of its input can be reprogrammed as a sequence of logically reversible steps (p.4). 'Transcription from DNA to RNA, after strand initiation, can be viewed as a logically reversible copying process', driven by removing pyrophosphate (p.4).
sources.relevance: Prices copy and delete. A duplicator writing onto blank agents, and its inverse merging two copies known equal back into blanks, are free in principle. Heat is owed only for erasing information the system cannot rebuild; resetting a state that is known (e.g. an eraser meeting what is known to be a leaf) can be done by a 1:1 mechanism at no cost, whereas a 2:1 merge applied to known data wastes work. This matches the README's substrate accounting, where heat is the erased leaves (194-807) plus the records only they led back through (2,300-6,600).

sources.title: Generalized Reversible Computing (Frank 2018)
sources.quote: only the subset of initial states that are assigned nonzero probability in a given statistical operating context must be transformed one-to-one into final states
sources.mechanism: A computation is an operation O together with an operating context, a probability distribution over initial states. It ejects no entropy iff O is one-to-one on the support of that context. This gives conditioned reversible operations: rSET(x|x=0), rCLR(x|x=1), rCOPY(x,y|y=v), rUnCOPY(x,y|y=x), and in general rF and rUnF with preconditions. 'A known state can be transformed to any specific new state reversibly' (p.25). rAND/rUnAND have simple adiabatic implementations (series/parallel CMOS transmission gates), much simpler than a full Toffoli gate, which would be overkill. Assertion 2 (stated as an assertion, not proved) is that truly fully adiabatic circuits correspond to conditioned reversible operations.
sources.relevance: Formalizes 'entropy relative to what the system knows'. A disp rule need only be one-to-one on the configurations that can actually occur where it fires (a duplicator only ever meets blank targets; an eraser meeting a leaf knows it is a leaf), which shrinks the table for a reversible core. Heat is owed only when an operation runs outside its precondition or two reachable states merge.

sources.title: Ballistic Asynchronous Reversible Computing in Superconducting Circuits (Frank, ISRDS'23 talk)
sources.quote: timing uncertainty per logic stage can now accumulate only linearly, not exponentially
sources.mechanism: Synchronous ballistic logic lets timing errors grow exponentially. BARC (ballistic asynchronous reversible computing) avoids direct interaction between moving entities: 'Require localized pulses to arrive asynchronously', at distinct non-overlapping times (p.5). Each device keeps a discrete stable internal state, and its behaviour is a reversible transition table on (state, input port, polarity). There is no power clock: 'The operation energy is carried by the pulse itself' and most of it leaves in the outgoing pulse (p.5). The simplest element, the 1-port reversible memory cell (RM), stores a flux quantum: 'If polarities are opposite, they are swapped'; if identical, the input fluxon reflects unchanged; the scattering is elastic and flux-conserving (p.6). Enumeration: 24 one-port two-state elements; of the two-port two-state flux-polarized functions, 96 conserve flux and 10 are nontrivial primitives, in 7 equivalence groups including the reversible shift register.
sources.relevance: Physical case for the matter/mediator picture: a clockless ballistic reversible system stays stable if every interaction is one moving thing against one stationary thing.
