For disp, mediators (apply, triage, duplicator) are the pulses and values are the stored state; restricting rules to mediator x matter and routing mediator x mediator meetings through matter would mirror this. The RM swap is the minimal exchange rule, close to the strand lattice's swap moves.

key_ideas: Garbage as matter, not as a numbered record: give each tree-calculus rule explicit source and sink wires so it is a bijection on its block. K's dropped argument and triage's untaken arms plus the branch taken leave on a sink wire as garbage matter; the duplicator's new agents arrive on a source wire as blanks. The conserved count of agents + blanks + garbage is an exact local invariant that could replace a record table keyed by global ids. (Fredkin-Toffoli 1982 p.6, p.8; Landauer 1961 p.4)

Compute, copy, mirror-uncompute per call: run, copy the answer onto blanks, run the mirror image. Argument and scratch come back clean and only the answer is new, so history never outlives a call and code is reused rather than copied ('The reversible program functions again in a catalytic manner', https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3520#page=6). The repo already has this as the `bennett` option for the trace machinery; the open step is doing it inside the substrate lattice. (Fredkin-Toffoli p.21; Bennett 1973; Bennett 1982 p.22)

History-free invertible functions: Silver's theorem gives garbage-free in-place token rearrangement only for functions that are BOTH invertible and conservative (Fredkin-Toffoli p.24); binary (a,b)->(a,a+b) is invertible but not conservative, so it needs dual-rail encoding or a scratchpad. The general route for any injective function is Bennett's seven-stage phi/phi^-1 scheme, where the inverse's history cancels the extra input and then itself (Bennett 1982 p.21), already present in the repo as `bijection f g x`.

Price copying and deleting by what is known: copying onto blanks and un-copying two equal copies are free in principle ('If they are to get rid of unwanted information at all, they must cancel it against equivalent information already present elsewhere', https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3520#page=6). Heat is owed for oblivious erasure ('when one of two mutually-correlated subsystems is obliviously erased', https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.00065#page=43) and for 2:1 operations applied to known data. The theoretical floor is E(x,y) = C(x|y) + C(y|x) up to log terms, uncomputable but a bound; compress garbage before erasing. (Bennett 2003 p.1-2; Li-Vitanyi p.15)

Conditional reversibility shrinks the rule table: a rule only has to be one-to-one on the configurations that can occur where it fires (a duplicator only meets blank targets; an eraser meeting a known leaf), and heat is charged only outside the precondition. The hardware analogue is the adiabatic 'no spark' rule: 'do not turn a switch (e.g., a FET) "on" when there is a non-negligible voltage difference between its source and drain terminals' (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.00448#page=3). (Frank 2018 p.1, p.25)

Reversible forgetting by pebbling on a chain: a checkpoint may be dropped or re-made only while its predecessor exists, trading time for heat; erasure buys space below Bennett's pebble bound at (2^(k+2) - 1)S bits to save kS. Disp's rewrites form a DAG, so this needs a DAG analogue. (Li-Vitanyi p.4, p.7)

One clock bit per cell turns random asynchronous pair updates into an exact copy of a synchronous 1D block CA, provided the run starts from a synchronous state; backward steps are allowed, and the quantum form is H = F + F-dagger. A uniform rate holds in 1D periodic systems but not in the 2D model, and full parallelism beyond 1D is open. Feynman's single cursor corresponds to a staircase configuration that is off every synchronous orbit. Extending this to 2x2x2 blocks is plausible but unshown. (Margolus 1990 p.1, p.7, p.9)

Heat and fuel as conserved particles: since conservation does not need injectivity, erasure could be a block rule that turns a bit into a heat particle drifting to the boundary, and counting each block's predecessors gives an exact local information-loss count (Margolus 1984 p.6; the heat-particle rule itself is a design proposal). Fuel can be recycled between neighbours as constant streams are passed between adjacent Fredkin gates (Margolus 2002 p.12). Toffoli argues a lattice gas 'does not indulge in wasteful "photocopying" and "shredding" practices', but that efficiency 'can only be achieved at the cost of using LG nodes that encompass a sufficiently large number n of sites' (https://arxiv.org/pdf/0709.1173#page=14), which is a caveat for purely local fuel recycling.

Interactions only between a mediator and matter: one moving pulse meets one stationary element, and the step is a bijection on (state, port). Nothing needs synchronizing, timing error grows only linearly, and the pulse carries its own energy. Examples: Morita's rotary element; Frank's RM cell, which swaps opposite polarities; and Osborn-Wustmann's shift register, where 'Its operation consists of the elastic swapping of flux between the stored and the moving bit' and which is 'powered by the input bits alone' (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.12999#page=1). Universality of an implementable fluxon element set is still listed as open in Frank's 2023 talk. Disp's apply/triage/duplicator meeting leaf/stem/fork already has this shape.

Keep the reachable states a chain: in a Brownian (driven random-walk) system every merge of computation paths makes the walk bog down in extraneous predecessors unless an extra kT ln 2 of drive is paid at each merge; emitting garbage instead keeps speed proportional to drive. This does not explain the substrate's measured 10-12x slower way back, which the README attributes to undo pieces having to come back together in space. (Bennett 1982 p.2, p.10)

History-free traversal as an extreme point: Lange-McKenzie-Tapp simulate a machine reversibly with no extra space, at exponential time, by traversing its configuration tree 'by alternating two permutations on half-edges' (swap and rotate) (https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0504088#page=8). The half-edges belong to the machine's configuration graph, not to the program's data structure, so the analogy to an interaction net's port map is loose. This is the zero-history, exponential-time, sequential corner of the space-time-heat trade-off.

field: Reversible and linear combinatory logic and interaction systems (Abramsky's reversible combinators from the geometry of interaction, Di Pierro-Hankin-Wiklicky reversible CL, interaction combinators and their symmetric and reversible variants, token machines, linear machines, information effects)

sources.title: A Structural Approach to Reversible Computation (Abramsky, 2005; arXiv 2011)
sources.quote: each variable which occurs does so exactly once in r and exactly once in s
sources.mechanism: Machine: a pattern-matching automaton (Q, q_in, q_out, R) with rules (q, r) -> (s, q'). A configuration is (state, ground term); the pattern must match the WHOLE term, but with left-linear patterns a step costs constant time (p.5). Orthogonal = non-ambiguous (no two same-state left sides unify) plus left-linear; biorthogonal = A and A^op (sides swapped) both orthogonal (p.6). So steps are deterministic forward and backward, A^op runs exactly the time reversal, and every variable occurs once on each side (no duplication or discarding). Signature: eps, l, r, p(_,_); p.22 shows one constant plus one binary constructor ('the pure theory of binary trees') suffice. Combinators as two-way rules: I l(x)<->r(x) (p.13); K l(x)<->r(r(x)), second argument 'does not get accessed' (p.14); B and C three rules each (p.15); D l(p(eps,x))<->r(x); delta l(p(p(x,y),z))<->r(p(x,p(y,z))) (p.17); F two rules; W (duplication, W.a.!b = a.!b.!b) r(r(x))<->l(r(r(x))), l(l(p(x,y)))<->r(l(p(l(x),y))), l(r(l(p(x,y))))<->r(l(p(r(x),y))), using the copy-tag field to split !b's address space (p.18). Replication !f = {(p(t,u),p(t,v))}; linear application LApp(f,g) = f_rr U f_rl;g;(f_ll;g)*;f_lr; on automata it is the disjoint union of state sets (p.20), so the compiled automaton is linear in the term size (p.23). Theorem 6.1: biorthogonal automata form an affine combinatory algebra; standard (S,K) application is derived as a.!b with S from B,C,I,W (pp.9-10). Termination is Sigma^0_1-complete (Thm 8.1). Readback: a boolean needs one run on r(r(eps)) (l(u) = true/K); numerals need a sequence of runs, a meta-computation that is 'prima facie irreversible' (p.24). Section 7 (pp.24-25): adding constants with a conditional and delta-rules keeps orthogonality but loses biorthogonality (the additives break partial injectivity).
sources.relevance: (a) The rule form 'tree pattern <-> tree pattern, each variable once per side' is the shape of iso.rs's Re (evaluators/rust-ic-strands/crate/src/iso.rs), and Abramsky gets universality from such rules plus feedback wiring and replication, with no Dup instruction: copying is a tag on the token. (b) A tree-calculus program could compile to a fixed circuit walked by binary-tree tokens. (c) K's unused argument is never visited rather than erased.

sources.title: Reversible Combinatory Logic (Di Pierro, Hankin, Wiklicky, MSCS 2006)
sources.quote: An important property of rCL is that reductions always increase the length of the history term
sources.mechanism: Basis B, C, W, K. Terms <M | H>; history steps T K^m_n, W^m_n, B^m_n, C^m_n and barred inverses, where n is the position and m = len(X) (p.5). Forward rules record K's dropped Y (<KXY|> -> <X|Y K^{len X}_0>); W, B, C record only position and length (p.6). Each forward rule has a symmetric backward rule (e.g. <XYY|> -> <WXY|W-bar>, which needs two equal subterms), so the reduction relation is nondeterministic (Example 4: <CBB|...> -> <WCB|...> via backward W, p.9). The converse relation is a deterministic partial function (Prop. 1). Histories form a group H:H-bar = eps, so loops cancel (p.5, p.8). Structural rule 2 shifts positions by len(Y). The intro (p.3) models computations as elements of the groupoid of the reduction relation, each reversible reduction being a permutation (unitary).
sources.relevance: Shows what a step's record must hold: only K's dropped argument plus a position; B, C, W are injective given the position. Keeps a group law (a step meeting its inverse record cancels), but the history is one global list, which is the thing to avoid. Warning: un-copying (backward W) needs an equality test of unbounded size unless a link between the copies is kept.

sources.title: Interaction Combinators (Lafont, Information and Computation 1997; third-party mirror)
sources.quote: we interpret the nets of combinators as reversible 2-stack machines
sources.mechanism: Agents gamma, delta (2 auxiliary ports) and epsilon (0). Six rules: annihilations gamma-gamma (ports exchanged), delta-delta (straight), eps-eps; commutations gamma-delta, gamma-eps, delta-eps. Strong confluence; universal for interaction systems under translations that preserve complexity and degree of parallelism. Delta cannot duplicate delta, so general nets are copied as a delta-free code plus a decoder (§2.6). §3.1 execution: for a net that reduces to a wiring, the wiring can be computed 'without reducing, just by travelling' with a pair of stacks (u, v) over {p, q}: enter an auxiliary port -> push, exit principal; enter principal -> pop, exit the matching auxiliary port (delta) or the other one (gamma). Prop. 5: execution is deterministic, reversible (the gamma-stack is mirrored p<->q on the way back), monotone, and invariant under reduction. §3.4 (p.28): the backward execution does not follow the same rules as the forward one; this would not happen if gamma-gamma were the same as delta-delta (that modified system has the same expressive power); directed combinators (6 symbols, 9 rules) separate forward and backward executions, and a net reducing in n steps has a covering reducing in 2n steps. §1.4 encodes cellular automata.
sources.relevance: One net, two dynamics that provably agree: parallel irreversible rewriting and a reversible, history-free stack walk. The 2-stack token is a concrete candidate for a particle moving along strands.

sources.title: Observational Equivalence and Full Abstraction in the Symmetric Interaction Combinators (Mazza, LMCS 2009)
sources.quote: an observable path carries the same information as its reversal
sources.mechanism: Symbols delta, zeta (binary) and epsilon (nullary). Same-symbol cells annihilate (Fig. 3; the right side is empty for epsilon), different symbols commute. No critical pairs, so strongly confluent (Prop. 1.8). 'An equally expressive variant of Lafont's interaction combinators'; Lafont's translation theorem (Thm 1.20) carries over. Duplication lemma 1.11: a tree of alpha cells duplicates only cut-free nets with no alpha cells; general nets are copied via 'the Lafont code' (Fig. 5) and a universal decoder. Semantics: edifices (subsets of Cantor space built from observable axioms in reducts), with full abstraction for two observational equivalences analogous to head-normal-form and normal-form equivalence in lambda-calculus. Addresses are unordered pairs because a path carries the same information as its reversal (GoI operators are Hermitian, p.25).
sources.relevance: Supports choosing uncrossed annihilations so the reverse token walk uses the same rules as the forward walk (the time-symmetric lattice law); the explicit statement of that consequence is Lafont §3.4, not Mazza. Edifices give a semantic test of when two nets are equal. The Lafont code confirms that layer-wise copying needs a delta-free code.

sources.title: Upward confluence in the interaction calculus (Salikhmetov, 2018)
sources.quote: a reversible interaction system is such that two active pairs never reduce to overlapping nets and any net can be the result of at most one active pair
sources.mechanism: Strong upward confluence is a backward one-step diamond. Two active pairs clash if their reducts (multisets of equations) are equal and non-empty (Def. 3); eps = eps clashes with nothing. A rule is disconnected if its reduct splits into two non-empty parts sharing no names (Def. 4): gamma-gamma and delta-delta annihilations are disconnected, gamma-delta duplication is connected. Def. 5 + Props. 4-6: strongly upward confluent iff no two active pairs clash and every rule is connected. Prop. 7: no two different rules share a positive arity, so a complete non-trivial reversible system needs pairwise-distinct agent arities. The linear-lambda system is upward confluent though not reversible. Open: a universal reversible interaction system ('the reversible combinators').
sources.relevance: A checkable test for a disp rule table: every rule connected and no clashing active pairs. Binary annihilations (pair meets unpair, apply meets lambda) fail it and would need a residue agent bridging their outputs. Payoff: backward steps commute like forward ones, so un-running is as parallel as running. The distinct-arity constraint limits how agent kinds can share arities.

sources.title: Reversible, irreversible and optimal lambda-machines (Danos, Regnier, TCS 1999)
sources.quote: which is but the word, will sometimes grow and sometimes shrink. It needs no external garbage-collection
sources.mechanism: IAM on linear-logic proof nets. The token is a pair of stacks (B, S), a box stack and a balancing stack; each is a sequence of multiplicative constants P, Q and exponential signatures (binary trees with leaves P', Q' and a hole). Actions are partial continuous one-to-one maps forming an inverse monoid, presented as clauses with non-unifiable heads (maps) and non-unifiable bodies (one-to-one); inversion swaps head and body, so the automaton is bi-deterministic and reversible. It implements linear head reduction. The KAM keeps closures; in its jump step the discarded environment cannot be freed, so it is inflationary and needs external garbage collection (same for the PAM). Using Asperti-Laneve call/return symmetry, the JAM adds setjump/longjump shortcuts to the IAM; under D = !D -o D it is isomorphic to the KAM, under the other embedding it is the PAM. Section 1 sketches memoizing redex-family paths as a Levy-optimal machine, leaving efficiency open.
sources.relevance: Explains why an IAM-like machine (the removed iso Machine, commit 2a327365) was reversible (only the token's word changes) and slow (it re-walks returns), and names the shortcut that trades reversibility for speed: jumping on return, which stores context the reversible machine refuses to keep.

sources.title: The Geometry of Synchronization (Long Version) (Dal Lago, Faggian, Hasuo, Yoshimizu, 2014)
sources.quote: Tokens cross a sync link l only when each in-edge of l is saturated
sources.mechanism: SMLL = multiplicative linear logic plus sync links. SIAM state T maps each token's starting position to its current position. Tokens move by the usual IAM rules; at a sync link they cross only when every in-edge is saturated. A one-link starts a token; that is the only transition changing T's domain. A switching-path correctness criterion (no switching cycles, boxes correct) guarantees deadlock freedom in both normalization and the machine. QSMLL labels sync nodes with unitaries and models a quantum lambda-calculus (entanglement via synchronization). The intro (p.1) notes that multiple plain IAM calls 'can proceed in parallel, without any need for synchronization'.
sources.relevance: Gives a local rule for joining parallel tokens (S's x z (y z) run by two tokens meeting at a sync node) and a static no-deadlock condition, which depends on a proof-net criterion that untyped nets lack. Confirms that many independent queries over one shared circuit need no synchronization.

sources.title: The Dynamic Geometry of Interaction Machine: A Call-by-need Graph Rewriter (Muroya, Ghica, 2017)
sources.quote: because they handle duplicated computation by repeating the same moves of a token on the fixed graph
sources.mechanism: A graph plus one token. The token uses the GoI to find redexes and can trigger local rewrites. Two extreme interleavings: 'passes-only' never rewrites (an ordinary token machine, call-by-name, re-evaluates u each time); 'rewrites-first' rewrites every sub-graph the token visits into its value, which corresponds to call-by-need or call-by-value depending on the token's route, and copies sub-graphs (space grows). Time efficiency in Accattoli's taxonomy is shown via a weak simulation of Danvy-Zerny's storeless call-by-need machine.
sources.relevance: One machine that both re-walks (reuses the circuit, pays time) and rewrites (copies, pays space). In disp the choice could be made per redex by an energy budget, though in the paper it is a fixed strategy. Caveat: a single walker.

sources.title: PELCR: Parallel Environment for Optimal Lambda-Calculus Reduction (Pedicini, Quaglia, 2004/2007)
sources.quote: The one and only reduction rule is the composition of two edges in the graph
sources.mechanism: Virtual reduction (Danos-Regnier 1993) computes Girard's execution formula by local rewriting on graphs whose edge weights live in the dynamic algebra. When two edges are composable (non-null product) a new edge y*x is added, and the originals are kept but marked with the rest of the composition ([y]x, [x]y), the 'bar', introduced to preserve the execution formula. VR produces bars of bars; directed VR (Danos-Pedicini-Regnier 1997) avoids them. PELCR runs DVR with the 'half combustion' strategy in C over MPI, with message aggregation and a fair load-distribution policy, reaching up to 70-80% of ideal speedup. Levy-optimal (no duplication of redex-family work).
sources.relevance: The local, parallel, walker-free counterpart of token semantics: paths are pre-composed by neighbouring edges instead of walked, and the bar residues are needed for correctness, i.e. history as part of the state.

sources.title: Lively Linear Lisp -- 'Look Ma, No Garbage!' (Baker, SIGPLAN Notices 1992; Wayback copy)
sources.quote: We can copy, but only by destroying the original list and creating two new lists
sources.mechanism: Register machine with a free-list register fr and a stack sp. Cons cells are moved only by exchanges r1<->r2, r1<->CAR(r2), r1<->CDR(r2). Atoms are handled differently: there are also assignments r1:='foo and r1:=r2 restricted to atoms, plus NULL, ATOM and EQ tests. CONS(r1,r2) = {r1<->CAR(fr); r2<->fr; fr<->CDR(r2)}; PUSH/POP are built from it. Prop. 1: every cons cell's reference count is always exactly 1 (exchanges preserve it); Prop. 2: no garbage is created. FREE ('Essentially the K combinator') returns a list's cells to fr and sets atoms to NIL; COPY ('Essentially the S combinator') builds a second list drawing cells from fr; EQUAL is recursive; a Lisp interpreter runs on top.
sources.relevance: A worked 'just move things around' core: if empty lattice sites act as the free list, building a node swaps a vacuum cell in, copying draws vacuum (fuel), and freeing refunds it, with the cell count conserved. It is linear and garbage-free, but not reversible: atom assignment and FREE's r1:='NIL overwrite information, so a reversible version needs atoms handled by swaps too. Baker's NREVERSAL paper adds that garbage collection can be a reversed (sub)computation.

sources.title: Information Effects (James, Sabry, POPL 2012; Wayback copy)
sources.quote: an explicit erase operation that can be used to discard values and an explicit create operation which can be used to introduce and duplicate
sources.mechanism: Pi: types 0, 1, +, x; programs are the type isomorphisms of a commutative semiring, closed under sequence, sum, product and inverse (adjoint). Pi^o adds isorecursive types (fold/unfold) and trace c : b2 <-> b3 for c : b1+b2 <-> b1+b3; it can loop, so its bijections are partial, and it hosts the translation of a Turing-complete first-order language with loops. A function is information-preserving iff its output entropy equals its input entropy (Def. 2.4); fanout(x)=(x,x) is information-preserving and its logical inverse fanin is partial, defined only on equal pairs (p.3). An arrow layer adds create and erase. An irreversible a -> b is translated to a bijection (h, a) <-> (g, b), heap h supplying constants and garbage g absorbing outputs (p.6). In Pi^o, constants can be created inside traces, so that translation needs no input heap, only garbage (pp.6, 10).
sources.relevance: Bookkeeping for disp rules: what a rule takes from a heap (fuel) and what it sends to garbage (heat). Copying (fanout) preserves information, so it should cost a blank but no heat; un-copy (fanin) is partial and needs equal halves or a link to the original. Trace is the typed loop operator for iteration.

sources.title: Compositional Reversible Computation (Carette, Heunen, Kaarsgaard, Sabry, 2024)
sources.quote: a fundamental limitation of this approach is that it fails to be compositional
sources.mechanism: Survey. A global history <H|A1> -> <H,A1|B> disambiguates reductions but fails to compose when one subterm must step forward and another backward (p.3); following CCSK the authors conclude that reversibility should be a basic building block rather than an extension of an irreversible system. Bennett's compute-copy-uncompute manages history without erasing it (p.4). Lecerf: a reversible machine is backward-deterministic at every step, which makes reversibility local and compositional (p.5). PInj (partial injections) is 'in a sense' the universal model of partial reversible computation (p.6); Pi arises from FinBij. Dagger Frobenius monads and arrows add effects (p.9). LR construction: morphisms A -> B are A+H -> B x G up to heap/garbage behaviour; fundamental theorem: every function is a coproduct injection into A+H, then a bijection, then a product projection from B x G (p.10). Quantum analogue: Stinespring dilation (p.12).
sources.relevance: The theory behind: (1) global history logs do not compose, so either reversible primitives or per-site records are needed; (2) the fuel/heat split is the heap/garbage factorization; (3) a quantum lattice fits 'prepare ancillas, apply a unitary, discard' (Stinespring).

key_ideas: The removed iso Machine (commit 2a327365) was sequential for a structural reason. It parked the rest of the tree inside the program, so a second reader needed its own copy of the code. In a GoI token machine (geometry of interaction: a token walks a fixed graph) only the token's word changes, and it 'will sometimes grow and sometimes shrink' with no garbage collection ([Danos-Regnier](https://www.pure.ed.ac.uk/ws/files/16874549/Reversible_irreversible_and_optimal_machines.pdf#page=4)). So many tokens can share one circuit, and independent queries 'can proceed in parallel, without any need for synchronization' ([Dal Lago et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1405.3427#page=1)).

Two dynamics on one net. Rewriting is parallel but irreversible. Walking with two stacks is deterministic, reversible and invariant under reduction, and for a net that reduces to a wiring it computes that wiring 'without reducing' ([Lafont §3](https://dcreager.net/pdf/Lafont1997.pdf#page=23)). The reversibility is in the walking: Abramsky's model is reversible 'not in the simplistic sense that application between combinators is itself reversible' ([Ciaffaglione et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.06759#page=4)).

Copy as a tag, not a copy ([Abramsky](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=18)). Replication !f leaves a copy-tag field on the token, and W splits that tag space with l/r. S's 'z used twice' then needs one circuit for z with two tag ranges. The cost moves from matter (copies) to token length and repeated walks.

Reuse or copy, chosen per redex ([Muroya-Ghica](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.10027#page=1)). The same redex can be re-walked (reuses the graph, pays time) or rewritten and copied (fast, pays space). The paper fixes the choice as a strategy; picking it by local energy is a disp proposal.

Salikhmetov's test as a rule-table check ([Salikhmetov](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.07275#page=4)): every rule connected, and no two active pairs with the same non-empty reduct. Binary annihilations (gamma-gamma, delta-delta, and pair/unpair-shaped rules) fail it; eraser-eraser does not. A residue agent bridging the outputs is one proposed fix. The reward is that backward steps commute like forward ones.

History as a residue the semantics needs, not a log. Virtual reduction keeps 'bars' (the leftover of each composition) on the old edges, and only they preserve the execution formula ([PELCR](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0407055#page=4)). Reversible CL shows the minimal record is K's dropped argument plus a position, and that records form a group ([rCL](https://www.doc.ic.ac.uk/~herbert/papers/mscs06.pdf#page=5)). A global history list 'fails to be compositional' ([Carette et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.20842#page=3)). Their remedy is reversible primitives; per-site records are the disp variant.

A vacuum reservoir for cells ([Baker, Linear Lisp](https://web.archive.org/web/20191008085057/http://home.pipeline.com/~hbaker1/LinearLisp.html)). Cons cells move only by exchanges, CONS is three swaps with the free list, COPY draws cells and FREE returns them, so the cell count is conserved and no garbage arises. Baker's machine still overwrites atoms, so it is linear but not reversible; a disp version would also need atoms moved by swaps. Garbage collection can be 'a reversed (sub)computation' ([Baker, NREVERSAL](https://web.archive.org/web/20191008050816/http://home.pipeline.com/~hbaker1/ReverseGC.html)).

Track for each rule what it takes in and what it leaves behind. Every function factors as a heap injection, then a bijection, then a garbage projection ([James-Sabry](https://web.archive.org/web/20161007070937id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/information-effects.pdf#page=1), [LR theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.20842#page=10)). fanout preserves information and its inverse fanin is partial, defined only on equal pairs ([James-Sabry](https://web.archive.org/web/20161007070937id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/information-effects.pdf#page=3)), so copying should cost fuel but no heat. The information an erasure loses is measured against the input distribution (the password checker's '1.2 bits', [Carette-James-Sabry](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1811.03678#page=29)).

Uncrossed annihilations would make the reverse walk time-symmetric. Lafont notes that his backward execution needs the mirrored gamma-stack, and that this 'would not happen' if gamma-gamma were the same as delta-delta ([Lafont §3.4](https://dcreager.net/pdf/Lafont1997.pdf#page=28)). That uncrossed system is Mazza's symmetric combinators, equally expressive, where a path carries the same information as its reversal ([Mazza](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.0380#page=25)).

Join parallel tokens at sync nodes that fire only when every input edge is occupied ([SIAM](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1405.3427#page=14)). These are local barriers; nodes labelled with unitaries carry the idea to a quantum substrate. The no-deadlock guarantee rests on a proof-net correctness criterion.

Make triage routing, not erasure. Abramsky's K never accesses its second argument ([page 14](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=14)), and he shows that constants plus a conditional lose biorthogonality, i.e. reversibility ([page 24](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=24)). A pure selector encoding of leaf/stem/fork would leave unchosen arms unvisited. A related route is symmetric pattern matching, whose clauses are non-overlapping and exhaustive on both sides ([Sabry-Valiron-Vizzotto](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1804.00952#page=4)).

Tokens can be disp values. Abramsky's token terms need only 'the pure theory of binary trees' ([page 22](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=22)), so the moving token and the data can share the same leaf/fork structure.

field: Reversible functional and isomorphism languages: Pi and information effects, Theseus, RFun/CoreFun, Janus, reversible primitive permutations (RPP), partial isomorphisms and join inverse categories, symmetric pattern matching, duplication with a partial inverse (dup/merge), garbage as an effect, fractional/negative types

sources.title: Information Effects (James, Sabry, 2012)
sources.quote: information is treated as a linear resource that can neither be duplicated nor erased
sources.mechanism:
Pi (Π): value types 0, 1, b+b, b×b. Programs are type isomorphisms built from primitive pairs swap+, assocl+/assocr+, unite/uniti (1×b↔b), swap×, assocl×/assocr×, distrib/factor ((b1+b2)×b3 ↔ b1×b3 + b2×b3), closed under id, sym c (the adjoint, which is the inverse), c1 # c2, c1 + c2 and c1 × c2. These isomorphisms are sound and complete for isomorphisms of finite types ([p.3](https://web.archive.org/web/20161007070937id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/information-effects.pdf#page=3)); Toffoli is expressible, so Π is universal for reversible combinational circuits (p.4).

Pi° (Π°) adds recursive types μx.b with fold/unfold and trace (c : b1+b2 ↔ b1+b3 gives trace c : b2 ↔ b3), giving partial isomorphisms and non-termination.

Effects live in an arrow metalanguage with create_b : 1 ⇝ b and erase : b ⇝ 1; fstA, leftA, join (forget which side of a sum) and clone are derived (p.7). An irreversible first-order language is compiled to bijections (h, a) ↔ (g, b), h a heap of constants, g garbage.

Asymmetry: create always makes a known constant, erase destroys information known only at run time ([p.6](https://web.archive.org/web/20161007070937id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/information-effects.pdf#page=6)); since Π° can express creation and erasure of constants, the heap is eliminated in favour of traceA and only garbage remains. fanout is information-preserving and it is possible to define a partial function fanin that is its logical inverse ([p.3](https://web.archive.org/web/20161007070937id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/information-effects.pdf#page=3)).
sources.relevance: The grammar of lossless moves. Tree-calculus values are μx. 1 + x + x×x, and a case on leaf/stem/fork is a distrib that moves the tag into the context, so shape-preserving steps can be written as Π isos plus a choice. The create/erase asymmetry is the accounting rule: erasing a known constant is the inverse of a constant-creating Π° program (partial: it diverges on any other value), so only run-time-unique information must leave as garbage.

sources.title: Isomorphic Interpreters from Logically Reversible Abstract Machines (James, Sabry, 2012)
sources.quote: must not drop or duplicate pattern variables and must be logically reversible
sources.mechanism:
Turns a small-step machine into a Π° program. Admission criteria, summarizing Abramsky's bi-orthogonal automata (p.8): (1) states are algebraic data / tuples; (2) start and stop states are distinguishable (several of each allowed); (3) each valid state matches a unique pattern on the left-hand and right-hand side of the step relation; (4) each step is computable in Π°, drops and duplicates no pattern variable, and is logically reversible.

Compilation (p.9): unfold inputs until left-hand cases are distinguished, unfold outputs likewise, shuffle matching terms (with mediating computations), then slide the sections to expose start/stop states and close the loop with trace.

Adder: ⟨n+1, p, m⟩ ↦ ⟨n, p+1, m+1⟩ from ⟨n, p, 0⟩ to ⟨0, n+p, n⟩ ([p.9](https://web.archive.org/web/20170118155739id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/iso-int.pdf#page=9)); the accumulator ends equal to n. Run backward from ⟨0,2,3⟩ it reaches ⟨2,0,1⟩ and gets stuck; the paper lists three remedies: GADTs, divergence, or declaring the stuck states valid stop states. Tree traversal uses zipper contexts □ | Lft c t | Rgt t c (p.11); the paper ends with a meta-circular interpreter for Π°. One machine state moves at a time.
sources.relevance: The literature form of a single-token reversible walker. The four criteria are a mechanical bijectivity test for a rule table, and the adder's accumulator shows a loop keeping its history inside its own output. It gives no parallelism beyond one state.

sources.title: Theseus: A High Level Language for Reversible Computing (James, Sabry, 2014)
sources.quote: Labels act as goto statements from one side to the other
sources.mechanism:
Functions are sets of clauses pattern ↔ pattern with two rules ([p.5](https://web.archive.org/web/20170118093456id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/theseus.pdf#page=5)): left patterns form a complete non-overlapping covering of the input type and right patterns of the return type; each variable appears once on a side and exactly once on the other, with the same type. The inverse swaps the sides. Parametrized maps take maps as arguments that must be instantiated at compile time (macro-like; inlined before compiling to Π°).

Iteration labels: occurrences of a label on the LHS must be a non-overlapping coverage of the label type (likewise RHS); meeting a label on the RHS jumps to the matching LHS clause. add (x, y) = (x+y, x) ([p.10](https://web.archive.org/web/20170118093456id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/theseus.pdf#page=10)): x, y ↔ iter (y, 0, x); iter (a, b, 0) ↔ a, b; iter (a, b, Succ n) ↔ iter (add1 a, add1 b, n). b counts up as n counts x down, so b ends as a copy of x. trace is definable with labels (p.10). Theseus compiles to Π°; evaluation is sequential.
sources.relevance: Gives a local, checkable condition for a set of pair-to-pair lattice rules to be a bijection: on each side the patterns must tile the type without overlap and variables are used once. Labels model intermediate agents that carry loop state; add is the textbook history-free (a, b) → (a+b, a).

sources.title: Fractional Types: Expressive and Safe Space Management for Ancilla Bits (Chen, Choudhury, Carette, Sabry, 2020)
sources.quote: allocation of a new boolean value initialized to false also creates a value 1/false
sources.mechanism:
Extends Π with a type 1/v indexed by one value and η_v : 1 ↔ τ × 1/v, ε_v : τ × 1/v ↔ 1. η makes v with a GC process 1/v that can reclaim only v; ε annihilates them. Π/D checks at run time that the value given to ε is the expected one (p.7); a later section removes the check by lifting to pointed/singleton types and extracting programs from safety proofs.

The net flow of money between the computation and the global entity is zero is the only invariant ([p.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.07020#page=3)), so the borrower need not repay. A process collecting a pair decomposes into one per component, 1/(a,b) ↔ 1/a × 1/b ([p.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.07020#page=8)). Example id' (p.7): allocate an ancilla, CNOT it with the input so the ancilla is redirected to the output, then GC the original input bit, which by then holds the default value. A footnote reads η/ε as creation and annihilation of entangled particle/antiparticle pairs ([p.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.07020#page=5)).
sources.relevance: A local mechanism for 'copying draws fuel, un-copy refunds': fuel is blank matter borrowed with a debt 1/v; debts split per layer and vanish on meeting an equal value; a mismatch (in Π/D an exception) is where heat must be paid.

sources.title: Reversible Computation and Reversible Programming Languages (Yokoyama, 2010; the Janus language)
sources.quote: The variable x on the left-hand side of an assignment must not appear in the expression e on the right-hand side
sources.mechanism:
Janus: imperative, every statement locally invertible.
- Updates x += e, x -= e, x ^= e with x not in e.
- if e1 then s1 else s2 fi e2: e2 is an exit assertion true exactly when the then-branch ran; in the backward direction an assertion acts as a test and a test as an assertion ([p.5](https://people.cs.rutgers.edu/~uli/cs516/spring2020/readings/ReversibleComputing-TheoreticalCompSci2010.pdf#page=5)).
- from e1 do s1 loop s2 until e2: e1 is an entry assertion true only initially, e2 the exit test.
- push/pop with zero-clearing; local x = e … delocal x = e frees only at a known value.
- call/uncall; an uncall effectively reverses the direction of execution for the procedure body ([p.8](https://people.cs.rutgers.edu/~uli/cs516/spring2020/readings/ReversibleComputing-TheoreticalCompSci2010.pdf#page=8)).
There are no global variables; parameters are passed by reference and variables live in a store, executed sequentially. With fixed-size integers Janus is not universal; with unbounded stacks it is r-Turing complete (p.9). A reversible self-interpreter is reported in a cited earlier paper. (a, b) → (a, a+b) is the single statement b += a.
sources.relevance: Two rules to adopt: (1) controlled update, where a value used only inside e is read, not consumed, and passes through unchanged, so the step needs no history; (2) every join of control flow carries an exit assertion that distinguishes the branches, so a dispatch whose arms leave distinguishable results needs no record of which arm ran.

sources.title: Join Inverse Categories and Reversible Recursion (Kaarsgaard, Axelsen, Glück, JLAMP 2017), with RFun Revisited (Kaarsgaard, Thomsen), both reprinted in Kaarsgaard's 2018 thesis
sources.quote: the duplication of a value in one direction requires an equality check in the other direction, and vice versa
sources.mechanism:
Describes RFun (Yokoyama, Axelsen, Glück): untyped, first-order, linear variables, patterns need not be exhaustive. Duplication/equality operator: ⌊⟨x⟩⌋ = ⟨x, x⟩; ⌊⟨x, y⟩⌋ = ⟨x⟩ if x = y, else ⟨x, y⟩ unchanged; it is self-inverse (p.88). The only control structure is case with the symmetric first-match policy: once a branch matches, its result must not match patterns that could have been produced by a previous branch. Recursion uses a call stack; the inverse of a recursive function calls its inverse. plus ⟨x, y⟩ = ⟨x, x+y⟩ (p.89): case y of Z → ⌊⟨x⟩⌋ | S u → let ⟨x', u'⟩ = plus ⟨x, u⟩ in ⟨x', S u'⟩; backward, the equality check is the base-case test.

Semantics: inverse categories with joins of inverse-compatible maps: f ≍ g iff f and g are restriction compatible (agree where both are defined) and so are f† and g† ([p.92](https://di.ku.dk/english/research/phd/phd-theses/2018/Robin_Kaarsgaard_Thesis.pdf#page=92)); this yields reversible fixed points and a uniform †-trace.

RFun Revisited ([p.182](https://di.ku.dk/english/research/phd/phd-theses/2018/Robin_Kaarsgaard_Thesis.pdf#page=182)): relevant typing (each dynamic variable used at least once, enabling implicit duplication of first-order data) and ancillary arguments t1 → t2 (static, returned implicitly), e.g. plus :: Nat → Nat ↔ Nat. It drops the duplication/equality operator in favour of an Eq type class (p.183), and makes the first-match check static where leaf types or ancillae are orthogonal.
sources.relevance: A total, self-inverse dup/merge: merging two trees layer by layer and unzipping at the first unequal layer is total, so an un-copy proposal is always a bijective move. The first-match policy gives a dispatch a two-way reading. Partial rule tables glue when inverse-compatible; disjoint domains and disjoint ranges is the simplest sufficient case (overlap is allowed where both directions agree).

sources.title: A class of Recursive Permutations which is Primitive Recursive complete (Paolini, Piccolo, Roversi, 2020; RPP)
sources.quote: The argument x which drives the iteration unfolding cannot be among the arguments of the iterated function f
sources.mechanism: Functions Z^k → Z^k. Five base functions (identity, sign-change, successor, predecessor, swap), sequential and parallel composition, finite iteration It[f] (applies f |x| times to the first k arguments; x is last and passes through) and selection If[f, g, h] (runs f, g or h on the first k arguments by x > 0, x = 0, x < 0; x passes through) (p.8). The inverse is given syntactically: sum (m, n) ↦ (m+n, n) iterates successor n times, its inverse iterates predecessor ([p.5](https://iris.unito.it/retrieve/e27ce42f-52ce-2581-e053-d805fe0acbaa/20-03-23-main-caricato-su-IRIS.pdf#page=5)). Ancillae are initialized to zero and cannot be forgotten. RPP is closed under inversion and is both PRF-complete and PRF-sound (p.5); it encodes Cantor pairing and packs a computation's history into a single ancilla so garbage is cleaned at the end of each PRF simulation (p.4).
sources.relevance: A small basis for history-free in-place arithmetic that isolates the linearity rule: the value deciding how often to loop, or which branch to take, is never an argument of what it controls and passes through unchanged.

sources.title: A Structural Approach to Reversible Computation (Abramsky, 2005)
sources.quote: Thus there is no "duplicating" or "discarding" of sub-terms matched to variables in applying a rule
sources.mechanism: Pattern-matching automata (Q, q_init, q_final, R) with rules (q, r) → (s, q'). Orthogonal: non-ambiguous and left-linear. Biorthogonal: A and its reverse A^op are both orthogonal, so computation is reversible step by step, and each variable occurs exactly once on each side (p.6). Functional terms compile to such automata of size linear in the term (p.1) via a linear combinatory algebra of partial injections: LApp(f, g) = frr ∪ frl;g;(fll;g)*;flr, and replication !f = {(p(t,u), p(t,v))}, where the first argument of p tags different copies ([p.11](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=11)). Combinators I, K, B, C, D, δ, F, W are realized by partial involutions; K : l(x) ↔ r(r(x)), and its second argument does not get accessed ([p.14](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=14)). The pure λ-calculus / multiplicative-exponential linear logic is interpreted reversibly, possibly with loss of soundness of some conversion rules; adding constants, conditionals and δ-rules loses biorthogonality, because this fails for the additives ([p.25](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=25)). Reading out a result is a further sequence of queries.
sources.relevance: Reuse instead of copy: no duplicator; each query carries a copy tag and one circuit answers every copy; K needs no eraser because the dropped argument is never asked. It locates loss at additive (case/conditional) constructs. Mapping that to tree calculus's triage is an analogy: tree calculus is pure but intensional, which this paper does not treat.

sources.title: Semantics for a Turing-complete Reversible Programming Language with Inductive Types (Chardonnet, Lemonnier, Valiron, 2024)
sources.quote: any computable, partial, first-order injective function is the image of a term in the language
sources.mechanism: A Theseus-based language whose isos can be fixpoints and can abstract over isos. Data contexts are linear; isos are closed computations that can be duplicated or erased at will ([p.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.12151#page=4)). Clauses must be pairwise orthogonal (non-overlapping) but need not be exhaustive or terminating, so isos may diverge or get stuck (pp.4-5). The inverse swaps each clause. Duplication is derived: Dup_A : A ↔ A ⊗ A by induction on the type, one constructor layer at a time, including fold x ↔ let ⟨x1,x2⟩ = Dup x in ⟨fold x1, fold x2⟩ (pp.6-7); its inverse, by partiality, is defined only on equal pairs. erase_v : A ⊗ Σ ↔ A = {⟨x, v⟩ ↔ x} erases its second argument only when its value is v; reversed it turns any x into ⟨x, v⟩ ([p.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.12151#page=7)). The language encodes any reversible Turing machine, has a sound and adequate semantics in join inverse rig categories, and is complete for computable partial first-order injective functions.
sources.relevance: Confirms that copying need not be primitive (layer-wise Dup with merge-on-equal inverse), that non-overlap without full coverage is the right requirement for partial rule tables, and that code may be copied/erased freely while data stays linear. Erasing a known constant is the inverse of making it.

sources.title: Sparcl: A Language for Partially-Invertible Computation (Matsuda, Wang, 2020)
sources.quote: It captures a snapshot of its invertible argument and uses the snapshot as a static value in the body
sources.mechanism: A linear functional language with a type constructor A• for invertible data; invertible functions have type A• ⊸ B•. Unrestricted arguments make functions partially invertible: add : Nat → Nat• ⊸ Nat•, add Z y = y, add (S x) y = S• (add x y) (p.6). pin : A• ⊸ (A → B•) ⊸ (A ⊗ B)• snapshots an invertible value, uses it statically in the body, and returns both (p.4). Invertible case branches carry 'with' conditions used to choose the branch backward (p.7). fwd/bwd run a function either way; fwd e v = u iff bwd e u = v (p.8). Lifted constructors C• are bijective. So (a, b) ↦ (a, a+b) can be written pin a (λa'. add a' b) (the reviewer's derivation, not an example in the paper).
sources.relevance: pin is one primitive for 'use a value without consuming it'. It suggests a pin-shaped reversible apply (f, x) ↦ (f, f x) with the function kept as the static snapshot.

sources.title: Compositional Reversible Computation (Carette, Heunen, Kaarsgaard, Sabry, 2024)
sources.quote: a fundamental limitation of this approach is that it fails to be compositional
sources.mechanism: Survey. (1) History-based reversibility (reversible λ-calculus, RCCS, CCSK) records left-hand sides in a history: ⟨H | A1⟩ → ⟨H, A1 | B⟩. With a global history, a term where one subterm steps forward and another backward needs incompatible actions on it, so composition fails; the paper's stated remedy is to take reversibility as a basic building block rather than an extension. (2) Landauer's history tape and Bennett's compute-copy-uncompute: Bennett's trick gives a reversible way of managing garbage without having to erase it outright, which lets procedures sharing scratch storage compose ([p.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.20842#page=4)). (3) Dagger and rig categories as semantics of Π. (4) Reversible effects as dagger Frobenius monads and arrows. (5) Fundamental theorem: every function f : A → B factors as A → A + H ≅ B × G → B (coproduct injection, iso, product projection) ([p.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.20842#page=10)); the quantum analogue (Stinespring) factors channels the same way.
sources.relevance: Argues against a single global per-rewrite event log as the core's history mechanism; histories must be local and uncomputed where they were made. A + H ≅ B × G is the ledger: H is fuel in, G is garbage out.

sources.title: The Two Dualities of Computation: Negative and Fractional Types (James, Sabry, 2012)
sources.quote: breaking global invariants into local ones that can be autonomously satisfied by a subcomputation
sources.mechanism: Extends Π with negative types (a + (−a) ↔ 0, realized by a dual evaluator that reverses execution for negative values) and fractional types (a × (1/a) ↔ 1, realized with logic variables and unification); combined, Π^η lets any rational number be a type. Negatives are debts satisfied by backtracking (one value exists at a time); fractionals are debts satisfied by constraint propagation, with a schedule in which every value independently and concurrently proceeds through its subcomputation ([p.2](https://web.archive.org/web/20120929133040id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/rational.pdf#page=2)). It would be disastrous if debts could be deleted or duplicated. The compact closed structure gives a trace; 1/(b1×b2) maps to (1/b1)×(1/b2). The multiplicative trace uses η× to generate all candidate values and prunes mismatches, which the paper uses for a SAT solver.
sources.relevance: Two physical readings for loops and fuel: a value flowing backward, or a debt settled concurrently. The concurrent reading is the parallel one, but its operational form is unification over logic variables (and even search over candidate values), so a lattice version would need Fractional Types' layer-wise anti-tree instead.

key_ideas: Controlled update gives history-free in-place updates. Whatever controls a step (a loop count, a branch condition, a static function argument) passes through unchanged and is not an argument of what it controls. Examples: Janus b += a with b not in the expression ([Yokoyama 2010](https://people.cs.rutgers.edu/~uli/cs516/spring2020/readings/ReversibleComputing-TheoreticalCompSci2010.pdf#page=4)); RPP's iteration driver ([Paolini et al.](https://iris.unito.it/retrieve/e27ce42f-52ce-2581-e053-d805fe0acbaa/20-03-23-main-caricato-su-IRIS.pdf#page=8)); RFun v2 ancillae ([Kaarsgaard & Thomsen](https://di.ku.dk/english/research/phd/phd-theses/2018/Robin_Kaarsgaard_Thesis.pdf#page=182)); Sparcl's pin ([Matsuda & Wang](https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/ws/files/244902875/ICFP20.pdf#page=4)). (a, b) → (a, a+b) needs no history because a is both the control and the record. For tree calculus this suggests (the reviewer's inference) a pin-shaped apply (f, x) ↦ (f, f x) and a scrutinee that passes through dispatch, leaving K's dropped argument and the dispatch's choice of arm to account for.

A loop's history can be its own output: count a register up while consuming the input, so the count ends equal to the input. Examples: Theseus's add (x, y) = (x+y, x) ([James & Sabry 2014](https://web.archive.org/web/20170118093456id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/theseus.pdf#page=10)); the adder machine ⟨n+1, p, m⟩ ↦ ⟨n, p+1, m+1⟩ ending at ⟨0, n+p, n⟩ ([James & Sabry 2012](https://web.archive.org/web/20170118155739id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/iso-int.pdf#page=9)); RFun's plus, whose base-case copy is checked for equality when run backward ([Kaarsgaard et al.](https://di.ku.dk/english/research/phd/phd-theses/2018/Robin_Kaarsgaard_Thesis.pdf#page=88)).

Price each disposal by what is already known, following information effects' create/erase asymmetry: create only makes known constants, erase destroys run-time information ([James & Sabry](https://web.archive.org/web/20161007070937id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/information-effects.pdf#page=6)). Three prices: erasing a known constant is the inverse of making it (erase_v = {⟨x, v⟩ ↔ x}, partial on any other value; [Chardonnet et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.12151#page=7)); un-copying needs only the twin (fanin, RFun's dup/eq, layer-wise merge); only erasing run-time-unique information must leave as garbage. (The repo's measured split of erased agents is a repo claim, not from these sources.)

Fuel as antiparticles ([Chen et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.07020#page=5)): η_v : 1 ↔ τ × 1/v and ε_v its inverse. Debts are values: they move, decompose per component (1/(a, b) ↔ 1/a × 1/b, [p.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.07020#page=8)) and can be repaid by any equal value; the only invariant is zero net flow ([p.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2002.07020#page=3)). On a lattice: anti-leaf/anti-stem/anti-fork agents that annihilate a matching layer; a mismatch is where heat is paid.

Whether a rule table is a bijection is a local syntactic check: left patterns must not overlap (and must cover, for a total table), right patterns must not overlap, each variable once per side. See Theseus ([p.5](https://web.archive.org/web/20170118093456id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/theseus.pdf#page=5)) and Abramsky's biorthogonality ([p.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=6)). Partial tables glue when they are inverse-compatible: they agree wherever both are defined, in both directions ([Kaarsgaard et al.](https://di.ku.dk/english/research/phd/phd-theses/2018/Robin_Kaarsgaard_Thesis.pdf#page=92)); disjoint domains plus disjoint ranges is the simplest sufficient case.

Copy need not be primitive. Dup_A by structural recursion, one layer at a time, with merge-on-equal as its (partial) inverse ([Chardonnet et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.12151#page=7)). RFun v1's ⌊·⌋ makes un-copy total and self-inverse (unequal pairs pass through unchanged; [Kaarsgaard et al.](https://di.ku.dk/english/research/phd/phd-theses/2018/Robin_Kaarsgaard_Thesis.pdf#page=88)), so un-copy can be proposed anywhere as a bijective move. Note RFun v2 dropped the operator for relevance typing plus an Eq type class, because programmers found it hard to understand.

Reuse instead of copy ([Abramsky](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=11)): replication is a tag carried by the query, !f = {(p(t,u), p(t,v))}, and K's second argument is simply never accessed ([p.14](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=14)). Copying and erasing then cost nothing; the trade is recomputation and one sequential token per query.

Parallelism is the gap in this field. Everything is sequential except Π's × composition and fractional debts, whose schedule lets every value proceed concurrently ([James & Sabry](https://web.archive.org/web/20120929133040id_/http://www.cs.indiana.edu/~sabry/papers/rational.pdf#page=2)), though that is realized by unification and pruning, not local moves. The token machines (logically reversible abstract machines, Theseus, Abramsky's automata) move one state at a time; maximal parallelism needs programs laid out as circuits that many values flow through at once.

Global histories do not compose ([Carette et al. 2024](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.20842#page=3)); Bennett's compute-copy-uncompute manages garbage without erasing it and lets procedures sharing scratch space compose ([p.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.20842#page=4)). The paper's broader remedy is reversibility as a basic building block. Every function factors as an injection into A + H, an iso, and a projection out of B × G ([p.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.20842#page=10)): H is fuel, G is garbage.

Universality bound: reversible Turing machines compute exactly the injective computable functions ([Axelsen & Glück](https://researchprofiles.ku.dk/en/publications/what-do-reversible-programs-compute/#main-content)), and Theseus-style isos are complete for computable partial first-order injective functions ([Chardonnet et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.12151#page=1)). A non-injective calculus such as tree calculus therefore runs reversibly only embedded, e.g. as x ↦ (x, f x), with garbage, or Bennett-cleaned.

Where loss appears: pure combinatory logic / multiplicative-exponential linear logic has a reversible (history-free) interpretation, while adding constants and conditionals breaks it because 'this fails for the additives' ([Abramsky](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.7154#page=25)). Reading tree calculus's triage as that additive step, and so as the core's irreducible loss together with K's drop, is an analogy the reviewer draws, not a result of the paper.

Program equivalences are themselves reversible programs: the coherence laws of symmetric rig groupoids are the sound and complete reversible program equivalences ('level-2 Π'; [Carette, James, Sabry](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1811.03678#page=1)). This could let .opt.disp overrides be reversible rewrites between circuits that carry their proof.

The classical fundamental theorem (bijections to functions with garbage, Toffoli) and the quantum one (Stinespring) arise from the same categorical construction ([Heunen & Kaarsgaard](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.12144#page=1)), and symmetric pattern matching extends to a notion of quantum control ([Sabry, Valiron, Vizzotto](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1804.00952#page=1)), so a rule table checked as above sits on the classical side of a unitary generalization.

field: Causal-consistent reversibility in concurrency (RCCS, CCSK, reversible pi, reversible Petri nets, out-of-causal-order undo): how undo stays local and parallel with no global clock or table, where the record of the past lives, and how that compares with a record per rewrite

sources.title: Reversible Communicating Systems (RCCS); author preprint titled 'Reversible Communicating Concurrent Systems', CONCUR 2004 (Danos, Krivine)
sources.quote: assign to each currently running thread an individual memory stack keeping track of past communications
sources.mechanism: CCS processes run inside threads m ⊲ P, where m is a stack: ⟨⟩ | ⟨1⟩·m | ⟨2⟩·m (fork) | ⟨*,α,Q⟩·m (semi-synch: did α, partner not yet known; Q is the discarded part of the choice) | ⟨m',α,Q⟩·m (synch with the thread whose memory is m'). Fork is a structural law, m ⊲ (P|Q) ≡ ⟨1⟩·m ⊲ P | ⟨2⟩·m ⊲ Q (#page=5), so each child inherits the parent's whole memory plus a fork number. The memory also 'yield[s] a unique identifier for the thread' (#page=2); coherence (memories branch at a fork) makes memories unique. A synch instantiates each partner's top entry with the other's memory (#page=9). After that 'One doesn't roll back a synchronization all alone': both threads are 'locked together' and the only way back is a backward synch of the same pair, the 'locking effect' (#page=8). Backtracking 'is seen as a synchronization and incurs no additional cost on the communication structure' (#page=1). Main theorem: two traces with the same start and end are causally equivalent; the authors summarise this as 'RCCS is a Lévy labelling for CCS' (#page=2). Discarded choice branches stay in memory. Irreversible actions push a placeholder ⟨◦⟩ with no inverse rule, and a memory-cleansing procedure is proved sound (#page=2, #page=14). No clock, no global table.
sources.relevance: (a) Identity without numeric ids: fork numbers make each thread's memory a unique local name. The forking token machine deleted in 2a32736 (walk.rs, tokens that split at a 'both' and rejoin) has the same shape as RCCS's fork. (b) The locking effect is what a net needs: the two agents of an active pair record each other, so undo is again a binary interaction between the same two things. (c) RCCS's one non-linear move is copying the memory at a fork; a shared fork record would avoid it (disp-side proposal, not in the paper).

sources.title: A Reversible Process Calculus and the Modelling of the ERK Signalling Pathway (CCSK plus execution control)
sources.quote: In order to manage correctly both communication and the reversing of communication we employ communication keys
sources.mechanism: Restates and extends Phillips–Ulidowski's CCSK. All operators are static: a step does not throw away the executed prefix or the losing branch; it marks them. α.X → α[n].X with a key n; a marked prefix still lets X move; X|Y moves on the left only if n is fresh in Y (fsh[n](Y), a check against the parallel sibling, #page=5); a synchronisation needs complementary actions with the same key. The reverse rules are the forward rules read backwards ('The rules for reversing computation are simply symmetric versions of the forward rules', #page=2; 'the reverse rules are simply the reversals of the forward rules', #page=5). A shared key stops one side of a past synch from regressing alone: 'cannot regress by reversing a[m] alone because key m is not fresh' in the sibling (#page=5). No separate memory: the term is its own history. New here: multiset prefixes and forward-only controllers ('controllers can only compute forwards (even when the process under control is reversing)', #page=2) that use key identifiers to steer which actions run or undo. These give out-of-causal-order reversal, used to model bond breaking in the ERK pathway.
sources.relevance: The static recipe is the closest match to 'keep what you would drop': a tree-calculus rewrite could leave its redex in place, marked spent, with K's dropped argument still attached. On a lattice the mark plus a wire between the two spent agents could play the key's role (disp-side proposal). Forward-only controllers are a model for 'something outside the reversible core decides direction'.

sources.title: Static versus dynamic reversibility in CCS (Lanese, Medić, Mezzina; Acta Informatica 58, 2021)
sources.quote: In CCSK, history information is embedded in the process structure, hence it is never duplicated
sources.mechanism: Puts RCCS (in its keyed variant: memories with action events ⟨k,α,Q⟩ and split events ↑; a split duplicates the memory, #page=4) beside CCSK (keys α[k] left in the term; 'the prefix is not discarded during the transition', #page=9). Gives encodings both ways and proves the forward and backward LTSs isomorphic, up to structural congruence and restricted to reachable processes (Theorem 3, #page=28). Neither encoding is compositional, and none can be, because reachable RCCS processes are not closed under parallel composition (#page=2, #page=29). In RCCS, only the side condition of rule R-PAR-L• (key k absent from the other component) stops one side of a synch from undoing alone (#page=6). Their verdict: 'CCSK is more compositional ... hence more easy to work with. On the other side, the approach of RCCS is more flexible', having been extended to π (#page=31).
sources.relevance: Where the record lives (on the thread vs in the structure) is a representation choice that does not change behaviour, for CCS. disp can pick whatever is cheapest on the lattice, e.g. records left in place as spent agents.

sources.title: Causal-Consistent Reversibility (Bulletin of the EATCS 114, survey; Lanese, Mezzina, Tiezzi 2014)
sources.quote: It introduces the notion of memories attached to threads to keep history information
sources.mechanism: Survey. Two things must be stored: what a step destroyed (e.g. a.P+Q → P loses a and Q, #page=5), and causality. Criteria: Loop Lemma, square property and causal equivalence, causal consistency, Parabolic Lemma (#page=5–6). Table 1 (#page=7): RCCS (stacks; memories as ids; fork numbers), CCS-R (stacks; thread ids), CCSK (no memory; communication keys; static rules), ρπ (non-structured memories; thread ids), Rπ (stacks; event ids; fork symbol), Reversible DSD (signal ids), reversible structures ('The gate structure is not consumed, and a cursor reminds which part of the gate already interacted', #page=7), RμOz (stacks; thread ids). Control (#page=8–10): irreversible actions as commit, roll-π explicit rollback to a named past action, alternatives, external controllers, energy-potential control (Bacci et al.). Space: the RμOz abstract-machine work shows 'an amount of history information which is linear in the number of steps is actually needed in the worst case' (#page=12). A step that loses nothing needs no history: x := x+1 'causes no loss of information' (#page=4).
sources.relevance: A menu for disp's core: memory per thread, memory in the structure, a memory entity per step, or memory in the consumer (a gate with a cursor). Steps that lose nothing need no record; for the rest, the worst-case lower bound means records can be shrunk (commit, recomputation) but not removed in general.

sources.title: A parametric framework for reversible π-calculi (Medić, Mezzina, Phillips, Yoshida; Information and Computation 275, 2020)
sources.quote: where elements of a triple are the key, the contextual cause and the label of the executed action
sources.mechanism: Recaps Rπ: m ⊲ P with a memory of events ⟨i,k,π⟩ (key, contextual cause, label) and split events ↑; the structural rule m ⊲ (P|Q) ≡ ↑·m ⊲ P | ↑·m ⊲ Q duplicates the memory (#page=4, #page=16). The new framework instead keeps executed prefixes in place annotated with a key and a set of contextual causes (CCSK style, 'static', #page=3–4). Each restriction ν a is decorated with a data structure Δ recording the extruders of a (#page=5); Δ is an abstract parameter, e.g. a set of keys or an ordered structure that remembers the first extruder (#page=6). An input on an extruded name picks a contextual cause from Δ, and different instantiations of Δ reproduce the different causal semantics of reversible π in the literature. Choice is left out (it could be added by making + static, #page=5).
sources.relevance: Negative but useful: most of reversible π's extra machinery exists because names are created, passed and extruded. Interaction nets have linear wires and no name passing, so disp's case needs only structural causality and can skip this machinery (disp-side inference).

sources.title: A General Approach to Derive Uncontrolled Reversible Semantics (Lanese, Medić; CONCUR 2020)
sources.quote: each entity of a system is labelled with its unique key. Also, each step of the system produces a memory allowing one to undo it
sources.mechanism: Input: a reduction semantics whose steps have the form P1|…|Pn → T[Q1,…,Qm] (#page=3). Output: a causal-consistent reversible semantics. Forward rule (F-Scm-Act, #page=6): k1:P1|…|kn:Pn → T[j1:Q1,…,jm:Qm] | [k1:P1|…|kn:Pn ; T[j1:•1,…,jm:•m]] with j fresh; 'the side condition ensuring that keys introduced during the step are fresh for the whole system' is the novelty (#page=6). Backward: the products plus their memory step back to the consumed entities. The memory is an entity in parallel (as in ρπ), not a table. Loop Lemma, Square Lemma, causal consistency, causal safety and liveness follow from the Lanese–Phillips–Ulidowski axioms (#page=8). Case studies: higher-order π and Core Erlang (including links).
sources.relevance: This is a proved-sound generic form of a record per rewrite (what was consumed plus keyed placeholders for what was made), the same shape as rev.rs's event record and the lattice substrate's records. Interaction-net rules (two agents become a small net) fit the n→T[m] shape if the wires to the rest of the net are treated as names, as HOπ does. Replacing keys by wires from the record to its products is a disp-side proposal.

sources.title: Reversibility in Massive Concurrent Systems (reversible structures; Cardelli, Laneve; SACS 21, 2011)
sources.quote: the symbol ^, called gate pointer, indicates the next operations (one forward and one backward)
sources.mechanism: Signals u:a (name a, history id u; in DNA the id is a 'history domain', #page=5) and gates A⊥.^B.C / A⊥.B.^C (absorbed inputs, wanted inputs, outputs, pointer ^, #page=8). Four axioms in two inverse pairs (#page=10): input capture u:a | A⊥.^a.B.C → A⊥.u:a.^B.C and input release (its inverse); output release A⊥.B.^u:a.C → u:a | A⊥.B.u:a.^C and output capture (its inverse). The gate is not consumed: it keeps what it absorbed and the pointer records progress, so history lives in the gate. 'Coherent' structures have singleton populations per species, and then causality agrees with RCCS (#page=2). 'Weak coherent' means 'ids are uniquely associated to names and co-names' (Def. 2, #page=11): several copies may share an id, so a backward step may release a different but same-id copy (example on #page=10). Weak-coherent structures are implemented with three-domain DNA strands via toehold exchange, and an asynchronous sub-calculus of RCCS is compiled into reversible structures. Process-calculus reversibility would require one 'to remember the position and momentum of each molecule' (#page=2), contrary to well-mixing; direction comes from 'an appropriate injection of energy and/or a change of entropy' (#page=2).
sources.relevance: A template for an apply with no separate record: the apply agent captures function and argument, releases the result, and keeps inside itself whatever K or triage drops. It also frames a choice for disp: exact identities (coherent) versus interchangeable copies carrying a shared history id (weak coherent).

sources.title: Reversing Place Transition Nets (Melgratti, Mezzina, Ulidowski; LMCS 16(4), 2020)
sources.quote: an occurrence net can be reversed by adding a reverse transition for each of its transitions
sources.mechanism: The key difficulty is backward conflict: 'a token can be generated in a place due to different causes' (#page=2). An occurrence net (acyclic, 1-safe, no backward conflicts, no self-conflicts, #page=6) is reversed by adding one reverse transition per transition, giving causal-consistent reversibility with no memory; every marking reachable in the reversed occurrence net is reachable by forward steps alone (#page=3). A P/T net is unfolded into a possibly infinite occurrence net, which is re-expressed as 'a finite net whose tokens are coloured by causal histories' (#page=1), colours being terms built from a(h, i) and t(H) (#page=7). The authors note colours resemble the memories of reversible process calculi.
sources.relevance: An exact test for when no record is needed: if each result could only have come from one producer (no backward conflict), the mirror rule alone reverses it. For disp, a second test (does the rule destroy data) must be added, since P/T tokens carry no data. Colouring products with a provenance term is an alternative to a record agent, but the colour grows and is carried by every output token.

sources.title: Reversible Computation in Cyclic Petri Nets (reversing Petri nets; Philippou, Psara 2020)
sources.quote: A base is a persistent type of token which cannot be consumed and therefore preserves its individuality
sources.mechanism: Reversing Petri nets have bases (individual tokens, neither erased nor cloned) and bonds between them. Transitions move bases and bonded clusters and create bonds. To decide what can be reversed, 'we associate transitions with a history storing keys in increasing order each time an instance of the transition is executed' (#page=9); a new key is max of all keys in the net plus one (#page=13). Backtracking: a transition is bt-enabled 'if its history contains the highest value among all transitions' (#page=16). Causal reversal: the state also carries a causal-dependence relation ≺ over transition occurrences, and t is reversible when nothing it caused remains (#page=24). Out-of-causal order: any executed transition may be reversed; when broken bonds split a coalition, 'each of these coalitions should flow back, as far back as possible, after the last transition in which this sub-coalition participated'. Out-of-order reversal 'is able to create new states unreachable by forward-only execution' (#page=4).
sources.relevance: Good: conserved individual matter with bonds as part of the record fits a 'fermions and bosons' picture. Bad: as soon as undo must respect order not visible in the bonds, this model uses a global counter and a global causality relation, which is the thing to avoid. Out-of-order undo reaching new states is how a catalyst gets released.

sources.title: Modelling of Bonding with Processes and Events (Phillips, Ulidowski, Yuen; RC 2013)
sources.quote: having helped A and B to react, the bond between C and A is broken thus releasing C into a solution to help other A, B pairs
sources.mechanism: Reaction systems for bonding: bases have a sort and an arity (maximum number of bonds; objects are undirected graphs whose node degrees are bounded by arity, #page=2–3); a system is a multiset of molecules. Rules say which bonds form (→) and which dissolve (⇝). Catalysis (#page=4): C,A → C·A; C·A,B → C·A·B; C·A·B ⇝ C, A·B. The enabling C–A bond is dissolved after the A–B bond formed, i.e. out of causal order, and C is freed unchanged. Long-running transactions with a compensation step are modelled the same way (#page=5). The paper also introduces reversible event structures, which allow reversal both in and out of causal order, and builds one from a reaction system.
sources.relevance: A pattern for reusing a circuit by binding, acting and releasing it instead of copying it. Applying it to tree-calculus apply would need an apply that reads the function without consuming it (disp-side inference). The 'reversible add with no leftover record' idea is a disp-side proposal, not in the paper.

sources.title: On the Statistical Thermodynamics of Reversible Communicating Processes (Bacci, Danos, Kammar; CALCO 2011)
sources.quote: processes must have a probability to fork that decreases exponentially as a function of the size of their local memory
sources.mechanism: RCCS with many-way synchronisation, made stochastic. Because memories hold history, 'the transition graph of a reversibilized process is acyclic because it incorporates its own history' (#page=3), more precisely nearly acyclic, i.e. acyclic up to swaps of concurrent steps (#page=5, #page=7). Hence any rates whose ratios come from a potential satisfy detailed balance for free; only convergence is an issue. Two potentials (#page=9): V0 charges only synchs along the path (forks free). It has no simple inductive formula, but it can still be met by 'a locally implementable rate function' (kf− = kf+, ka−/ka+ = exp(εa)). V1 sums the energies recorded in each thread's memory; fork rate e^(−(n−1)V1(Γ)) is 'an entirely local solution'. Section 5 shows explosive growth: if forks are too cheap (as under V0) histories multiply faster than energy penalises them and no equilibrium exists. Convergence holds if the fork penalty per unit of memory exceeds α²β·log(4(β+1)) (α = max threads synchronising at once, β = max successive forks between communications, #page=2); then a success state is reached in finite mean time (#page=1).
sources.relevance: Directly about Metropolis moves on a lattice: once the state records its history, detailed balance comes for free; the danger is entropy from copying. A duplicator's energy cost should grow with the history it copies, computed locally. Whether explosive growth arises in a deterministic, conflict-free net is open.

sources.title: Bridging Causal Reversibility and Time Reversibility: A Stochastic Process Algebraic Approach (Bernardo, Mezzina; LMCS 19(2), 2023)
sources.quote: time reversibility can be obtained by using in the operational semantic rules backward rates equal to the corresponding forward rates
sources.mechanism: RMPC is a Markovian process calculus reversed with Phillips–Ulidowski's static method (executed actions stay in the term with keys); each backward label carries its own backward rate (#page=6). Causal reversibility is proved via the Lanese–Phillips–Ulidowski axioms (#page=11–13). Time reversibility is Kolmogorov's criterion: the product of rates around any cycle is the same in both directions (#page=2). It holds if every backward rate equals its forward rate, or, whatever the rates, if 'parallel composition cannot occur within the scope of action prefix or choice' (#page=3). This supports efficient product-form steady-state computation (#page=16).
sources.relevance: A check for a lattice acceptance rule: either use symmetric base rates and put all bias in an energy landscape, or know which shapes keep detailed balance whatever the rates. Spawning parallel work after an action is exactly what can break it.

key_ideas: Undo stays local because causality is stored as links between the things that interacted, not as timestamps. RCCS partners write each other's memory into their own and are then 'locked together' (they can only undo jointly); CCSK partners share a key left in the term; Lanese–Medić records name their products by key. An undo is enabled by a local test: all products of the step are present and unused. Reversing Petri nets show the alternative to avoid: a global increasing key counter and a stored global causality relation, used for all three of their undo modes. Sources: [RCCS](http://web.archive.org/web/20060528171615id_/http://www.pps.jussieu.fr:80/~danos/pdf/rccs.pdf#page=8), [Lanese–Medić](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol171-concur2020/LIPIcs.CONCUR.2020.33/LIPIcs.CONCUR.2020.33.pdf#page=5), [Philippou–Psara](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.04000#page=9).

A record per rewrite is proved sound in general. Lanese–Medić turn any reduction semantics with steps 'n entities → context with m entities' into a causal-consistent reversible one by emitting a memory [consumed ; products-with-fresh-keys] per step. Interaction-net rules fit this shape if boundary wires are treated as names. Their keys must be fresh for the whole system; replacing each key with a wire from the record to its products is the disp-side proposal for removing the numbered record table that the lattice substrate (phys=1) still uses. Source: [Lanese–Medić](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/storage/00lipics/lipics-vol171-concur2020/LIPIcs.CONCUR.2020.33/LIPIcs.CONCUR.2020.33.pdf#page=6).

For CCS, where the record lives does not change behaviour: memory on the thread (RCCS) and memory left in the term (CCSK) give isomorphic transition systems. The in-place form is more compositional and never duplicates history at a fork; the thread form has proved easier to extend (to π). In-place marking means the redex stays as a spent node and the program becomes its own trace. Sources: [Static vs dynamic](https://iris.unito.it/bitstream/2318/1891802/2/s00236-019-00346-6.pdf#page=2), [CCSK rules](https://www.cs.le.ac.uk/people/iu3/Publications/RC2012-Web.pdf#page=2).

Only some steps need a record. A step that loses no information reverses by its inverse alone (x := x+1). In a net whose places each have at most one producer (no backward conflict), adding one mirror transition per transition is enough. For disp, a rule needs no record if it neither destroys data nor has a result that could have come from a different redex; the data test is a disp-side addition, since Petri-net tokens carry no data. Sources: [Melgratti et al.](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.04266#page=3), [survey](https://bulletin.eatcs.org/index.php/beatcs/article/download/305/287#page=4).

Memory in the consumer. A reversible-structures gate absorbs its inputs and keeps them, and a pointer marks how far it got. Four rules (capture or release an input, release or capture an output) form two inverse pairs, and the gate is never consumed. Modelling apply this way would keep what K or triage drops inside the spent apply agent, with no separate record. Source: [Cardelli–Laneve](https://lucacardelli.name/Papers/Reversibility%20in%20Massive%20Concurrent%20Systems%20%28SACS%29.pdf#page=10).

Exact versus interchangeable identity. In coherent reversible structures every species is a singleton, and causality matches RCCS.
