In weakly coherent ones each history id belongs to one name, but several copies may share an id, so an undo may release a different copy with the same id. Ids do not disappear; they become per-species instead of per-molecule. For a deterministic calculus where equal trees are interchangeable, this may be enough (open). Sources: [Cardelli–Laneve, coherence](https://lucacardelli.name/Papers/Reversibility%20in%20Massive%20Concurrent%20Systems%20%28SACS%29.pdf#page=2), [weak coherence defined](https://lucacardelli.name/Papers/Reversibility%20in%20Massive%20Concurrent%20Systems%20%28SACS%29.pdf#page=11).

Reuse a circuit instead of copying it, by catalysis: bind, react, then dissolve the enabling bond out of causal order, so the catalyst leaves unchanged. Out-of-order undo reaches states that forward execution cannot. Applying this to a function in disp needs an apply that reads the function without consuming it (open). Sources: [bonding](https://www.cs.le.ac.uk/people/iulidowski/MGS/2014/RC2013.pdf#page=4), [Philippou–Psara](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.04000#page=4).

Commit means no record, and records it depends on become collectable. An irreversible action needs no memory ('there is no need to remember anything, so one uses instead a placeholder'). Memories that can never be undone again are 'locked' and can be collected. On a lattice this could be a priced 'forget' that walks back along made-by wires and pays heat per record erased (disp-side proposal). Sources: [Transactions in RCCS](http://web.archive.org/web/20110706161151id_/http://www.pps.jussieu.fr/~danos/pdf/transactions.pdf#page=4), [collecting locked memories](http://web.archive.org/web/20110706161151id_/http://www.pps.jussieu.fr/~danos/pdf/transactions.pdf#page=7).

Physics of a history-keeping system. Its state graph is nearly acyclic (acyclic up to swapping concurrent steps), so any rates derived from a potential give detailed balance for free. The thing to price is entropy from copying: with free forks histories explode and there is no equilibrium. Fork cost must grow with the memory being copied, and that can be computed locally. Keep base rates symmetric and put all bias in energy. Energy written as local patterns with a finite refined rule set (thermodynamic graph rewriting) keeps detailed balance with fixed per-rule rates. Sources: [Bacci et al.](http://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/people/ohad.kammar/publications/bacci-danos-kammar-on-the-statistical-thermodynamics-of-communicating-processes.pdf#page=9), [Bernardo–Mezzina](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.01420#page=3), [Danos–Harmer–Honorato-Zimmer](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1503.06022#page=1).

Direction is relative. In Aubert–Krivine, reversible computation is a (partial) group action in which every event is its own inverse, and 'the backward or forward orientation of an event exists only relatively to a given past state'. This matches 'every rule is reversible; energy picks the direction'. Source: [Aubert–Krivine 2025](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.06585#page=2).

No name passing, no name causality. Most of reversible π's machinery (a parametric record of extruders on each restriction, contextual causes) tracks causality created by passing private names around. Linear wires without name passing leave disp only structural causality. Source: [Medić et al.](https://iris.unito.it/retrieve/aa62db52-ce84-46f0-9945-52b247c9bd09/1-s2.0-S0890540120301322-main.pdf#page=16).

Check reversibility with a few local axioms on a transition system with independence instead of global theorems: square property, backward transitions are independent, well-foundedness, and coinitial propagation of independence. Causal consistency, causal safety and causal liveness then follow. Source: [Lanese–Phillips–Ulidowski](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.13360#page=1).

The forking token machine had RCCS's shape. walk.rs (deleted in 2a32736) split a token only at a 'both' and rejoined the halves, like RCCS's fork with fork numbers, so it was parallel only where a program said 'both'. In an interaction net every ready pair is independent, so the same memory discipline would give parallelism everywhere. Source: [RCCS](http://web.archive.org/web/20060528171615id_/http://www.pps.jussieu.fr:80/~danos/pdf/rccs.pdf#page=2).

Hard floor. In the worst case, causal-consistent undo needs history linear in the number of steps (result reported for a reversible abstract machine). Steps that lose nothing need none, so in practice the bound bites on lossy steps (inference), and records can be reduced by commit or recomputation but not abolished in general. Source: [survey](https://bulletin.eatcs.org/index.php/beatcs/article/download/305/287#page=12).

field: History, garbage and clean space as resources: Bennett's reversible computation and pebbling, time/space/heat tradeoffs, catalytic (borrowed full-memory) computation, dirty ancillae, automatic uncomputation, reversible adders

sources.title: Logical Reversibility of Computation (Bennett 1973)
sources.quote: there exists a subtle mutual redundancy between it and the machine that produced it
sources.mechanism: A reversible Turing machine built from quadruples. Each quadruple either reads and writes or shifts, and each is a one-to-one map on whole-machine states. The inverse of a quadruple swaps its start and end states and negates the shift. The run has three stages. (1) Run forward, writing the index of each transition used onto an initially blank history tape. (2) Copy the output onto a blank output tape. This is reversible and adds no history ('the generation (or erasure) of a duplicate copy of data requires no throwing away of information', #Eqn11). (3) Run the inverse quadruples. They read the history back off, clear the history tape and turn the working tape back into the input. What remains is the input plus a copy of the output. Peak cost is one history record per step. To save space, the job can be cut into n segments, each run and then retraced. Each segment leaves a restart dump for the next segment and also a copy of its own input. The chain of dumps is a higher-level history: after the final output is copied, a higher-level reversal erases it. With the best choice of segment count, this needs about 2*sqrt(ns) of storage for twice the time (#Table2). This is the seed of pebbling. When the output determines the input and an inverse program exists, a seven-stage version maps input to output and leaves nothing else (#Discussion): compute f, copy, uncompute f; swap; compute f^-1, cancel the extra input copy, uncompute f^-1. The history can be erased reversibly because it is redundant with the machine that produced it.
sources.relevance: Already used by `bennett` in evaluators/rust-ic-strands/crate/src/iso.rs and cited (via another copy) in research/REVERSIBLE_PIPELINE.md. Two things carry over. (a) The redundancy argument: a residue (the part a rewrite drops) can be removed reversibly by its own producer's inverse, so it should stay wired to the rewrite that made it rather than go into a global trace. The stronger claim, that only the producer's inverse can do this, comes from Bennett 1982 #page=20. (b) The seven-stage construction is the general recipe for running injective programs with no history, given an inverse program.

sources.title: The Thermodynamics of Computation - a Review (Bennett 1982)
sources.quote: Six of these could be converted into blank tapes by a logically and thermodynamically reversible process
sources.mechanism: Brownian computers: the computation is a path of states that the system random-walks along, with a slight drift from a weak driving force. Drift velocity is proportional to that force, so dissipation per step goes to zero only as speed does (#page=1). The worked example is RNA polymerase (#page=8 to #page=11). The reaction is reversible, and the enzyme is pushed forward because metabolism keeps the pyrophosphate concentration away from equilibrium. A drive of epsilon per step gives a forward/backward step ratio of exp(epsilon/kT) and, for small epsilon, a speed proportional to epsilon. Fuel (#page=31): a tape of N zeros can do NkT ln2 of useful work as it randomizes. Seven identical copies of a random tape can be reversibly turned into six blank tapes plus one random tape, by subtracting one copy from another digit by digit. Copying onto blank tape is a 1:1 operation with no irreducible kT ln2 cost (#page=20, #page=25). Erasing one of two copies known to be identical is the logical inverse of copying (#page=27). History: an 'untidy' reversible machine keeps a history tape, and its inverse (the cleanup machine) erases it. That cleanup machine is 'not a general-purpose garbage disposer: the only garbage it can erase is the garbage produced by the untidy machine of which it is the inverse' (#page=20).
sources.relevance: This grounds a price list. One unit of fuel is a blank site or strand. A copy (duplicator) uses up a blank; un-copying a twin known to be identical gives the blank back. Erasing unique data costs about kT ln2 per bit. N known-equal copies are worth N-1 blanks, so an eraser that cancels a duplicator before it has diverged from its twin is a refund, not heat. Treating epsilon per forward rewrite as the Metropolis bias is our extrapolation, not something the paper says about lattices.

sources.title: Reversibility and Adiabatic Computation: Trading Time and Space for Energy (Li, Vitanyi 1996)
sources.quote: If one deletes a pebble not following the above rules, then this means a block of bits of size S is erased irreversibly
sources.mechanism: Models Bennett's 1989 simulation as a reversible pebble game on nodes 1..T_G. Each node stands for S steps of the irreversible run, and a pebble is a stored S-bit checkpoint. A pebble may be put on or taken off node 1 at any time. On node i>1 it may be put on or taken off only while node i-1 is pebbled. Lemma 1: n pebbles cannot win for T_G >= 2^n. This lower bound holds within the pebble-game model; the authors conjecture it applies to all reversible simulations (#page=13). Bennett's strategy wins for 2^n - 1 nodes in about 3^n moves, so it uses space nS and time about S*T_G^(log 3) (#page=10). Taking a pebble off against the rules means irreversibly erasing S bits. They show you CAN save kS of space at the cost of (2^(k+2)-1)S erased bits (#page=4, #page=12); this is an upper bound, not shown to be optimal. With no time or space limits, the least irreversibility cost of computing y from x is within a log term of C(y|x)+C(x|y) (#page=16-17). That cost counts BOTH the program bits supplied and the garbage bits left over: E_R(x,y) = min{|p|+|q| : R(<x,p>) = <y,q>}.
sources.relevance: REVERSIBLE_PIPELINE.md already cites the pebble rule (line 135). New use: give each stored residue an energy cost (a chemical potential) on the lattice, so the dynamics itself trades space against recomputation. The erasure rate means the first pebble saved costs 7S erased bits, and each further pebble roughly doubles the bill, so forgetting pays only for a few levels. The C(x|y)+C(y|x) theorem bounds total irreversibility. The finer split, where the erased part is about C(x|y), comes from the Information Distance paper (arXiv 1006.3520), not from this one.

sources.title: Time and Space Bounds for Reversible Simulation (Buhrman, Tromp, Vitanyi 2001)
sources.quote: The configuration tree can be traversed by alternating two permutations on half-edges
sources.mechanism: Covers the whole time/space range of reversible simulation. At one end is LMT (Lange, McKenzie, Tapp), with exponential time and 'hardly any extra space'. It walks the tree of configurations around the input configuration as an Euler tour, alternating two permutations on half-edges: a swap that crosses an edge, and a rotation to the next half-edge at the same configuration. A log m-bit counter, incremented on forward simulated steps and decremented on backward ones, lets the walk stop m steps ahead. It then XORs that configuration into a target section and walks back, and the starting copy is blanked by XOR against the original (bridge(), #page=8). At the other end is Bennett's pebbling with log T levels. A hybrid with k pebbles takes S*3^k*2^O(T/2^k) time and O(kS) space (#page=3). k=0 is LMT and k=log T is Bennett. k = log log T gives subexponential time and subquadratic space at the same time.
sources.relevance: An analogy for the deleted token machine (commit 2a32736, 'take out the machines that walk a program'). The no-history end is a single walker with only a step counter, so it is sequential and exponential in time. Speed comes only from checkpoints (stored history). LMT walks the configuration graph of an IRREVERSIBLE machine, predecessor branches included, which differs from iso's token walking an already-reversible program. Our hypothesis: iso's two-way combinators are a reversible dataflow language, and it was the walker that made them sequential. The paper does not test this.

sources.title: Time and space complexity of reversible pebbling (Kralovic 2004)
sources.quote: a pebble can be removed from a vertex v if and only if all direct predecessors of the vertex v are covered by pebbles
sources.mechanism: A reversible pebble game on any DAG. R1: a pebble may be placed on v if and only if all direct predecessors of v are pebbled. R2: it may be removed under the same condition. The game differs from the standard pebble game only in R2. Results for the chain: optimal space is Theta(lg n), and pebbling a chain with optimal space needs Omega(n lg n) time for infinitely many n (O(n^log2 3) is achievable). Time/space tradeoffs for chains are given (#page=9). The complete binary tree of height h has a tight optimal-space bound of h + Theta(lg* h), compared with h+1 for the standard game (#page=3).
sources.relevance: R1/R2 is a local uncompute rule for a net: an intermediate agent may be built or unbuilt only while the agents it was computed from are still wired to it. This is analogous to Unqomp's ordering edges and Silq's const. The tree bound applies only when the computation's DEPENDENCY graph is a complete binary tree, as in a balanced divide-and-conquer fold. A term merely being tree-shaped is not enough. A reduction sequence is a chain, which needs Theta(lg n) live values for n steps and more than linear time at that space.

sources.title: Computing with a full memory: catalytic space (Buhrman, Cleve, Koucky, Loff, Speelman 2014)
sources.quote: it is not sufficient to have just reversibility
sources.mechanism: Catalytic space: a small amount of clean space plus a large auxiliary memory that holds arbitrary, possibly incompressible content and must be returned exactly. Transparent programs over a ring R use registers r1..rm and instructions ri <- ri +/- u*v, where u and v are constants or registers other than ri. An instruction's inverse swaps + and -, and a program's inverse runs the inverted instructions in reverse order (#page=5). P transparently computes f into ri if it ends with ri = tau_i + f(x), with the other registers arbitrary. The cleaning step (#page=6) runs r -= r1, then P, then r += r1, then P^-1. Every register returns to its start value except r, which gains f(x); this 'cleanly' computes f. Footnote 6 (#page=5): any instruction ri <- sigma(ri), where sigma is a permutation of R that may depend on the inputs and the other registers, is also reversible. Results: TC1 is in catalytic logspace (so is the determinant), and catalytic logspace is in ZPP. Plain reversibility is not enough, because reversible simulations [Ben73, LMT97, BTV01] need memory that starts blank. Their example use case is memory filled by a paused background computation (#page=2).
sources.relevance: Adding into a cell instead of writing into a blank one is what lets junk serve as workspace: the borrowed value's contribution cancels in the difference. For disp, the residues that K and triage (two of the core tree-calculus rules) leave could become lendable registers. Footnote 6 matters here: reversibility alone needs only a family of permutations of a cell indexed by other cells. The cleaning trick also uses subtraction (a group). Copying onto a blank (Dup) is the special case where the target starts blank.

sources.title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems (Mertz 2023)
sources.quote: formally cancel out the contributions of the initialized catalytic tape without ever inspecting its values
sources.mechanism: A survey of space reuse. Lemma 1 (#page=9, adapted from Ben-Or and Cleve and from Barrington) uses three bit registers in an arbitrary start state (tau0, tau1, tau2). For each gate g, a program Pg(i) does Ri += value(g) and leaves the other registers unchanged. For an AND of g1 and g2 into R0 (#page=10): P1(1); R0 += R1R2; P2(2); R0 += R1R2; P1(1); R0 += R1R2; P2(2); R0 += R1R2. Over F2 each P undoes itself, the tau cross terms cancel, and R0 = tau0 + v1v2. Each AND makes four recursive calls, so length grows like 4^depth with 3 registers, which gives Barrington-style width-8 branching programs. Catalytic machines are made reversible by an Eulerian tour around the configuration graph (#page=26). Update (#page=34): Cook and Mertz [CM23] found IMPROVED clean register programs (space n+1 over a linear-size ring, O(n) recursive calls), which put TreeEval (tree evaluation) in O(log n * log log n) space.
sources.relevance: The 8-step AND is the smallest worked example of reusing borrowed workspace without looking at it, and it is a tree recursion. The cost is sequential recursion, exponential in depth, which works against parallelism. Williams (2025) extends Cook and Mertz to simulate time t in O(sqrt(t log t)) space; that claim is checked separately at https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.17779#page=1, and this survey (2023) does not contain it.

sources.title: Quantum networks for elementary arithmetic operations (Vedral, Barenco, Ekert 1996)
sources.quote: This enables us to reuse the same temporary register
sources.mechanism: A plain adder |a,b> -> |a,a+b> with a carry register that starts at 0. A network of CARRY gates (Toffolis and a CNOT) computes each carry c(i+1) = MAJ(ai, bi, ci), up to the most significant bit of the result. Then every carry step except the last is undone in reverse order, which resets the carries to 0; during this sweep SUM gates write bi <- ai XOR bi XOR ci (#page=3, Fig. 2 on #page=8). Run backwards, the network subtracts, and the top bit then signals overflow and acts as a comparison. Modular addition adds, subtracts N, CNOTs the overflow bit into a temporary qubit, and later resets that qubit with a further subtraction and comparison (#page=3-4). Modular multiplication computes (x,0) -> (x, ax mod N), swaps the registers, and runs the multiplier for a^-1 mod N backwards, 'resetting one of the registers to zero and freeing it' (#page=12). Modular exponentiation needs 7n+1 qubits, reducible to 4n+3 (#page=5).
sources.relevance: Two reusable patterns. (1) Write the output during the uncompute sweep, which merges Bennett's copy stage into his cleanup. (2) For a bijection f, go (x,0) -> (x,f(x)) -> swap -> (0,f(x)) by running f^-1's circuit backwards. In disp terms, an injective tree function plus its inverse gives an in-place version that leaves no residue.

sources.title: A new quantum ripple-carry addition circuit (Cuccaro, Draper, Kutin, Moulton 2004)
sources.quote: we apply the UMA gate, which restores ai to Ai and ci to Ai-1 and writes si to Bi
sources.mechanism: Wires are interleaved on a line: c0, b0, a0, b1, a1, ..., b(n-1), a(n-1), z. c0 = 0 is the single ancilla, and z receives the high bit. MAJ acts in place on three neighbours (ci, bi, ai): CNOTs from ai onto bi and ci, then a Toffoli controlled by ci and bi onto ai, leaving c(i+1) in ai's cell. MAJ ripples up the line, the last carry is CNOTed into z, and UMA ('UnMajority and Add': a Toffoli plus 2 or 3 CNOTs) ripples back down. UMA restores ai and ci and writes si into bi's cell. Result: (a, b, z) -> (a, a+b mod 2^n, z XOR s_n), with the ancilla back at 0. The basic circuit has linear depth. The improved version reaches depth 2n+4 by combining several changes (#page=3): the first CNOTs of all MAJs, and the last CNOTs of all UMAs, each go in one time slice; the 3-CNOT UMA is used; each Toffoli is swapped past a commuting CNOT of the neighbouring gate; and c1 is computed with a single Toffoli.
sources.relevance: The reference answer to 'a reversible add (a,b) -> (a,a+b) that leaves no history and reuses its own history'. On the way out, park each step's history in the data being walked; on the way back, consume it while writing the output. Two 3-site bijective lattice rules (MAJ, UMA) on a chain of bit sites would run it as physics. Applying the same shape to a zipper walk over a tree is our proposal; the paper does not discuss it.

sources.title: Factoring with n+2 clean qubits and n-1 dirty qubits (Gidney 2017)
sources.quote: dirty bits are more plentiful, since any temporarily unused bit is a borrowable dirty bit
sources.mechanism: Quantum circuits for Shor's algorithm, built almost entirely from classical reversible gates (NOT, CNOT, Toffoli), that use dirty ancillae. A dirty ancilla is a qubit in an unknown and possibly entangled state that must be restored by the end. Any temporarily unused qubit can be borrowed, and controlled modular addition can borrow its own controls (#page=7). Tricks: (1) Increment a register by subtracting x and then NOT x = -x-1, for any x, so the borrowed x cancels (#page=8-9). (2) For increment, cut the need from n dirty bits to one by splitting the register into halves (#page=9). (3) 'Commutator controlling': find G and H whose commutator G*H*G^-1*H^-1 equals the wanted operation, so only one of them needs controls. For addition, H is NOT on every target wire, since NOT(NOT x + K) = x - K, and only the NOTs need controls (#page=8). (4) Comparison, as in Haner et al. [14]: an addition followed by a slightly smaller subtraction, which leaves only the overflow signal in the target bit (#page=7).
sources.relevance: Rule of thumb for the core. Reuse one after another means borrowing, which is free if the borrowed state comes back exactly. Reuse at the same time means copying: one blank per copy, refunded by un-copy. The commutator trick keeps control local: a big operation is controlled by controlling only a cheap self-inverse step around it.

sources.title: Unqomp: Synthesizing Uncomputation in Quantum Circuits (Paradis, Bichsel, Steffen, Vechev 2021)
sources.quote: temporary values produced during the computation must be reset to zero before they can be safely discarded
sources.mechanism: Automatic uncomputation on a circuit graph, a DAG instead of a gate sequence (#page=5-6). Each qubit has an init node and then one node per gate that targets it. Edges are target and control edges, plus anti-dependency edges (t before c whenever some value c' controls t and is then overwritten by c). Any order consistent with the graph gives the same circuit. To uncompute ancilla a, Unqomp processes the gates that targeted a, last first (Algorithm, #page=8). For each one it asserts the gate is qfree (classical on basis states), inserts its inverse with the same controls (using already-uncomputed versions where possible), and adds anti-dependency edges so the inverse comes after the last use of a's value and before any of its controls is overwritten. It then asserts the graph has no cycles, rejecting the program otherwise, and finally linearizes the graph. Compared with existing Qiskit implementations that uncompute by hand, the results average 71% fewer gates and 19% fewer qubits.
sources.relevance: A local uncompute rule that does not depend on a global order. Pair each write to a temporary with its inverse, and fire the inverse once the temporary's last reader is done and while its inputs are still attached. In disp's net this would be an 'unwrite' partner for each rewrite that leaves a residue, scheduled by dataflow. Where Unqomp hits a cycle it just rejects the program. Reading those cases as the residues that must be pebbled or erased is our interpretation; Unqomp does not analyse them.

sources.title: Silq: A High-Level Quantum Language with Safe Uncomputation and Intuitive Semantics (Bichsel, Baader, Gehr, Vechev 2020)
sources.quote: uncomputing x is possible whenever in every summand of the state, the value of x can be reconstructed
sources.mechanism: A quantum language that is linear by default: quantum parameters are consumed unless marked const, meaning kept in the context and readable. qfree functions add no superposition, so their effect can be described classically, and mfree functions perform no measurement (#page=7). 'Lifted' means qfree with only const parameters (#page=5). A lifted subexpression whose result is not consumed is uncomputed automatically by reversing the reconstruction, because its value can be rebuilt from the const arguments still present. A non-lifted quantum expression must be consumed, or the program is rejected (#page=6-7). The general principle is a sufficient condition: x can be uncomputed WHENEVER its value is determined by the other values in every summand. Silq's type system enforces a static version of it through 'lifted'. Weakening and contraction (dropping and duplicating) are allowed only for classical (!tau) and const variables, and a dropped const variable is uncomputed at the end of the function (#page=8).
sources.relevance: This is the 'reader that does not consume' that REVERSIBLE_PIPELINE.md says is missing at Bennett's copy step: add a const (borrow) mode to disp's linear core. Dropping a lifted result is a refund, and any other drop must be an explicit, priced erasure. The droppability test (is the value determined by what is still present?) is a concrete version of the user's 'entropy relative to what the system knows'.

key_ideas: Three currencies: fuel, heat and space. A blank is fuel. Copying onto a blank and erasing one of two copies KNOWN to be identical are both reversible: a copy spends one blank and an un-copy refunds it. N known-equal copies are worth N-1 blanks. Erasing unique data costs about kT ln2 per bit. Sources: Bennett 1982 (https://sites.pitt.edu/~jdnorton/lectures/Rotman_Summer_School_2013/thermo_computing_docs/Bennett_1982.pdf#page=31); Bennett 2003, quote 'erasure of one of two copies of data known to be identical' (https://arxiv.org/pdf/physics/0210005#page=2).

Residues stay where they were made. History can be removed reversibly by its producer's inverse, because it is redundant with the machine that produced it (Bennett 1973, https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/fall06/cos576/papers/bennett73.html#Introduction). Bennett 1982 adds that the cleanup machine can erase only the garbage of the machine it inverts (https://sites.pitt.edu/~jdnorton/lectures/Rotman_Summer_School_2013/thermo_computing_docs/Bennett_1982.pdf#page=20). Proposal: each K or triage rewrite leaves its dropped part wired to the rewrite site, never in a global trace. A residue then has four possible fates: un-copy against a twin (refund), uncompute with its producer (costs time), lend as workspace (free), or erase (heat).

The local uncompute precondition is the reversible pebble rule: build or unbuild a value only while all its direct inputs are present (Kralovic R1/R2, https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1051/ita:2004008.pdf#page=3; analogous to Unqomp's anti-dependency edges and Silq's const). If recomputation is allowed, a COMPLETE BINARY TREE dependency graph of height h needs h+Theta(lg* h) live values. A chain of n steps, which is what a reduction sequence is, needs Theta(lg n) live values, and more than linear time at that space.

Prices for forgetting. You can save kS of space by spending (2^(k+2)-1)S irreversibly erased bits; this is an achievable rate, not proven optimal (Li and Vitanyi, https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/9703022#page=4). Total irreversibility (program bits supplied plus garbage left over) for x -> y is C(x|y)+C(y|x) up to log terms (same paper, #page=16). Within that total, about K(x|y) bits must be erased and K(y|x) bits of program supplied (Bennett, Gacs, Li, Vitanyi, Zurek, 'Information Distance', quote 'a necessary and sufficient number of bits of K(x|y) (the garbage) needs to be irreversibly erased', https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.3520#page=32). This is a formal version of 'entropy relative to what the system knows'.

Add into a cell instead of writing into a blank one. Transparent programs (ri <- ri +/- u*v) cancel the borrowed content by taking differences: r -= r1; P; r += r1; P^-1 (Buhrman et al., https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/22659/22659B.pdf#page=6). The 8-step AND on dirty registers is the smallest example (Mertz, https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/179/download/#page=19). Reversibility alone needs only a family of permutations of a cell indexed by other cells (Buhrman et al. footnote 6, #page=5); the cancellation trick also needs subtraction. Dup is the special case where the target starts blank. Cook and Mertz call this 'clean computation' (https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2023/174/download/#page=5), and Williams builds on their Tree Evaluation algorithm to simulate time t in O(sqrt(t log t)) space (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.17779#page=1).

Two-phase wave with history kept in place: MAJ up the line, UMA back down (Cuccaro, https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0410184#page=2); or compute the majority carries, then reset them while writing the sums (Vedral, Barenco, Ekert, https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/9511018#page=3). This gives (a,b) -> (a,a+b) with nothing left over. Proposal for trees: a zipper walk (one that keeps its return path inside the tree) that parks history in the data on the way down and consumes it into the output on the way up, so Bennett's separate copy stage disappears.

Bijection trick: (x,0) -> (x,f(x)) -> swap -> (0,f(x)), by running the f^-1 circuit backwards (Vedral, Barenco, Ekert, https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/9511018#page=12; Bennett 1973's seven stages, https://www.cs.princeton.edu/courses/archive/fall06/cos576/papers/bennett73.html#Discussion). Injective disp programs with a known inverse run with no residue.

Borrow versus copy. Reuse one after another means borrowing: any idle state, even another computation's leftovers, can serve as dirty workspace if it is returned exactly (Gidney 2017, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.07884#page=1; Haner, Roetteler, Svore, quote 'one can only use toggling of qubits to propagate information', https://arxiv.org/pdf/1611.07995#page=3). Reuse at the same time means copying, at one blank per copy. To reuse a circuit, run it, copy the small result out, then run it back; the circuit is restored for the cost of time plus one result's worth of fuel.

Uncomputing can be cheaper than computing. Computing a temporary AND costs 4 T gates, but uncomputing it by measuring and then fixing up costs 0. Quote: 'This surprising asymmetry is due to the fact that measurement is not reversible' (Gidney 2018, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1709.06648#page=3). A classical analogue on a lattice would be pricing: unbuilding a value its neighbours determine could run energetically downhill, as a refund (this is our proposal).

Parallelism costs clean space. Carry-lookahead adds in O(log n) depth using O(n) ancillae (Draper, Kutin, Rains, Svore, https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0406142#page=1). Draper's Fourier adder needs no temporary carry bits (https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0008033#page=1), but only on a quantum substrate. A ripple adder is serial but needs a single ancilla.

The no-history extreme is a single walker: LMT's Euler tour using two permutations plus a log-sized step counter (Buhrman, Tromp, Vitanyi, https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0101133#page=7). It needs hardly any extra space but exponential time. k levels of checkpoints give the tradeoff S*3^k*2^O(T/2^k) time against O(kS) space (#page=3). The deleted iso.rs token machine is an analogous single walker. Our inference: parallelism needs checkpoints or copies.

Pebbling schedules can be computed rather than hand-written. Meuli et al. 2019 compute reversible pebbling of DAGs under a qubit cap with a SAT solver (quote 'We show how this problem exactly matches the reversible pebbling game', https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.02121#page=1). On the lattice, an energy cost per stored residue might let Metropolis moves find the schedule instead (untested proposal).

field: Quantum and physical substrates: quantum cellular automata (QCA), block-partitioned (Margolus) cellular automata, Feynman's cursor computer and Margolus's parallel version with local clocks, Brownian and enzymatic computers, token-based Brownian circuits, and reversible DNA strand displacement and chemical reaction networks (CRNs). Focus: reversible local dynamics that could really be built, where parallelism comes from, what a clock or cursor does, and how heat, copies and history are paid for.

sources.title: Quantum Mechanical Computers (Feynman 1985, Optics News 11(2))
sources.quote: then sending the data back to the machine in the opposite direction
sources.mechanism: There are two kinds of two-state atoms. Register atoms hold the data. A line of program sites holds a single cursor, an excitation that marks the current step. The Hamiltonian is H = sum_i q*_{i+1} q_i A_{i+1} + its complex conjugate, where A_i is the i-th reversible gate and q_i lowers the cursor at site i. The number of occupied program sites is conserved, and in normal operation exactly one is occupied. If the cursor is found at site k, the register has been multiplied by A_k...A_1, however much it wandered back and forth. Going backward is the conjugate term, i.e. the cursor stepping back. Nothing is logged. To get down to three-atom interactions he switches to two primitives, NOT and SWITCH. The SWITCH term is q*cp + r*c*p + c.c.: a cursor at p goes to q if control atom c = 1, to r if c = 0, and c flips on the way. From these he builds controlled NOT, 'if a then M else N', and sequencing. The garbage clearer uses the same machine M both ways through the switch: copy the input into M with CNOTs, run M, copy the output out, flip a flag f, then go back through M along the switch's other line. That clears the garbage and un-copies the input, and f is reset on the way out. Reusing a subroutine needs flags that record where you are in its cycle, plus where it was called from. Memory addressing uses trees of switches, with a second tree set the opposite way to carry the cursor back out (page 9). Energy: if the cursor scatters with probability p per step, an external force must pull it. The free-energy loss per step is kT * p * (minimum time / time allowed), a formula he credits to Bennett. With p = 0 or unlimited time the loss can be zero.
sources.relevance: The deleted two-way calculus machine (iso.rs Machine: a token walks a laid-out program tree, and going back means turning the token around) is this design. Margolus 1990 states that in Feynman's model only one logic element is active at a time, so a single token is serial by construction. Worth keeping: SWITCH (route a token by a bit and flip the bit) as the local form of triage; the garbage clearer (one circuit run both ways through a flag) as a way to reuse code instead of copying it; and the loss formula as an energy model for the lattice's Metropolis acceptance (the random-move-plus-energy-check step).

sources.title: Parallel Quantum Computation (Margolus 1990)
sources.quote: add a single bit of update-count to each cell, we can run the system asynchronously while retaining a perfectly synchronous causality
sources.mechanism: Start from a 1D block-partitioned cellular automaton: pairs (even, odd) are updated by an invertible rule D_i, then the pairing shifts to (odd, even). Give each cell an update count. Adjacent cells can never get more than one step apart, so only the lowest bit (the 'clock bit') is needed. A pair may update when both cells are at the same step with the pairing that step calls for, and then both counts advance. Under any order of local updates, a cell updated n times holds the state it would have after n synchronous steps, which gives 'hills and valleys of time'. Backward steps are allowed as undoing a forward step. Quantum version: F = sum_i D_i (x) (clock lowering on the pair), H = F + F-dagger. The computation runs at a uniform rate if [F, F-dagger] = 0. On computational configurations that reduces to: is the number of blocks ready to go forward always equal to the number ready to go back? (page 11). Yes for a 1D periodic automaton; no for his earlier 2D model. That 2D model is rescued only by sweeping a 1D active row across it (one dimension of parallelism). Fully parallel quantum computation in more than one dimension is left open. Feynman's serial model is a special case: an alternating clock pattern forms 'a staircase with a landing' (page 12).
sources.relevance: A direct fix for the serial token. Give every site or agent a small phase (clock) bit. An interaction fires only when its participants' phases agree and advances both; the reverse undoes it. Updates can then happen in any order and in parallel, with no log. The forward-ready versus backward-ready count is a candidate diagnostic for the strand lattice, but read it carefully. In Margolus it is the condition for coherent constant-speed quantum motion. Using it for a classical random walk (equal counts means no drift without a bias) is our own analogy, not his claim.

sources.title: Space-Time Circuit-to-Hamiltonian Construction and Its Applications (Breuckmann and Terhal 2014)
sources.quote: the global clock in the Feynman-Kitaev construction gets replaced by a time-configuration
sources.mechanism: Each qubit q has its own clock register t_q in 0..D, where D is the circuit depth; it is a counter, not a bit. A one-qubit gate at depth t contributes -U (x) |t><t-1|_q + h.c. + projectors. A two-qubit gate on q and p contributes -U (x) |t,t><t-1,t-1|_{q,p} + h.c. + projectors, so it acts only when both clocks read t-1 and moves both to t. Invalid time-configurations, where one partner has passed a two-qubit gate and the other has not, are never reached from a synchronised start. Valid ones have every interacting pair spacelike or lightlike separated. The zero-energy state is the history state, a superposition over valid time-configurations. For 1D circuits (with circular time) they lower-bound the spectral gap, and the Hamiltonian dynamics is diffusion of a string around a torus. The construction is inspired by, and related to, a 2D interacting-fermion model of adiabatic computation, and the main uses are QMA-completeness proofs and adiabatic computation.
sources.relevance: Generalises Margolus's clock bits from a regular grid to any circuit graph, which is the right shape for a net whose agents meet pairwise. Each wire or agent carries its own counter, and a two-body rule fires only on matching counters and advances both. The run's 'now' is a front, and the front diffuses. Caveat: the circuit is hard-wired into the Hamiltonian (one term per gate at a fixed depth), while disp's nets rewrite themselves. So this is a model of clocking, not of a self-modifying program.

sources.title: Physics-Like Models of Computation (Margolus 1984)
sources.quote: an invertible mapping could change two copies of this document into one copy, and several sheets of blank paper
sources.mechanism: The grid is split into 2x2 blocks, alternating between two blockings offset by one cell (the Margolus neighbourhood). Each block acts as a 4-in/4-out conservative logic gate. In the billiard-ball automaton (BBMCA) rule, a lone 1 moves to the opposite corner, two 1s on a diagonal turn into the other diagonal (a collision), and every other block is unchanged. The rule is reversible and conserves the number of 1s. Collision sites act as reversible universal gates, and fixed patterns act as mirrors. Page 6: a rule can conserve 1s without being reversible, and for each block you can count how many predecessors the result has, which measures exactly how much information a step loses. On entropy (page 3): a reversible CA only re-encrypts its state, but creatures inside it cannot use correlations spread across many cells, so 'for all practical purposes' entropy rises. It is 'very difficult for a locally invertible evolution to put the redundant pieces back together': one invertible map acting on both copies can un-copy, but two separate maps, one per copy, cannot.
sources.relevance: The repo's 2x2x2 block moves are a 3D Margolus neighbourhood. Being 'physically grounded' then means each block move is a permutation of block states that conserves agents. The two-copies remark gives the locality rule for refunds: an un-copy can only refund once both copies are brought back within reach of one local invertible map. The observer-relative entropy idea matches the user's 'entropy relative to what the system knows'.

sources.title: A thermodynamically reversible generalization of Diffusion Limited Aggregation (D'Souza and Margolus 1999)
sources.quote: Information about exactly when and where a particle undergoes a phase transition is stored in the heat particles
sources.mechanism: Each site holds 7 bits: crystal, 2 gas slots, 2 heat slots, and 2 pseudorandom bits. Diffusion has two parts. Mix: swap a site's two particle slots of a species if its random bit is 1. Transport: slot 1 takes from the neighbour at +k, slot 2 from -k, horizontal on even steps and vertical on odd. The random bit-planes are themselves just shifted each step (fixed co-prime shifts in their runs; to run backward you reverse the shifts), so the random subsystem is invertible and can be run backward on its own. Interaction is checkerboarded (even sites, then odd, with neighbours held fixed). A gas particle aggregates iff it has exactly one crystal neighbour, there is room, and the heat bits can take one unit; it then releases one heat particle. Evaporation is the exact reverse and absorbs a unit of heat. The whole dynamics is invertible: running the inverse rule recovers the initial state, with heat flowing back. Irreversible-looking growth appears because heat diffuses away into an initially empty bath.
sources.relevance: A template for 'erasing makes heat' and for 'history as a physical resource'. An eraser, a K drop or a triage drop becomes a local bijection that emits heat tokens, which then diffuse. It also shows how to make the lattice's random Metropolis proposals reversible: give each site random bits that are shifted rather than drawn, so the whole lattice is a reversible CA coupled to an explicit heat bath.

sources.title: Reversible Quantum Cellular Automata (Schumacher and Werner 2004)
sources.quote: the description we just gave of a circuit with timing constraints is nothing but the definition of a partitioning QCA
sources.mechanism: A QCA is a translation-invariant global step on a quantum lattice that is reversible (has an inverse) and has strictly finite propagation speed. Theorem 6 claims every nearest-neighbour QCA can be represented in a generalised Margolus partitioning scheme. Corollary 7: the inverse of a nearest-neighbour QCA is again nearest-neighbour. That contrasts with classical injective CA, whose inverse can need a much larger neighbourhood. Constructing a QCA from a classical CA needs the classical rule to be locally invertible. Their counterexample, c' = c_{x-1} + c_x + c_{x+1} mod 2, is invertible on rings whose length is not divisible by 3, but it has no inverse CA and so no quantum version. A row of CNOTs with overlapping timing is not reversible even classically ('all 1' and 'all 0' both map to 'all 0'), even though each gate is. Scheduling the gates into two clock cycles where same-cycle gates touch disjoint registers gives a partitioned QCA. So partitioning is a timing discipline. Quantum walks are the one-particle sector of a particle-conserving lattice-gas QCA.
sources.relevance: A test for 'physically grounded': the global step must be a bijection whose inverse is also local. A rule made of block permutations satisfies this automatically, because each block's inverse fits in the same block. The CNOT-row example warns that updates which are each reversible but overlap in time can lose information, so some timing discipline (alternating partitions, or local clock bits as in Margolus 1990) is required.

sources.title: An overview of Quantum Cellular Automata (Arrighi 2019)
sources.quote: it computes the future state of that cell from the local information available
sources.mechanism: Theorem 1 (Arrighi, Nesme, Werner): give every cell a blank spare half-cell. Then any QCA G is simulated by H = (product of S_x)(product of K_x), where S_x swaps the two halves of cell x and K_x = G-dagger S_x G is local to the neighbourhood x + N. Each K_x computes cell x's next state from its neighbourhood and puts it aside in the spare half. The K_x commute with one another, so they can run in any order, and in parallel where they don't overlap. A final swap finishes the step, and the spare half is blank again, so no history is kept. Partitioned QCA (PQCA: one scattering unitary on blocks, alternating partitions) are intrinsically universal, meaning they can simulate any QCA while preserving its space-time layout. In 1D, QCA are exactly translation-invariant two-layer circuits, yet still not exactly PQCA. In 2D they are three-layer circuits (setting translation-invariance aside) and not exactly PQCA. Theorem 1 does not extend to noisy QCA, because there can be no such structure theorem for probabilistic CA. Quantum causal graph dynamics are unitaries over superpositions of graphs whose connections themselves evolve. Section 2.6 notes that Schumacher and Werner's two-layer proof was broken outside 1D.
sources.relevance: (a) 'Compute into a blank, then swap' has the shape of Bennett's compute, copy, uncompute done per cell (K_x = G-dagger S_x G literally runs forward, swaps out, runs back). Its pieces commute, so they need no ordering, and it leaves no history. (b) The probabilistic-CA result is a warning: a local random update rule cannot in general be written as a finite-depth circuit of local random gates. Whether that bites a Metropolis lattice is our inference; making the randomness explicit lattice state, as D'Souza and Margolus do, sidesteps the question. (c) Causal graph dynamics is the relevant theory for rewriting nets whose connections change.

sources.title: The thermodynamics of computation, a review (Bennett 1982)
sources.quote: the merging of two trajectories into one cannot be brought about by conservative forces
sources.mechanism: A Brownian computer random-walks along its computation graph, driven by a weak bias of epsilon per step. The forward/backward ratio is e^(epsilon/kT), the net speed is proportional to epsilon for small epsilon, and the dissipation is epsilon per net step. RNA polymerase is a Brownian tape copier: it takes in a nucleoside triphosphate, releases pyrophosphate, and shifts one notch, and the reaction also runs backward. With 10% excess triphosphates it makes 11 forward steps per 10 back at kT ln(11/10), about 0.1 kT, per net step, and the back steps are not errors. His hypothetical enzymatic Turing machine (page 11): the tape is a macromolecule with a chemical group marking the head. There is one enzyme per transition rule; each binds the groups to be removed, brings the groups to add, drops off and is reused. Each enzyme is coupled at some point in its cycle to ATP to ADP, giving an adjustable drive. Merges (erasure, overwriting, program points reachable from several places) create extraneous predecessor states. Ballistic computers cannot tolerate any. A Brownian computer tolerates a slightly branched graph with an arbitrarily small drive, but runs slower; e.g. randomly undoing a reassignment usually leads to a 'garden-of-Eden' state with no predecessor. Exponentially branching backward trees need a finite drive: about kT ln 2 per bit thrown away, or about kT times the log of the mean number of immediate predecessors per step. Otherwise the computation is greatly slowed, or for infinite trees wanders off never to return. A history tape plus cleanup (compute, copy the output, uncompute) gives a reversible computation that keeps only input and output.
sources.relevance: The user's 'matter plus mediators' picture is Bennett's enzymatic computer: an information polymer as matter, one reusable enzyme per rule as mediator, and fuel coupling as drive. Energy rule for the lattice: each net forward step costs epsilon. A few merges (K dropping z, triage dropping two arms, an eraser) are tolerable at tiny drive. Merges that compound into exponential backward branching need about kT ln(mean predecessors) per step, or the walk gets lost in extraneous branches.

sources.title: Computation time and thermodynamic uncertainty relation of Brownian circuits (Utsumi, Ito, Golubev and Peper 2022)
sources.quote: The CJoin is the only circuit element producing environment entropy
sources.mechanism: Token-based Brownian circuits (Peper, Lee and coworkers). Tokens are Brownian particles moved by thermal fluctuations. A Boolean value is encoded by which of two wires holds the token (dual-rail). There are three primitives. Hub: a three-wire junction where a token can take either branch at rate Gamma or come back along its track. Ratchet: a one-way 'diode' used for readout, i.e. detecting a token. Conservative Join (CJoin): if one token enters on the left and one on the right, one leaves at the top and one at the bottom, at forward rate gamma+ and backward rate gamma-. The CJoin synchronises through two-token scattering and is the only element producing environment entropy; setting gamma+ > gamma- pushes the computation. The Ratchet changes system entropy, and that measurement cost is not counted as environment entropy. The circuits are proven universal provided stochastic backtracking is not disabled. The paper models them as stochastic Petri nets and relates computation time to entropy production. Single-electron implementations of the primitives have been proposed, and a skyrmion Hub has been demonstrated experimentally.
sources.relevance: The closest physical analogue to the strand lattice's random moves and to the deleted split/join token machine. Design rule: moving along a wire or through a junction is unbiased diffusion and produces no environment entropy; the only biased, entropy-producing move is the two-body meeting, i.e. the active-pair interaction. Their universality proof relies on backtracking, so in a noise-driven system stepping backward is part of how computation works, not just a feature.

sources.title: Efficient Turing-Universal Computation with DNA Polymers (Qian, Soloveichik and Winfree 2011)
sources.quote: brings the chemical system into the same exact physical state as it was in the beginning, including recovery of fuel reagents and any energy used
sources.mechanism: A formal reaction X + Y -> A + B is built from a cascade of strand-displacement steps through fuel complexes F1..F6 held at high concentration. The irreversible version has a final irreversible step. In the reversible version that step is removed, and the forward product becomes the first fuel of the backward reaction. If only X is present, X binds F1 and the backward step releases it unchanged. They describe this as 'reversible exploration to determine whether a subsequent step is possible'. Bias is per reaction: more F1 speeds the forward reaction, more F6 the backward, and equilibrium fuel concentrations give no bias. Signals are 'history-free': a signal strand carries no domain recording which reaction made it, so a reverse reaction can take up any copy of the species. A polymer reaction pushes or pops a monomer at the end of a DNA polymer. A geometry-free CRN controlling two polymer stacks gives a Turing-universal stack machine. Bennett's logically reversible Turing machine runs with physically reversible reactions. Energy per step is kT ln m, with m the mean number of immediate predecessors, so it is 0 for reversible machines. Each signal species is typically present as a single copy.
sources.relevance: The 'copy draws fuel, un-copy refunds' accounting exists concretely here: run the reactions backward and the fuel comes back, with a per-rule fuel concentration as the bias knob. Tentative reversible binding that undoes itself when the partner is absent is what a random local proposal on the lattice should be. And a value should look the same whatever produced it, so that un-making it does not depend on where it came from.

sources.title: Space and energy efficient computation with DNA strand displacement systems (Thachuk and Condon 2012)
sources.quote: the same gate can only be used next to consume a B signal, produce an A signal, and reset itself to the forward orientation
sources.mechanism: Tagged CRN: each reaction uses a gate that reverses orientation when used, so a used gate can next only run the reaction backward, which resets it. Space is the most free signals present at once plus the number of gates. To implement it in strand displacement, a single-copy 'mutex' species makes each cascade a transaction: it either completes or returns to its prior state, and the mutex is held during the cascade so no other reaction can start. Post-order traversal of a perfect binary tree of height h: recursively traverse the left subtree, mark the left child, reverse all the steps of that traversal, move to the right child, traverse it, and mark it. That takes Theta(3^h) reaction steps and Theta(h) space and is logically reversible (Lemma 3, page 7). Combined with reversible clause checking, it decides quantified 3-SAT, so any PSPACE problem can be solved by a logically reversible CRN in polynomial space. They also show that reachability in CRNs and strand displacement systems is PSPACE-hard.
sources.relevance: Two ideas. (a) An element that flips after use is its own history: no log is needed, and it becomes reusable after being run backward ('reuse circuits, and the history is part of the circuit'). (b) The reversible way to evaluate a tree: compute a subtree, store its result in the parent, uncompute the subtree. That trades time (3^h) for space (h) and fits disp's tree evaluation. Warning: their atomicity comes from one global single-copy mutex, which serialises everything. Disp should get atomicity from block-local moves instead.

sources.title: Fundamental costs in the production and destruction of persistent polymer copies (Ouldridge and ten Wolde 2017)
sources.quote: Once mixed, however, templates cannot be matched to copies a priori, and correlations cannot be leveraged
sources.mechanism: A copy B is grown on a template A and then separated. The minimum (reversible) work is <w>_rev = F_B[p_f] - F_B[p_0] - T H_f(B) + kT I_f(A;B) (page 2). Compared with the cheapest template-independent output, a template-specific copy costs extra work made of three terms: a bond-energy difference, a sequence-entropy difference, and kT I(A;B). The first two can be of either sign, but kT I and the total are non-negative. The extra is stored as free energy, not dissipated. Even if copying is reversible, the parent can recover these resources only by reversing the copy, which destroys the offspring. Once copies from many templates are mixed, templates can't be matched to copies and the correlations can't be exploited. If the mixing happens irreversibly, the entropy of the universe rises by k I(A;B). Template-free (non-specific) breakdown of polymers generates entropy of about kT M N ln m - kT M H[p_z(b)], where m is the number of monomer types. So it is cheap when the polymers come from a broad (high-entropy) distribution and expensive for accurate copies of a few templates. That generalises Bennett's kT ln m per monomer.
sources.relevance: The physics behind 'copy draws fuel, un-copy refunds, erasing unique info makes heat, entropy relative to what the system knows'. An accurate duplicator copy stores correlation free energy (kT * I(original; copy) is part of its extra cost). That can be refunded only by reversing the copy against its own original while the two can still be matched, for example while still joined by a wire or sharing the label the repo's labelled duplicators carry. Breaking one copy down blindly instead dissipates up to about kT ln m per symbol (kT ln 2 per bit), less if the copies were not well correlated with any known source.

key_ideas: Per-agent clocks instead of a walking token. A single cursor is the serial special case ('a staircase with a landing'). Give each site or agent a small phase: a 1-bit clock on a regular grid, or a counter per wire on an arbitrary circuit. A two-body rule fires only when the participants' phases match and advances both; the reverse undoes it. The result is parallel and order-free, needs no log, and the run's 'present' is a front that diffuses. Sources: Margolus 1990 (https://people.csail.mit.edu/nhm/pqc.pdf#page=9) and Breuckmann and Terhal 2014 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.6101#page=5). Caveat: in Breuckmann and Terhal the circuit is hard-wired into the Hamiltonian, unlike a self-rewriting net.

Forward-ready versus backward-ready count. In Margolus's quantum model, the computation runs at a uniform coherent speed when the number of blocks ready to step forward always equals the number ready to step back. This holds in 1D rings and fails for his 2D model, and fully parallel 2D/3D is left open. For a classical random-walk lattice the analogous (our own, not Margolus's) reading is: equal counts mean no entropic drift, so net progress must come from an explicit bias. Measuring these counts on the strand lattice would show whether a run is computing or just diffusing. Source: Margolus 1990 (https://people.csail.mit.edu/nhm/pqc.pdf#page=11).

Every rule a block permutation. Each 2x2x2 move should be a bijection on block states that conserves agents. Its inverse then automatically fits in the same block, which is a concrete meaning of 'physically grounded' (a step with a local inverse). Overlapping updates that are each reversible can still lose information without a timing discipline (alternating partitions or local clocks). Caveat: Schumacher and Werner's claim that every nearest-neighbour QCA is a two-layer block circuit holds only in 1D, according to Arrighi. Sources: Schumacher and Werner 2004 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0405174#page=7), Margolus 1984 (https://people.csail.mit.edu/nhm/bbmca-physica.pdf#page=6), Arrighi 2019 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.12956#page=5).

Heat as lattice particles, and history held in the heat. An erasure, a K drop or a triage drop becomes a local bijection that emits heat tokens, which then diffuse; running the inverse rule brings the heat back and undoes it. Randomness should be bit-planes that are shifted rather than drawn, so the Metropolis-style lattice stays a reversible CA with an explicit heat bath. Source: D'Souza and Margolus 1999 (https://people.csail.mit.edu/nhm/ra.pdf#page=3).

Brownian energy accounting. With a bias of epsilon per step, net speed is proportional to epsilon and dissipation is epsilon per net step. Moving through wires and junctions is unbiased and produces no environment entropy; in Brownian circuits only the two-token join does (readout is costed separately). A few merges (K dropping z, triage dropping two arms, an eraser) are tolerable at tiny drive. Merges that compound into exponential backward branching need about kT ln(mean predecessors) per step, about kT ln 2 per bit thrown away, or the walk gets lost in extraneous branches. Feynman's version for a scattered cursor: loss per step = kT * p * (minimum time / time allowed). Sources: Bennett 1982 (https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/863.18/notes/computation/Bennett-1982.pdf#page=18), Utsumi et al. 2022 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.10735#page=9), Feynman 1985 (https://opn-web-afd-d3bfbkd5bcc5asbs.z02.azurefd.net/opn/media/images/pdfs/11557/11557_23417_110730.pdf#page=8).

Un-copy refunds only when both copies meet. An accurate copy stores correlation free energy (kT * I(original; copy) is part of its extra cost over a random product). That is refundable only by an invertible move acting on both copies together, i.e. reversing the copy against its original. Once copies are mixed or can't be matched, the correlation is unusable, and irreversible mixing generates k * I of entropy. A wire or label tying twins together is what keeps the refund available. Sources: Margolus 1984 (https://people.csail.mit.edu/nhm/bbmca-physica.pdf#page=3) and Ouldridge and ten Wolde 2017 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.05554#page=2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.05554#page=3).

Reuse circuits by running them backward instead of copying them. Feynman's garbage clearer runs one machine both ways through a switch and a flag, and subroutine reuse needs flags marking the position in the cycle and the caller. Thachuk and Condon's gates flip orientation when used, so a used gate is its own history and is reset by running backward. Sources: Feynman 1985 (https://opn-web-afd-d3bfbkd5bcc5asbs.z02.azurefd.net/opn/media/images/pdfs/11557/11557_23417_110730.pdf#page=8) and Thachuk and Condon 2012 (https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~condon/papers/dna-pspace.pdf#page=3).

Reversible tree evaluation. Post-order: compute a subtree, mark the result in the parent, uncompute the subtree, then go right. That costs Theta(3^h) time and Theta(h) space with no garbage. Feynman's trees of switches route a token into a memory tree, and a second, opposite tree brings it back out. Sources: Thachuk and Condon 2012 (https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~condon/papers/dna-pspace.pdf#page=7) and Feynman 1985 (https://opn-web-afd-d3bfbkd5bcc5asbs.z02.azurefd.net/opn/media/images/pdfs/11557/11557_23417_110730.pdf#page=9).

Compute into a blank, then swap. Each cell's update K_x = G-dagger S_x G computes its next state into a spare half-cell, using only its neighbourhood. The K_x commute, so they run in any order and in parallel where they don't overlap, and a final swap finishes the step. This has the shape of Bennett's compute, copy, uncompute done per cell, and the spare half is blank again afterwards, so no history is kept. Source: Arrighi 2019 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.12956#page=5).

Matter plus mediators is Bennett's enzymatic computer. The tape (matter) is changed by reusable enzymes, one per rule (mediators), driven by fuel coupling. A proposal is a tentative, reversible binding that undoes itself if the precondition fails, and each rule's bias is a fuel concentration. Values should be history-free, looking the same whatever produced them. Sources: Bennett 1982 (https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/863.18/notes/computation/Bennett-1982.pdf#page=11) and Qian, Soloveichik and Winfree 2011 (https://www.dna.caltech.edu/Papers/DNA_stack_machines2011_LNCS.pdf#page=7).

Recycling and parallel copies are in tension. A recycling n-bit counter whose waste is polynomial in n (i.e. polylogarithmic in its 2^n-step run) fails when Theta(n) copies of its starting species are present, and such low-waste schemes are impossible with polynomially many copies. If disp gets parallelism by self-reproduction and also wants circuit reuse, something must keep each reused part tied to its own copy, such as spatial position or tethers. Source: Condon, Hu, Manuch and Thachuk 2012 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443/articles/PMC3363036/#s1b); spot-checked here against its abstract, not fully verified.

Asynchronous reversible gates have been designed for real hardware. In a superconducting gate, simulated but not yet built, a stored flux bit elastically swaps with a moving bit, and inputs may arrive at any time as long as their order is kept. That is a concrete design for 'a gate that holds its own history and moves things around'. Source: Osborn and Wustmann 2023 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2201.12999#page=1); spot-checked here.

Lattice CRNs with local synchronisation. A surface CRN is an asynchronous stochastic CA with rules A -> B and A + B -> C + D between neighbouring sites. Local clock-tick or synchronisation-gate schemes keep a cell from ever getting more than one tick ahead of its neighbours. This is the same idea as Margolus's clock bits, in a form proposed for DNA. Their rules are not required to be reversible. Source: Clamons, Qian and Winfree 2020 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov:443/articles/PMC7276541/#RSIF20190790BX4); spot-checked here.

Contrasts worth knowing. Global resonant pulses make a whole array apply a CA rule in parallel with no local addressing, but the sequencing is central (Lloyd 1993, https://fab.cba.mit.edu/classes/862.22/notes/computation/Lloyd-1993.pdf#page=1). Data can also walk through a fixed landscape of interactions, with gates built so the result does not depend on walk timing (Janzing 2007, https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/0506270#page=1). Both put the program in the substrate rather than in the matter, the opposite of disp's code-as-trees. Both spot-checked here.

field: Reversible rewriting and abstract machines: token machines from the geometry of interaction (GoI, the semantics in which a program is a fixed graph and running it means sending a token along paths through it), hardware compilation that reuses circuits instead of copying them (Geometry of Synthesis), the dynamic GoI machine mixing tokens with rewriting, Lamping-style sharing graphs, reversible term rewriting and reversible (DPO / space-time) graph rewriting. Focus: reusing code (read without being consumed) versus copying it, and what each costs in locality and parallelism.

sources.title: Reversible, irreversible and optimal lambda-machines (Danos, Regnier 1999)
sources.quote: The amount of information needed to keep the machine running, which is but the word, will sometimes grow and sometimes shrink
sources.mechanism: Compares machines for linear head reduction. The KAM (Krivine's environment machine) keeps closures. Implementations share the environment by pointer, so in the 'jump' (value retrieval) step the discarded part of the environment cannot be freed; information grows steadily and an external garbage collector is needed (same for the PAM, the pointer abstract machine). The IAM (interaction abstract machine) presents the term as a bi-deterministic automaton (a proof net that never changes). A token walks it carrying a pair of stacks: B, the 'boxes stack', and S, the 'balancing stack'; stacks hold multiplicative constants P/Q and exponential signatures (binary trees saying which virtual copy of a duplicable subterm is meant). Bi-deterministic means: given a word and a node, at most one transition applies and at most one could have produced it, so the machine is reversible; the word grows and shrinks and needs no garbage collection. Code is never copied: 'which copy' is a signature on the token. The JAM (jumping abstract machine) shortcuts the IAM's redundant backtracking steps; specialized to lambda-terms it is isomorphic to the KAM under the translation D = !D -o !D and to the PAM under D = !D -o D.
sources.relevance: This is the 'reader that does not consume' that research/REVERSIBLE_PIPELINE.md (line 59) says Bennett's copy step needs. Unlike the removed iso.rs walker (which parked its context in the code tree, so a second reader needed its own copy of the code), the IAM keeps code untouched and puts all context on the token, so many tokens can read one copy. A disp core could keep code as static wiring and move tokens whose stacks are short strand chains.

sources.title: A Structural Approach to Reversible Computation (Abramsky 2005)
sources.quote: using the copy-tag field of !b to split its address space into two
sources.mechanism: Model: biorthogonal pattern-matching automata, rules (q,r)->(s,q') where both the rule set and its converse are orthogonal (non-ambiguous, left-linear), so computation is deterministic and reversible step by step; every variable occurs exactly once on each side, so nothing is duplicated or discarded. Terms over Σ0={ε}, Σ1={l,r}, Σ2={p}. Combinators are partial involutions: I: l(x)<->r(x); K: l(x)<->r(r(x)) ('the second argument does not get accessed'); D: l(p(ε,x))<->r(x); W (W·a·!b = a·!b·!b): r(r(x))<->l(r(r(x))) plus l(l(p(x,y)))<->r(l(p(l(x),y))) and l(r(l(p(x,y))))<->r(l(p(r(x),y))), splitting the copy tag of !b into l/r instead of copying. Replication !f = {(p(t,u),p(t,v)) | (u,v) in f}. LApp(f,g) = frr ∪ frl;g;(fll;g)*;flr, a feedback loop. B,C,K,D,δ,F,W form an affine combinatory algebra; combinatory completeness gives universality, and termination is Σ01-complete. Finitely describable partial involutions are not closed under linear application (Prop 8.1).
sources.relevance: Closest match to reversible + linear + history-free + universal at once. K erases nothing (its second argument is simply never queried), and W's copy is an l/r split of the asker's address. A disp core could compile △-application into fixed combinator wiring with tokens as the only moving matter; the catch is that triage inspects data shape, so data must answer queries as a process.

sources.title: Geometry of Synthesis IV: Compiling Affine Recursion into Static Hardware (Ghica, Smith, Singh 2011)
sources.quote: storing the source of the signal in a set-reset register
sources.mechanism: SCI (Syntactic Control of Interference, an affine version of Reynolds's Idealized Algol) compiles to static circuits via its game/GoI model. Contraction (identifier reuse) is allowed in product formation but not in function application or parallel execution. Sharing in a product uses a 'diagonal' circuit, behaviourally a stateful multiplexer-demultiplexer: it routes a request from either user to the shared interface, records which side asked in a set-reset register, and routes the answer back by that bit; the semantic model guarantees every output on the shared interface is followed by the matching input. Recursion 'in space' unfolds at compile time. Recursion 'in time' folds all instances into one: registers become indexed registers selected by an up/down counter (the 'virtual' instance), raised on each recursive call and lowered on each return; overflow raises an error signal, and the recursive call must not occur in a concurrent context. The compiler decides per function whether the circuit 'must be reinstantiated or can be reused', trading area/power against latency/throughput (p.2).
sources.relevance: Gives a concrete mux agent as the cheap alternative to the Dn duplicator: two clients, one shared subtree, one bit saying who asked, cleared when the answer passes back. It serializes; copying buys parallelism. The reuse-or-reinstantiate choice could be made by energy at run time instead of at compile time.

sources.title: The Dynamic Geometry of Interaction Machine: A Token-Guided Graph Rewriter (Muroya, Ghica 2019)
sources.quote: keeps the underlying graph fixed and uses the data stored in the token to route it
sources.mechanism: Graphs are proof-net-like (λ, @, !, ?, D, Cn contraction, ...). Token data (d, f, S, B): direction, rewrite flag f ∈ {□, λ, !}, computation stack S, box stack B. Pass transitions move the token over one node; passing a Cn node pushes the old position onto B. When the token reaches λ with @ on top of S it raises flag λ, and a β rewrite removes the λ/@ pair at constant cost. Flag ! triggers on-demand copying of a !-box (cost bounded by the box's size); one copy is rewritten further while the original is kept. 'Passes-only' never rewrites (an ordinary token machine, call-by-name, recomputes arguments); 'rewrites-first' gives call-by-need and both call-by-value orders, differing only in when the cache is created. Rewriting trades space for time.
sources.relevance: The cleanest framework for 'walk shared code until it is worth copying, then copy it'. For disp, the rewrite flag would become local agents, the box copy would be Dn's layer-at-a-time copy, and the dial could be set by energy instead of a fixed strategy.

sources.title: The Geometry of Synchronization (Dal Lago, Faggian, Hasuo, Yoshimizu 2014)
sources.quote: multiple tokens could travel the net in parallel, but what we compute is exactly the same, because the tokens do not interact
sources.mechanism: SMLL: multiplicative linear logic plus units and n-ary 'sync links'. The SIAM is a multi-token interaction machine: tokens cross a sync link only when each of its in-edges is saturated, and all cross simultaneously; a one-link can start a new token; tokens enter a ⊥-box only once it is unlocked. Correctness is an adaptation of the Danos–Regnier criterion (no switching cycle). The SIAM is shown sound for cut elimination, and deadlock freedom follows. IAMs in general are described as bi-deterministic. Used to interpret a quantum λ-calculus, where CNOT needs two tokens to synchronize.
sources.relevance: In a reuse machine, parallelism means many tokens on one shared code, and interaction between them is a local join node, like the strand lattice's pairwise interactions.

sources.title: On Jumps, Interactions, and Intersection Types (Catozi, Dal Lago, Vanoni 2026)
sources.quote: the possibility to jump from one subterm to another, thus losing locality and reversibility
sources.mechanism: PaJAM states are (t, C, L, T, d, k): subterm, context, log, tape, direction, and a backtracking-depth budget k. The IAM finds an argument by nested backtracking; the JAM jumps using logged positions. In the PaJAM, entering a backtracking phase (bt1) decrements k and leaving it (bt2) increments k; at k=0 bt1 is replaced by a jump. k=0 is the JAM, k=∞ behaves as the IAM. The machine is stated to be deterministic but not reversible. For every finite k the run length is polynomial in the number n of weak head β steps (O(n^(6k+5))), the degree growing with k. Background (Accattoli, Dal Lago, Vanoni 2021, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.12988#page=2, re-verified): t1 := I, tn+1 := tn I takes time exponential in n 'to be evaluated by the IAM, but only linear time in any environment machine'.
sources.relevance: Puts a number on the price of reuse by re-walking (exponential at worst) and names the fix, a saved pointer, at the cost of locality and reversibility. On a lattice the pointer could be a physical strand left behind and retracted (open design).

sources.title: PELCR: Parallel Environment for Optimal Lambda-Calculus Reduction (Pedicini, Quaglia 2004)
sources.quote: The one and only reduction rule is the composition of two edges in the graph
sources.mechanism: Builds on Danos–Regnier virtual reduction (VR), a local and asynchronous way to compute Girard's execution formula over a graph weighted in the dynamic algebra. When two edges are composable (product of weights nonzero), VR derives a new edge and the original edges are 'marked by the rest of the composition' (a bracketed filter recording what they already composed with). Directed VR (DVR) instead creates a new node and two new edges (called the residuals) with weights from the stable form of b*a. The half combustion strategy marks each edge incoming or combusted, so filters need not be kept; an on-the-fly storage-recovery scheme deletes nodes that reach valence zero and cannot reach the result. With message aggregation and dynamic load balancing over MPI, it reaches up to 70/80% of ideal speedup.
sources.relevance: An existence proof that a GoI-style, path-based evaluator can be local, asynchronous and parallel with essentially one rule; composing edges without consuming them is 'read without consuming' at the level of wires.

sources.title: About the efficient reduction of lambda terms (Asperti 2017)
sources.quote: different levels of sharing, and the introduction of suitable operators acting as brackets in the graph to delimit the scope of duplicators
sources.mechanism: A short survey by a BOHM (Bologna Optimal Higher-order Machine) author. Lamping-style sharing graphs perform the minimum amount of duplication; the hard part is to 'duplicate the abstraction node without jointly duplicating the whole body' (p.2). Beyond duplication there is 'bookkeeping' to enforce correct matching between sharing and unsharing, done with levels of sharing and bracket operators that change duplicators' levels. Careless bracket management accumulates exponentially (Asperti–Chroboczek), e.g. in Gonthier's implementations; the polynomial cost of bookkeeping is only conjectured. Terms typable in elementary linear logic need no brackets, and the non-elementary worst case of optimal reduction comes from duplication itself, not bookkeeping.
sources.relevance: disp's Dn already copies a layer at a time. Lamping's missing piece is levels, which enforce correct sharing/unsharing matching; stratified (ELL-like) code would need no brackets.

sources.title: Reversible Computation in Term Rewriting (Nishida, Palacios, Vidal 2018)
sources.quote: a substitution with Dom(σ) = Var(l)\Var(r) which will record the bindings of erased variables
sources.mechanism: A Landauer embedding for term rewriting: rewriting on pairs <t, π> with π a list of trace terms β(p, σ) (rule label, position, bindings of erased variables only; σ = id for non-erasing rules); the backward relation uses them to undo steps. To drop positions, systems are flattened into pure constructor conditional systems (pcDCTRS: basic left-hand sides, constructor right-hand sides) where reductions happen at the top. Injectivization rewrites each rule to f^i(s) -> <r, β(y, w)>, returning the trace beside the result with subcall traces nested; inversion gives the backward functions. The paper notes injective functions may allow dropping rule labels and non-erasing rules dropping σ.
sources.relevance: Tree calculus as a TRS: K erases z, S erases nothing, triage erases the untaken arms (and the rule label records which arm fired). That is the formal backing for iso.rs's trace, and injectivization is the move from a log bolted on to history returned as a value.

sources.title: A Reversible Crumbling Abstract Machine for Plotkin's Call-by-Value (Pizzo, Sacerdoti Coen 2026)
sources.quote: exhibits a particularly compact Landauer's embedding, requiring only constant space overhead for each step
sources.mechanism: A naive Landauer embedding of weak call-by-value must store the redex position plus enough to rebuild it (to recover (λx.y)M from y you need all of M), linear per step. Explicit substitutions remove the argument cost but the position is still linear. 'Finest crumbling' allows explicit substitutions only of applications of a variable to a variable or of λ-abstractions, with results assigned to a special variable *, so terms become environments. The resulting RCAM is bilinear in time and needs only O(1) extra space per machine step to be reversible. Applying an abstraction still copies (α-renames) its body.
sources.relevance: Independent confirmation that once arguments are shared by name, the trace drops to a constant per step. On the lattice, names become wires and position becomes where the record sits.

sources.title: Fundamentals of Compositional Rewriting Theory (Behr, Harmer, Krivine 2023)
sources.quote: An interesting consequence of the definition of DPO semantics is that rule applications are always reversible
sources.mechanism: In double-pushout (DPO) rewriting both squares are pushouts, so rule applications are always reversible; the no-dangling condition stops a rule from applying when it would otherwise be irreversible (deleting a node with incident edges outside the match). Under sesqui-pushout (SqPO) such a deletion always applies and silently drops the incident edges, and a rule that merges nodes generally loses which edges belonged to which. For non-input-linear (non-monic) rules the pushout complement need not be unique, so several candidate rewrites exist.
