Measurement: CNOT copy of S into a blank symmetric D has minimal work and heat 'both zero' (Eqs. 107-108, p.27). Feedback using a correlated D can reset S or extract up to kT I (p.28-29). Logical reversibility depends on where the boundary between logical and environmental degrees of freedom is drawn; thermodynamic reversibility does not (p.13, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.1886#page=13).
sources.relevance: A K or triage drop is not dissipation in itself: its minimum heat is the logical entropy that disappears, and that can be paid reversibly if the protocol matches the arm's distribution. On a bijective lattice, 'heat' can be modelled as moving bits into an explicit environment region. Copy into a blank and reset against a twin both have zero minimal information cost; only speed costs.

sources.title: Dependence of dissipation on the initial distribution over states
sources.quote: specifies a logically-reversible map from x0 to x1 (i.e., a permutation over X), then incorrect prior dissipation is 0
sources.mechanism: For a fixed process implementing p(x1|x0), with prior q0 being the input distribution that minimizes dissipation (assumed full support), running it on r0 adds dissipation D(r0||q0) - D(r1||q1) (Eq. 10). This equals D(r(X0|X1)||q(X0|X1)), the KL divergence between Bayesian posteriors over the input given the output (p.5). It is zero for permutations and reaches its maximum D(r0||q0) for input-independent maps such as erasure. It depends only on the map and q0, not on the physical details (p.5). It does not assume local detailed balance (p.2), and it carries over to coarse-grained computational macrostates (p.1). The result is about whole-system distributions; a subsystem version needs the later solitary-process framework (Wolpert 2019, Ouldridge-Wolpert 2023).
sources.relevance: Each rule is a fixed device with a built-in prior. Averaged over firings, Landauer cost plus mismatch cost equals E[-ln q(z | output)], i.e. the cross-entropy of the dropped information given what remains. So 'charge the surprisal under the rule's own prior' is exact on average. Ouldridge-Wolpert 2023 Eq. 16 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.06895#page=7) gives the same number, -ln q(z|island), for a single deterministic input. Any rule that is a permutation of block states has zero mismatch.

sources.title: The stochastic thermodynamics of computation
sources.quote: each iteration will contribute a strictly positive mismatch cost in general, without cancellation of terms
sources.mechanism: EP splits into Landauer cost, mismatch cost (summed over islands) and residual EP. For a device run K times with the same prior, Landauer costs telescope, but residual EP and mismatch cost are 'strictly positive in general' every iteration unless the prior is updated (p.46). If an offboard copy of the input persists until the input is reset, that reset's Landauer cost can be zero and mismatch cost is zero, but 'there will invariably be entropic costs involved in making the offboard copy of the input in the first place' (p.47, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.05669#page=47). Wires have zero Landauer and mismatch cost, so all their cost is residual EP (p.37, p.65). On reversible circuits (Section XI, pp.71-74): the extended (Bennett-style) circuit leaves f(x_IN) plus a copy of x_IN, and that copy still has to be reinitialized. Fairly compared, its answer-reinitialization costs are generally greater than those of the all-at-once device. 'as soon as you try to use the system more than once, to complete a full cycle, the miracle vaporizes' (p.71).
sources.relevance: A fixed rule table applied at every site and clock is the periodic case. Mismatch does not telescope, so many-to-one firings pay mismatch whenever the actual distribution differs from the rule's prior, which is generically the case. A record kept next to what it describes zeroes the cost of resetting that thing later, but making the record has its own cost. Bennett's run-copy-run-back does not make computation free over a full cycle, because the kept input copy must eventually be reset too.

sources.title: Thermodynamics of computing with circuits
sources.quote: we should choose the wiring diagram for which the parents of each gate are as strongly correlated among themselves as possible
sources.mechanism: Each gate runs as a solitary process, with only the gate and its inputs coupled. Circuit Landauer loss (minimum extra heat compared with one all-at-once device) is L_loss = I(p_IN) - I(p_OUT) - sum over non-wire gates g of I(p_pa(g)), where I is multi-information (Corollary 4, p.14). Two erasers on correlated inputs, each reversible alone, are not reversible when run in parallel (p.1). The bound on Landauer loss holds only for out-degree 1. Proposition 1 (p.15, proof p.25, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.04103#page=25) builds the counterexample by fanning out a copy of an input v to a separate erasure gate, which adds S(p_v) to the loss; iterating makes the loss arbitrarily large. As a simple model, wire residual EP can be taken proportional to wire length (p.14).
sources.relevance: The proof of Proposition 1 is literally 'fan out a copy, then erase it with a separate gate': each such copy adds its full entropy to the loss. That is the S-rule or duplicator copy later dropped by an independent K eraser. Design rule: erase correlated things together, i.e. un-copy at the sharing node rather than erase the copy leaf by leaf. Strand-lattice wire tension corresponds to the wire residual-EP model.

sources.title: Thermodynamics of modularity: structural costs beyond the Landauer bound
sources.quote: the minimum irretrievable modularity dissipation over the duration of an operation due to the locality of control is proportional to the reduction in mutual information
sources.mechanism: Split the state into the controlled part Z^i and the frozen rest Z^s. The local minimum work is kT ln2 (H[Z^i_t] - H[Z^i_t+tau]). The modularity dissipation is Sigma_mod / (k ln2) = I[Z^i_t; Z^s] - I[Z^i_t+tau; Z^s] (Eq. 5, p.4), which equals a conditional mutual information because Z^i_t+tau depends only on Z^i_t. The derivation assumes all informational states have equal internal free energies (p.2). For information ratchets, the dissipation is minimized when hidden states are predictive of the input (work extraction) or retrodictive of the output (pattern generation) (p.1, p.3). The cure is 'designing internal ratchet states that capture the global correlations' (p.1).
sources.relevance: Gives the exact extra heat per local firing: the information the block shared with the outside that its update destroyed. It is zero for a bijective block update. For a drop of z it is roughly the correlation z had with the rest of the lattice: zero for fresh randomness, and all of H(z) if z is a copy whose twin is alive elsewhere. This is an ensemble quantity. Counting drops with a living twin is a reasonable per-run proxy, not the quantity itself.

sources.title: Thermodynamics of deterministic finite automata operating locally and periodically
sources.quote: One is if all islands have a single element, i.e., the local update function ρ is invertible
sources.mechanism: Each update is a solitary process on the local state (automaton state plus current symbol), using the same protocol every iteration. EP is bounded below by marginal mismatch plus modularity cost per step. That bound is positive whenever an island with nonzero probability has two or more reachable elements. It is avoided only if (a) the local update rho is invertible, or (b) the input distribution makes each island effectively single-element, which needs a finely tuned prior that 'risks high costs for overconfidence' (p.8). A uniform prior q = 1/L_c within each island minimizes the worst-case EP. For a deterministic input, per-step EP is -ln q(z|c) >= ln L_cmax (Eqs. 15-16, p.7, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.06895#page=7). The DFA's whole run (input word plus start state to input word plus end state) is always invertible, yet 'The logical properties of the overall computation are therefore not helpful in understanding the necessary EP of a local, periodic device' (p.9). Regular languages split into ones recognisable at zero EP and ones that necessarily cost EP (p.1). The authors expect variants for push-down automata, RAM machines and Turing machines, but warn that overwriting input or memory will affect the modularity cost in ways not covered (p.10).
sources.relevance: The key theorem for a reversible lattice. If every block move is a bijection of block states, locality and periodicity cost nothing. Global invertibility (a far-away trace, or the preserved input word in the DFA case) does not rescue a non-invertible local step. Eq. 16 gives a per-instance -ln q(z|island) charge for many-to-one moves, and uniform priors bound the worst case at ln(largest island). The authors flag lattice-style overwriting of memory as not covered.

sources.title: Work and information processing in a solvable model of Maxwell's demon
sources.quote: it consumes one resource – a blank or partially blank memory register – to build up another
sources.mechanism: A 3-state demon (A, B, C) is coupled to one bit at a time: 6 joint states. The edges A0-B0, B0-C0, A1-B1 and B1-C1 do not involve the bit, and one coupled edge C0-A1 means the demon goes C->A only while flipping the bit 0->1 (and back). The mass is lifted on each C->A transition. The tape, with excess of zeros delta = p0 - p1, passes at rate 1/tau. Phases: engine, eraser and dud (Fig. 3, p.4). The bound W <= kT dS holds for all epsilon, delta and tau, with equality only when epsilon = delta (p.5), i.e. only in the trivial case where no work is done. Dimer extension (p.5, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1206.5553#page=5): with matched pairs b_2k-1 = b_2k and 50/50 bits, the demon lifts the mass 'effectively by "digesting" the pairwise correlations'. The outgoing pairs are less ordered (e.g. 01 11 10 10 11), not blanks.
sources.relevance: A template for a small-state local agent that walks a record strand: it is pushed forward by the strand's low entropy (or correlations) and, driven the other way, becomes a priced eraser. Same device, both directions. The dimer case shows that pairwise correlations are fuel for a reader that sees both members together. The reader turns correlated pairs into less correlated pairs; it does not cancel copies into blanks.

sources.title: Correlation-powered information engines and the thermodynamics of self-correction (with companion 'Leveraging environmental correlations: the thermodynamics of requisite variety')
sources.quote: an information engine must have more than one memory state in order to leverage input environment correlations
sources.mechanism: The ratchet is a finite-state transducer making joint Markov jumps with the current tape symbol under detailed-balance rates. A memoryless ratchet's work depends only on single-symbol statistics: it 'cannot distinguish between input strings 01010101 . . . and 00110011' (p.6). Information-processing second law: <W> <= kT ln2 (h'_mu - h_mu), the change in entropy rate. A 3-state ratchet extracts positive work from a period-2 tape where single-symbol bounds wrongly predict none (p.3). It resynchronizes after corruptions up to a critical corruption level (p.1). The companion (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.05353#page=1, MATCH: 'to optimally harvest work a ratchet’s memory must reflect the input generator’s memory') shows memory is needed to best use correlated inputs. It also finds that finite-state optimal ratchets cannot reach the IPSL bounds, that infinite-state ratchets can exceed them by spending their own 'negentropy', and it sketches ratchet swarms.
sources.relevance: A stored history is fuel for a later local reader only through its redundancy (entropy rate below raw capacity), and only if the reader's state carries the matching correlation. A memoryless eraser walking the trace (10,828 nodes in 427 distinct subtrees for add 1 1, per evaluators/rust-ic-strands/README.md around line 1446) can use only per-node statistics. Harvesting duplicates needs a reader that holds one copy while consuming the other.

sources.title: The minimal work cost of information processing
sources.quote: It is given by the entropy of the discarded information conditional to the output of the computation
sources.mechanism: A logical process is written as an isometry into output plus discarded register E. The single-shot work bound is kT ln2 H_max^eps(E|X'). For classical maps with zero error, W >= kT ln2 log2 max over x' of sum over x of p(x'|x), the sum over inputs with nonzero probability. For deterministic maps that is 'the maximum number of input states that map to a same output state' (p.3), so AND costs log2 3 ~ 1.6 bits and XOR 1 bit. The minimal work 'depends in general on the specific logical process, and not only on the input and output states' (p.4, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1211.1037#page=4): a process with AND's input and output distributions but different logic can cost less. When the discarded information is entangled with the output, the conditional entropy is negative and work can be extracted (p.3).
sources.relevance: A per-run (single-shot, worst-case) price suited to a system that runs one term. A K drop costs log2 of the largest number of distinct inputs (with nonzero probability) that collapse to the same visible result. If what remains determines z (z is fixed library code, or the eraser can see z's twin), that number is 1 and the bound is 0. Two rule sets reaching the same answer can differ in minimal work.

sources.title: Fundamental costs in the production and destruction of persistent polymer copies
sources.quote: Once mixed, however, templates cannot be matched to copies a priori, and correlations cannot be leveraged
sources.mechanism: Reversible work for a persistent copy B of template A, from a blank start: <w>_rev = F_B[p_f(b)] - F_B[p0(b)] - T H_f(B) + kT I_f(A;B) (Eq. 1, p.2). Transient binding during growth cannot lower the overall work. Compared with a template-independent copy of the same average length, an accurate copy costs extra work kT I(A;B) and stores it as free energy (Eq. 2). For a perfect copy the -T H_f(B) and +kT I terms are of equal size, so the extra is relative to an inaccurate copy, not to nothing. That stored free energy can be recovered only 'by reversing the copy and hence destroying the offspring' (p.2, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.05554#page=2). Once copies of different templates are mixed, the I term drops out of F (p.3), because pairs can no longer be matched.
sources.relevance: Makes 'accurate copying stores fuel, un-copy refunds it' precise, with the condition that the refund needs the pair to stay identifiable. In the strand lattice a pair stays identifiable while a sharing node or lazy duplicator still links the twins. A finished copy that drifted away (copy-ahead, dnroom) is the 'mixed' case, and the correlation is no longer locally usable.

sources.title: The thermodynamics of computation - a review
sources.quote: Six of these could be converted into blank tapes by a logically and thermodynamically reversible process
sources.mechanism: Brownian computers random-walk along the computation with a weak drive. 'the drift velocity is proportional to the driving force', so dissipation goes to zero only at zero speed (p.1, https://sites.pitt.edu/~jdnorton/lectures/Rotman_Summer_School_2013/thermo_computing_docs/Bennett_1982.pdf#page=1). Backward branching: in an infinite exponentially branching tree, the dissipation per step must exceed about kT ln(mean number of predecessors) or the computation wanders off. When branching is stopped by garden-of-Eden states, extraneous states slow the computation unless backward excursions are suppressed by dissipating 'about kT times the logarithm of the mean number of immediate predecessors' (p.19). Fuel (p.31): N zeros are worth NkT ln2. A pi tape can be fuel via a reversible decompressor. A random tape is fuel only to an apparatus holding a verbatim copy, which in effect cancels against it. Seven identical random tapes convert reversibly to six blanks plus one random tape.
sources.relevance: (a) Drive per rule from backward branching: steps that keep their record need only a small drive (speed cost). A step with b plausible pasts needs about kT ln b to avoid backward wandering, or else it runs slower. substrate.rs's single drive epsilon = 8 at T = 1.5 (README around line 1489) mixes the two. (b) The fuel value of a history is its redundancy: N identical copies are worth N-1 blanks.

key_ideas: Price a drop by surprisal under the rule's own prior. Charge a dropped value z at kT times -ln q(z | what the block keeps after the move). Averaged over firings this is exactly Landauer cost plus mismatch cost (Kolchinsky-Wolpert 2017, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.00956#page=5), and for a single deterministic input it is the per-step EP -ln q(z|island) of Ouldridge-Wolpert 2023 Eq. 16 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.06895#page=7). Faist et al. give the zero-error single-shot version: log2 of the largest number of possible inputs collapsing to one output (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1211.1037#page=3). Erasing fresh randomness costs about its entropy. Erasing library code or a copy next to its twin costs about 0 only if the rule's prior or support is conditioned on what the block sees, i.e. the rule must be an un-copy rule, not a generic eraser.

Make every block move a bijection of block states, with each rewrite keeping its record inside the block. Bijective local moves have zero mismatch and zero locality-plus-periodicity cost (Ouldridge-Wolpert 2023, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.06895#page=8). Global invertibility elsewhere (a far-away trace) does not help (same paper, p.9). The authors warn that machines which overwrite memory affect the modularity cost in ways their DFA analysis does not cover (p.10). Keep exactly one many-to-one move, 'forget', priced as above. On a reversible substrate, forgetting can be modelled as moving bits across the logical/environment boundary into an explicit bath region (Sagawa 2014, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.1886#page=13).

The price of locality per firing is I(block before; outside) - I(block after; outside) (Boyd-Mandal-Crutchfield 2018, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1708.03030#page=2; Eq. 5 on p.4, assuming equal state free energies), summed over firings as the modularity term of Ouldridge-Wolpert 2023. It is an ensemble quantity. Counting drops whose dropped value has a living twin is a usable proxy in disp's simulators. The README's add 1 1 data (102 of the 116 thrown-away pieces are copies of program parts) suggests much of the current erase heat is avoidable locality cost.

Erase copies by un-copying at the twin. Wolpert-Kolchinsky's Proposition 1 is proved by fanning out a copy of an input to a separate eraser: each such gadget adds the input's full entropy to the extra heat, so it can be made arbitrarily large (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1806.04103#page=25). Cancelling a copy against its twin is reversible (Bennett 1982, https://sites.pitt.edu/~jdnorton/lectures/Rotman_Summer_School_2013/thermo_computing_docs/Bennett_1982.pdf#page=31; Sagawa's feedback reset, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.1886#page=1). The refund needs the pair to stay identifiable (Ouldridge-ten Wolde 2017, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.05554#page=3). So copy lazily through a sharing node that links the twins, and treat copy-ahead (dnroom) as turning a refundable correlation into one that cannot be used locally.

History is fuel through its redundancy. N identical random tapes convert reversibly to N-1 blanks plus one random tape (Bennett 1982, p.31). Fuel value is the entropy-rate gap, i.e. correlations and not just bias (Boyd-Mandal-Crutchfield 2017, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.08506#page=1). A local demon can digest pairwise correlations of a duplicated stream (Mandal-Jarzynski 2012, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1206.5553#page=5); note that it outputs less-ordered pairs, not blanks. A deterministic run's history has zero entropy given program plus input, so it can be uncomputed reversibly. Over a full cycle the kept input copy still has to be reset, so this is not free cycle-wise (Wolpert 2019, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.05669#page=71).

A local harvester must carry the correlation it spends ('to optimally harvest work a ratchet's memory must reflect the input generator's memory', https://arxiv.org/pdf/1609.05353#page=1). A memoryless reader sees only single-symbol statistics (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1606.08506#page=1, p.6). To harvest duplicates in the trace, a reader must hold one copy while consuming the other: a merge agent that sits on two subtrees, compares the top layer, un-copies it on a match, and spawns agents on the children. That is the duplicator read backward, and a thermodynamic reading of the repo's memo radius experiment (README section 'Memo radius: merging equal computations (tried, not kept)'). This design is an inference, not something in the sources.

Set the Metropolis drive per rule from its backward branching. Drift is proportional to drive (Bennett 1982, https://sites.pitt.edu/~jdnorton/lectures/Rotman_Summer_School_2013/thermo_computing_docs/Bennett_1982.pdf#page=1). Record-keeping steps need only a small drive, while a step whose undo could go b ways needs about kT ln b. That is strictly required for unbounded backward trees; otherwise it trades against slowdown (same paper, https://sites.pitt.edu/~jdnorton/lectures/Rotman_Summer_School_2013/thermo_computing_docs/Bennett_1982.pdf#page=19). This separates speed cost (residual EP) from information cost instead of folding both into one epsilon = 8.

A fixed rule table pays mismatch on every iteration in general, because mismatch does not telescope when the prior is never updated (Wolpert 2019, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.05669#page=46). Two levers follow. Choose priors that make known things cheap, e.g. concentrated on library code. Or use a uniform prior within each island, which provably minimizes the worst-case EP at ln(largest island size) (Ouldridge-Wolpert 2023, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.06895#page=7). Finely tuned priors risk large overconfidence costs (p.8).

Under modular (block-local) protocols, statistical correlation between the separately evolving subsystems cannot increase, and its drop is a lower bound on EP (Kolchinsky-Wolpert 2021, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2008.10764#page=13). Correlation between blocks is 'inaccessible' free energy until both sides are inside one controlled unit. So twins must be brought into one block to be refunded, e.g. by an energy term pulling a dropped copy toward its sharing node, as substrate.rs's bonds pull what an undo needs.

Forgetting everything but the answer has an algorithmic floor of K(input | output). It is a tradeoff, not a pure heat floor: any computable realization 'faces a fundamental cost of K(x|y), which can be paid either by producing a large amount of heat, by computing an input-output map with high complexity, or by having a heat function with high complexity' (Kolchinsky-Wolpert, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.04685#page=3). substrate.rs's erase-every-leaf mode charges 194-807 leaves plus the 2,300-6,600 records only they led back through (README around line 1532). That one-unit-per-record count is not this floor. Whether most of those records are recomputable ('pi-tape' style) and so ideally near-free is a hypothesis to test, not something the README states.

Being reversible as a whole is not enough under local plus periodic constraints (Ouldridge-Wolpert 2023, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2208.06895#page=9). The two-way calculus in evaluators/rust-ic-strands/crate/src/iso.rs (still present) gives the global inverse. The thermodynamic requirement is that each block step is invertible, so a reversible add (a, b) -> (a, a+b) pays only speed cost only if built from invertible block moves.

field: Timing physics of the strand lattice: how long things tied together by strands take to meet and settle when they diffuse on a lattice (first-passage times, polymer relaxation, whether local moves can reach every state, patch formation in A+B annihilation), plus the scaling limits on wire length and heat removal for nets laid out in 3D

sources.title: Monte Carlo Methods for the Self-Avoiding Walk (Sokal 1994 review)
sources.quote: The nonergodicity of the Verdier-Stockmayer algorithm was noticed as early as 1968
sources.mechanism: State: a self-avoiding walk (SAW) on Z^d, moved by local Metropolis proposals (A one-bead flip, B end rotation, D/E crankshafts, F two-bead). (1) Madras-Sokal 1987 (p.40): every local N-conserving algorithm is nonergodic in d=2,3 for large N, and each ergodic class is an exponentially small fraction of SAW space. The trap is the 'double cul-de-sac' (p.41), frozen under A,B,D,F: it cannot leave or be reached; folding it once more defeats k-bead moves for any k. Separately, in d=3 (and only there) 'knots' in a loose sense (open walks cannot be truly knotted) stop the chain reaching a straight rod, though they are not fully frozen (p.41). (2) Relaxation (p.43): heuristic tau ~ N^(2+2nu) elementary moves, a rigorous lower bound, exact for ordinary random walks under Verdier-Stockmayer, possibly not exact for SAWs. Pure one-bead (Verdier-Stockmayer) and pure two-bead (Kranbuehl-Verdier) dynamics for SAW/NRRW have conservation laws that slow relaxation by at least a further factor N; mixing one- and two-bead moves breaks them. Hilhorst-Deutch-Boots analyse this by mapping to a gas of 1D random walkers with exclusion. (3) Slithering snake (p.44): append at one end, delete at the other. It is bilocal, nonergodic only when both ends are trapped in culs-de-sac, and heuristically tau ~ N^2 moves. (4) BFACF (pp.53-54): one-bead flip (dN=0), kink insertion (+2), kink deletion (-2), each made by displacing the middle bond of a three-bond group one unit sideways, with detailed balance p(+2)=beta^2 p(-2). Ergodic in d=2. In d=3 it is nonergodic for endpoints at sup-distance 1 (knots) and ergodic for sup-distance >=2, because strands can pass between the endpoints. For rings the ergodic classes are exactly the knot classes. tau_exp is infinite for all beta>0, because of arbitrarily slow modes tied to the minimal surface spanned by two walks. tau_int,A is bounded below by about <N>^4, and numerically tau_int,N ~ <N>^p with p close to 4.
sources.relevance: The strand lattice's wire moves are BFACF-like: flip is dN=0, fold is kink deletion. Madras-Sokal's theorem is about N-conserving moves, so the right comparison for disp is BFACF, which changes length, and its d=3 knot obstruction disappears if wires cross freely at switchboards. The leftover traps would be capacity jams, the analogue of culs-de-sac. Without a kink-insertion move mid-wire, new length enters only at agent ends. Note that Sokal's end-only (slithering) dynamics is ~N^2 moves; the N^3 figure comes from the repton tube picture, not from this review. Mixing move kinds breaks hidden conservation laws. Tension near the entropy threshold (README: aux tension vs 2 ln 5) is the BFACF near-critical regime, where tau_int grows like <N>^4.

sources.title: First passage time approach to diffusion controlled reactions (Szabo, Schulten, Schulten 1980)
sources.quote: An inhomogeneous differential equation is derived which, for problems with high symmetry
sources.mechanism: Smoluchowski diffusion in a potential U(r), with a radiation boundary (rate kappa) at a and a reflecting wall at R. The mean passage time solves L+ tau(r0) = -1 and reduces to quadrature: tau = Int_a^R dx [D p_eq(x)]^-1 [Int_x^R p_eq]^2 + [kappa p_eq(a)]^-1 (eq. 2.20). For kappa->0, tau(r0) = 1/(kappa p_eq(a)), independent of r0 (eq. 2.18): particles equilibrate and then react. Table I (free diffusion, x=a/R small, kappa->inf): 1D ~ R^2/(3D); 2D ~ (R^2/2D) ln(R/a); 3D ~ R^3/(3Da). Gaussian-chain end-to-end closure: 1D tau = L^2/(D ln 2) form (eq. 4.6, with a=0); 3D expansion (3D/L^2) tau = sqrt(pi/2)/alpha + ..., with alpha=a/L, so the leading term is proportional to L^3/(Da). Repressor-operator (p.5): step 1 is radial diffusion between two concentric cylinders onto the DNA (the cylindrical, 2D-radial row of Table I); step 2 is 1D sliding along DNA of length 2L. tau = tau_1 + tau_2, with tau_2 = L^2/(3 D_2).
sources.relevance: It gives the formula for undo waits. In the reaction-limited regime the wait is about 1/(tries per clock x equilibrium chance that all needed agents sit in one aligned block). The README's add 1 1 numbers (535,718 tries found it apart, about 2,470 records) give about 1 success per 200 tries. The two-step repressor result is the template for putting things that must re-meet on a shared strand, so the last stage of the search is 1D.

sources.title: Non-Markovian polymer reaction kinetics (Guérin, Bénichou, Voituriez 2012)
sources.quote: The strong dependance of the mean reaction time with the target size in this limit is the signature of a non-compact exploration
sources.mechanism: Phantom Rouse chain of N monomers on linear springs (stiffness k, friction zeta, bond l0), with tau_R = N^2 zeta/(pi^2 k). A monomer's MSD goes 6Dt, then alpha t^(1/2) (walk dimension 4 > 3, so compact), then 6 D_CM t with D_CM = D/N. Small target a << l0/sqrt(N): intermolecular tau = V/(4 pi D a); cyclization tau = sqrt(pi/8)(l0 sqrt N)^3/(D a), i.e. ~N^(3/2)/a. This regime is non-compact, and Wilemski-Fixman and the harmonic-spring model agree with it. Intermediate target l0/sqrt(N) << a < l0 sqrt(N): intermolecular tau = V/(4 pi D_CM a_eff), with a_eff ~ l0 sqrt(N), independent of a as a->0 (p.6). Cyclization tau = c(a/(l0 sqrt N)) N^2 zeta/(pi^2 k): the Rouse-time scale times a function of a only through a/(l0 sqrt N). Markovian theories underestimate a_eff and c by about 2x, because at the moment of reaction the chain is more extended than at equilibrium.
sources.relevance: For two agents joined by a wire of l strands, with a target of about one strand (so a is about l0, the intermediate regime), contact takes about the wire's Rouse time, ~l^2, and depends only weakly on the target size. Without a joining chain, a point searcher in volume V needs about V/(4 pi D a): volume-limited and target-limited. This supports making the undo receipt a wire rather than a number plus a distance energy.

sources.title: Geometry-controlled kinetics (Bénichou, Chevalier, Klafter, Meyer, Voituriez 2010)
sources.quote: is not the subdiffusive vs diffusive nature of the transport process, but its compact vs non compact type
sources.mechanism: A Markov walker with walk dimension d_w in a reflecting domain of N sites with fractal dimension d_f, started at distance r from the target. The first-passage time (FPT) distribution is (1 - Pi) delta(theta) + Pi psi(theta), with theta = T/<T>, and <T> ∝ N in all cases. Non-compact (d_w < d_f, e.g. 3D diffusion): Pi ≈ 1 - alpha/r^(d_f - d_w) and psi = e^-theta. The kinetics are exponential, set by the volume and essentially independent of the start for r well above the step size, except for return or recombination events (p.8). Compact (d_w > d_f): Pi ∝ (r/R)^(d_w - d_f). The time scale runs from r^d_w (start near the target, with probability 1-Pi) to R^d_w (far start), and the reduced variance is ∝ (R/r)^(d_w - d_f) (p.6). Mean FPT from S = Pi <T> ∝ r^(d_w-d_f) R^d_f.
sources.relevance: Once a twin or refund particle drifts off in 3D, re-meeting costs time proportional to the explored volume, and being born close buys only a ~a/r chance of a quick geminate return. On a 1D path (d_w=2 > d_f=1, compact) a nearby partner is found in typical time ~r^2, against R^2 from far away. The mean is ~rR, because of rare long excursions. Design rule: things that must re-meet should search along a shared strand.

sources.title: Applications of field-theoretic renormalization group methods to reaction-diffusion problems (Täuber, Howard, Vollmayr-Lee 2005)
sources.quote: This conservation law provides a slow mode in the dynamics that is crucial in determining the long-time behavior
sources.mechanism: A+B->0 conserves the local difference a-b, which (for D_A=D_B) obeys a diffusion equation, so it is a slow mode. With equal initial densities n0, Toussaint-Wilczek argue that inside each diffusion length only the initial local majority survives. The species segregate, giving a(t) ~ sqrt(n0)/(sqrt(pi)(8 pi D t)^(d/4)) (p.8, eq. 5), which dominates the mean-field t^-1 for d<4. Ovchinnikov-Zeldovich [28] are cited as first noting that uniform mixing fails. Bramson-Lebowitz proved the exponent exact [16,17,31]. Lee-Cardy recover t^(-d/4) for 2<d<4 from field theory with initial-fluctuation 'surface' terms (p.35). Unequal densities: the minority decays exponentially for d>2. Initially separated species form a Gálfi-Rácz front of width t^(1/6). A+A->(0,A) has d_c=2, so it is mean-field in 3D (p.6). mA+nB keeps t^(-d/4) for d < 4/(m+n-1). Reversible reactions approach equilibrium as t^(-d/2), driven by conservation laws (Rey-Cardy, p.37).
sources.relevance: Anti-trees or refunds drawn independently of what they cancel would segregate into patches in 3D (t^-3/4), so reaching leftover density rho costs ~rho^(-4/3) instead of rho^(-1). Pair-creating each at its partner's site removes the large-scale initial imbalance that TW kinetics feed on. Our inference: Lee-Cardy say only the initial fluctuations matter for 2<d<4. Equal-value coalescence (A+A) is mean-field in 3D.

sources.title: Structural modes of a polymer in the repton model (Barkema, Panja, van Leeuwen 2011)
sources.quote: a snake-like motion in which stored length travels back and forth along the polymer, and can be created and annealed only
sources.mechanism: Rubinstein's repton model: each link is taut (a unit vector) or slack (a unit of 'stored length'). Motion is stored length diffusing along the chain, created and annealed only at the ends (pp.3-4), so the tube changes only at the ends. D = 1/((2d+1)N^2) (van Leeuwen-Kooiman), shown exact by Prähofer-Spohn and Widom-Al-Lehyani. Stored-length density fluctuations relax by tau_R ~ N^2; the tube renews at tau_d ~ N^3 (p.5). Rouse-mode amplitude correlations of the repton chain decay as exp(-(p/N)^2 A(t)), with one A(t) shared by all modes. Simulated with bit operations.
sources.relevance: This is the closest exact model of a wire whose path changes only through its end agents: layout renewal ~l^3, while slack redistribution along it is ~l^2. The N^3 comes from forbidding mid-chain kink creation (the tube constraint). That disp's mid-wire flips and folds would give Rouse-like l^2 relaxation is general polymer knowledge (cf. Sokal), not shown in this paper. Slack as a conserved hopping particle is a ready picture for refunds riding wires: a 1D exclusion gas, which explores compactly.

sources.title: Long range bond-bond correlations in dense polymer solutions (Wittmer et al. 2004)
sources.quote: a lattice Monte Carlo scheme where a monomer occupies 8 lattice sites
sources.mechanism: What the source says (p.1): in the bond fluctuation model (BFM) each monomer occupies 8 lattice sites (a 2x2x2 cube), and bonds between neighbours 'can vary in length and direction, subject only to excluded volume constraints and entanglement restrictions' (refs [7,8], Carmesin-Kremer). Ensembles up to N=2048 (single chains to 32768) were created 'using a mixture of local, slithering snake and double-bridging moves'. Not in this source: the move rule (step one site, check the leading face), how the allowed bond set forbids crossing, what double-bridging does, and any claim that nonlocal moves are required.
sources.relevance: BFM is the polymer world's analogue of a 2x2x2 block object, and its bonds obey non-crossing ('entanglement') restrictions inside a local Monte Carlo scheme. That is weak support for the idea that non-crossing can be enforced locally; the actual local rule lives in Carmesin-Kremer 1988, which is unverified. The use of slithering and double-bridging for long chains is consistent with, but does not prove, the need for moves along a wire's own frame.

sources.title: Locality, communication, and interconnect length in multicomputers (Vitányi 1988)
sources.quote: realistic models for non-sequential computation should charge extra for communication, in terms of time and space
sources.mechanism: Unit-size nodes are packed in a 3D sphere of radius R = (3N/4 pi)^(1/3); wires have length but no volume and can pass through nodes (p.5). Theorem 2 bounds average edge length for any graph in terms of edge orbits under its automorphism group and its diameter D. Corollary 4: for edge-symmetric graphs the average is at least 7R/(16D), and the constant can be improved to 3/4. Complete graph and star: average Omega(N^(1/3)), total Omega(N^(4/3)). Binary n-cube and CCC: about N^(1/3)/log N average. Complete binary tree: O(1) via the H-tree. The abstract (p.3) says the bound is optimal for all topologies examined (complete graph, star, n-cube, CCC, complete binary tree, torus/ring).
sources.relevance: A lower bound on wire length for small-diameter, highly symmetric sharing graphs, even with zero-volume wires. Tree-shaped computation can stay at O(1) average wire. The bound strictly needs edge symmetry (or few edge orbits); a disp net after copying is not edge-symmetric, so for generic expander-like wiring Gromov-Guth is the better bound.

sources.title: Generalizations of the Kolmogorov-Barzdin embedding estimates (Gromov, Guth 2011)
sources.quote: Kolmogorov and Barzdin essentially observed that a random graph is an expander
sources.mechanism: Theorem 1 (Kolmogorov-Barzdin): any graph of N vertices with degree at most d embeds in R^3 with thickness 1 (non-adjacent edges, vertices, and edge-to-nonincident-vertex all at distance >= 1; picture balls and tubes) in a ball of radius C(d) N^(1/2). Conversely, a random bipartite degree-6 graph on 2N vertices (an expander w.h.p.) has no thickness-1 embedding in a ball of radius c N^(1/2), and any thickness-1 embedding has a 1-neighbourhood of volume at least c N^(3/2). The paper extends this to k-complexes in R^n (Theorem 2) and to knot distortion.
sources.relevance: Strands have thickness (bounded strands per link), so this is the right bound for disp wires. An expander-like net needs volume ~N^(3/2). Since vertices fill only ~N, the tubes must have total length ~N^(3/2), i.e. ~N^(1/2) per edge (our inference). Link capacity L changes only the constant, not the exponent. Radius N^(1/2) is always achievable.

sources.title: Horizons of Parallel Computation (Bilardi, Preparata 1993)
sources.quote: The main result is that scalability holds only for neighborly interconnections, such as the square mesh
sources.mechanism: Finite signal speed plus minimum device size. A family has slowdown tau(k), the maximum duration of one step of member k, and is strict-sense scalable if tau = O(1) (p.9). Bounded-dimension cellular automata and one-head Turing machines are scalable because 'communication occurs only within bounded distance'; these are 'the only examples of strict-sense scalable machines we know of' (p.10). Multihead TMs are not. A RAM has tau = Theta(sqrt(m log m)) under a planar memory layout. For networks, the longest wire is L_p = Omega(max(sqrt p, B_p)/D_p) (Leighton 1981, a 2D VLSI layout bound), so trees, hypercubes and CCC are not scalable and the mesh is (p.12). Latency hiding cannot lift a mesh's P-RAM throughput above O(sqrt p) ops per unit time, and fails for the hypercube (pp.18-22). Remark (p.12): CA nodes 'are indistinguishable from each other and independent of array size', whereas mesh nodes carry IDs whose size grows.
sources.relevance: This is the formal version of locality criteria 1-3. A lattice stays strict-sense scalable only while every site is finite-state and nameless. A global record table, plus ids and record numbers carried by agents, are 'IDs whose size grows'. Any rule whose effect reaches beyond a block adds slowdown proportional to that reach.

sources.title: Reversibility for Efficient Computing (Frank 1999 PhD thesis; R3M)
sources.quote: irreversible computers turn out to ultimately be limited to processing rates that are only proportional to their surface area
sources.mechanism: R3M (p.100): a family of fixed-capacity machines, each a uniform 3D array of processing elements (PEs) capable of fully logically and arbitrarily thermodynamically reversible operation, each connected to '(say) its 6 nearest neighbors'. PE storage, bandwidth and clock rate are finite. Entropy is explicit: a nonzero entropy coefficient per PE, finite maximum entropy flux density, finite velocity of entropy transport, and entropy from optional erasure. Irreversible operations are optional and under program control. Unwanted information must be exported through the surface, which grows as n^2 against the processor count's n^3 (p.97). Reversible operation is limited by friction, with dissipation per operation proportional to speed (p.97). Even reversible machines eventually hit the surface limit on energy supply (p.98), so reversibility wins by 'small polynomial factors in the machine size' (p.25); the exact factor on p.27 is OCR-garbled.
sources.relevance: Sets the price for erasure. In an L^3 lattice, sustained erasure is at most ~L^2 per clock, and the entropy must travel to the boundary. A physical core that emits heat carriers needing to reach a sink would automatically throttle bulk erasure and make un-copying and uncomputing the cheap default. It also supports the Bennett-style drive (energy proportional to speed) as the model for forward bias.

key_ideas: Diagnosis of the 10-12x slower backward runs (README: of add 1 1's undo tries, 535,718 found the agents apart). A forward rewrite needs 2 agents one strand apart on a principal wire under tension, which is a 1D, compact search. An undo (substrate.rs `undo`/`gather`) needs every product, plus the near ends of each joined wire, inside one aligned Margolus 2x2x2 block, tied only by `bond_de`. That is a k-body, wire-less 3D coincidence. In the reaction-limited regime, the wait is about 1/(tries per clock x P_eq(all needed agents in one aligned block)) (Szabo-Schulten-Schulten eq. 2.18), roughly 1 success per 200 tries here. Caveat: the R/a 3D-to-1D ratio in SSS Table I is a diffusion-limited result. In the reaction-limited regime the ratio is set by p_eq and scales more like R^2/a^2, so the apparent match to 10-12x is suggestive only.

Make every inverse a binary, wired event. Guérin et al.: two points joined by a chain meet in about the chain's Rouse time (~l^2), only weakly dependent on target size. An unjoined searcher needs ~V/(4 pi D a). SSS repressor: 3D then 1D search. So keep a receipt strand between what a rewrite made, or split rules so each inverse needs only two agents to meet; avoid k-body conditions.

Undo pieces, copy twins and refunds should search along a strand (compact exploration), not through open 3D (non-compact) (Bénichou et al. 2010). In 3D, being born adjacent buys only a ~a/r chance of a quick geminate return, and the rest wait volume-limited times. On a strand, a nearby start buys a factor ~(R/r)^2 in typical time, but only ~R/r in mean time (the mean 1D first-passage time is ~rR).

Pair-create every anti-particle or refund at the site of what it cancels; never draw them from a uniform reservoir. Independently placed A+B annihilation segregates into patches and decays as t^(-3/4) in 3D instead of t^-1, so the tail costs rho^(-4/3) (Toussaint-Wilczek, proved by Bramson-Lebowitz, via Täuber et al.).

If annihilation must find one specific partner, tether the partners with a strand. Otherwise let any two equal values un-copy: A+A coalescence has critical dimension 2, so it is mean-field and fast in 3D (Täuber et al.).

Wire move set (Sokal review: Madras-Sokal, BFACF; repton). BFACF (flip, kink insert, kink delete) is the right comparison, since disp's fold changes length. Free crossing at switchboards removes the 3D knot-class obstruction. Confirm or add a mid-wire length-creating move, or wire layout can only renew through the ends: repton tube renewal ~l^3 against stored-length relaxation ~l^2. Mix move kinds to break hidden conservation laws (pure one-bead or pure two-bead dynamics pay at least an extra factor N). Keep tension away from the entropy threshold (README: aux tension near 2 ln 5), the BFACF near-critical regime where tau_int grows like <N>^4.

Any locally conserved quantity (fuel, heat, strand count, the anti-minus-particle difference) is a slow diffusive mode (Täuber et al.: the a-b field; Rey-Cardy t^(-d/2)). Budget for it, or carry it along wires.

Heat is a physical flux. Sustained erasure in an L^3 lattice is at most O(L^2) per clock (Frank, R3M), and even reversible operation is eventually surface-limited, so the advantage is polynomial. A core that emits heat carriers needing to reach a boundary sink makes un-copying and uncomputing the cheap default (the carrier design is ours; Frank assumes finite-velocity entropy transport).

Expected wire cost of laying out post-S nets in 3D. Trees: O(1) average wire (Vitányi, H-tree). Edge-symmetric small-diameter sharing: average at least 7R/(16D) ~ N^(1/3)/D, even with zero-volume wires (Vitányi). Expander-like wiring with thick strands: volume ~N^(3/2), hence ~N^(1/2) average wire (Kolmogorov-Barzdin via Gromov-Guth). Time per wire: ~l for a demand pulse, ~l/v for a tension-driven walk, ~l^2 diffusive. So copy near the reader, re-use instead of copy, and keep sharing local.

Locality audit (Bilardi-Preparata): the only strict-sense scalable machines known are bounded-range CAs, whose cells are nameless and independent of size. The substrate's global record table and per-agent ids/record numbers are growing IDs, and must become bounded local state or strands for the core to scale.

The bond fluctuation model (BFM) uses 2x2x2 (8-site) monomers whose bonds obey only excluded-volume and entanglement (non-crossing) restrictions in a local Monte Carlo scheme (Wittmer et al.). That is weak evidence that non-crossing can be enforced locally; the exact local rule is in Carmesin-Kremer, which is unverified. disp's free crossing remains the better choice for reachability.

field: Dataflow and spatial hardware for fine-grained functional evaluation: the engineering record on re-using a circuit versus copying it under maximal parallelism (static vs tagged-token dataflow, throttling, elastic/latency-insensitive circuits, systolic arrays, combinator hardware, local circuit sharing)

sources.title: A Preliminary Architecture for a Basic Data-Flow Processor (Dennis & Misunas 1975)
sources.quote: An operator or a link cannot fire unless there is no token present on any output arc of that operator or link
sources.mechanism: Static dataflow. A program is a fixed graph of actors (operator, link, decider, T-gate, F-gate, merge, Boolean operator) joined by arcs. Firing rule: an actor fires when its inputs hold tokens and every output arc is empty, so each arc is a one-slot buffer. Fan-out is an explicit link node that 'places tokens on its output arcs bearing copies of the input value' (p1). Erasure is explicit: a T-gate given a false control token will 'absorb the data token on its input arc and place nothing on its output arc' (p3). A merge passes on the token from the input its control token selects. The machine stores each actor as an Instruction Cell of three registers (instruction plus two operands); enabled cells send operation packets through an Arbitration Network to pipelined Operation Units, results return through a Distribution Network, and deciders feed Decision Units that emit gate- or value-type control packets through a Control Network. Concurrent activation of procedures is listed as future work (p7), so two simultaneous activations of the same code need two copies of the graph. Nothing is kept once a token is consumed.
sources.relevance: Baseline that disp's net already follows: a wire is a one-slot arc, Dn plays the role of the link (explicit copy) and Eps the absorbing gate (explicit erase). Lesson: static wiring is local, but every parallel activation costs a copy of the code. Reading the 'output arc must be empty' clause as tokens-forward/holes-backward conservation is the reviewer's interpretation, not something this paper states.

sources.title: Executing a Program on the MIT Tagged-Token Dataflow Architecture (Arvind & Nikhil 1990)
sources.quote: keeping a single copy of the function body, and by tagging each token with a context identifier
sources.mechanism: Tagged dataflow. Tokens carry a context ('think of a context exactly as a "frame pointer"', p4), destination instruction, datum and port; there is one copy of each function body and activations are distinguished by context. Two-input instructions fire when the wait-match unit, 'the rendezvous point for pairs', finds a partner with the same tag; it has associative-memory semantics 'but can be implemented using hashing' (p15). get-context allocates a context from a manager (managers are 'often distributed', p12); change-tag/extract-tag move tokens between contexts. Context resources must be recycled only when the activation terminates (p8). Loops: a k-throttled loop's prelude enables k-1 iterations, Dk operators advance the iteration context mod k, and the switches' Booleans are gated so iteration i+k waits for i (p12-13). 'Loop throttling amounts to inserting extra data dependencies', and if throttled too much a loop can deadlock where the unthrottled one would not (p12). k may be a compile/load-time pragma or 'dynamically generated based on the current load'. I-structures are write-once cells with Present/Absent/Waiting presence bits and deferred-read lists (p7). In the earlier U-interpreter 'each context carried within it the entire chain of its parent contexts' (p17). Id World plots parallelism profiles (p17).
sources.relevance: Clearest statement of copy-versus-share: share code by naming activations, at the price of a match table and context managers. Transferable without the table: recycle a shared resource only after completion is signalled, and throttling adds dependencies that can themselves deadlock. The U-interpreter's full-path tag is the dataflow analogue of a copy-tag history, used only as a name.

sources.title: Resource Management for the Tagged Token Dataflow Architecture (Culler 1985, MIT/LCS/TR-332)
sources.quote: loops exhibit bounded unfolding if and only if the graph forms a single strongly connected component
sources.mechanism: Four resource problems between the U-interpreter and the TTDA, each with a mechanism (abstract, p3): (1) termination detection by augmenting graphs with auxiliary arcs so a particular operation's firing signifies completion; (2) token-store overflow avoided by computing worst-case token storage as an integer linear program over legal graph configurations and reserving it; (3) iteration-identifier overflow: loops have bounded unfolding iff the graph is one strongly connected component, and a transformation gives controlled unfolding and 'automatic reuse of iteration identifiers'; (4) program deadlock from an over-broad invocation tree, fixed by a strategy that 'constrains program unfolding so that just enough parallelism is exposed to fully utilize the machine'.
sources.relevance: Directly usable design rule: a region closed into one strongly connected cycle (forward data plus a backward credit path) can only unfold a bounded amount; feed-forward regions can run away. Aim for 'just enough' parallelism. Calling the bounded-token property a conservation law is the reviewer's gloss (it is the standard marked-graph invariant), not Culler's wording.

sources.title: Monsoon: an Explicit Token-Store Architecture (Papadopoulos & Culler 1990)
sources.quote: Arcs in the graph for the function are statically mapped onto slots in the frame by coloring the graph
sources.mechanism: Tag = (frame pointer, instruction pointer). The instruction names a frame offset and matching inspects that one slot via presence bits: 'If the slot is empty, the value on the token is deposited in the slot (making it full)', otherwise the partner is taken and the instruction fires (p2). Arcs map to slots by graph colouring 'much like modern register assignment', so a slot can serve several arcs whose lifetimes do not overlap. 'Initially, all slots in a frame are empty and upon completion of the activation they will have returned to that state'; compiled graphs include an explicit frame release. Frames form a tree, not a stack. For loops several frames are allocated and 'a frame is not reused until the previous uses of it are complete'. No associative search.
sources.relevance: A matching store reduces to one rendezvous slot per arc per activation; in an interaction net the wire already is that slot, so what disp lacks is code sharing, not matching. The empty-full-empty slot cycle is a clean resource cycle, but note Monsoon still releases frames by an explicit compiled release, not by detecting emptiness.

sources.title: WaveScalar (Swanson, Michelson, Schwerin, Oskin 2003)
sources.quote: In WaveScalar, the same processing element handles the instruction for all iterations
sources.mechanism: Instructions are placed in PEs of the WaveCache (about 2K PEs in clusters of 16, 8 instructions per PE) and stay for 'potentially millions of' invocations; 'the same processing element handles the instruction for all iterations' (p4). Every data value carries a wave-number tag; WAVE-ADVANCE, placed by the compiler at each wave entry (including loop back-edges), increments it. Matching is per instruction: input queues need 'as few as 2 entries per instruction', are 'indexed relative to the current wave', with full/empty bits, 'obviating the need for content addressable memories' (p5). Overflow values spill to virtual memory at an address formed from instruction, queue number and wave number, with prefetch back (p10); performance is largely unaffected by queue size except for the smallest sizes. Memory order uses wave-ordered memory.
sources.relevance: A local alternative to a global match table: stationary code, small per-instruction queues indexed relative to the current wave, and tag advancement done by ordinary instructions. It is still a tagged machine (every value carries its wave number), but the tag is a small counter interpreted locally.

sources.title: The TYR Dataflow Architecture: Improving Locality by Taming Parallelism (Agarwal et al. 2024)
sources.quote: Each local tag space can be tiny (two tags is enough) without risking deadlock
sources.mechanism: Unordered dataflow with local tag spaces per concurrent block. Diagnosis: 'limiting the tag space leads to deadlock' because prior machines allocate from a single global tag space (p2). allocate pops a tag at each transfer point; to guarantee forward progress it 'will pop the last tag only if the context is ready', where ready means all of the context's inputs have arrived (p7). Tail-recursive allocations need a 'spare tag', so external allocates pop only if at least two tags remain. free returns a tag after a compiler-inserted join whose transitive fan-in reaches every instruction of the block (free barrier); every instruction emits a token with its input's tag so the barrier sees completion. changeTag/extractTag move tokens between tag spaces. Deadlock freedom and bounded live tokens are proved after general recursion is turned into tail recursion with an explicit stack (p9). Result: 'parallelism nearly identical to a naïve unordered dataflow architecture with orders-of-magnitude less state'. Ordered dataflow (FIFO between instructions): 'there is no need for a tag, other than the instruction itself', back pressure does not risk deadlock, but it is prone to stalls because long-latency operations block later instances of the same instruction (p5). Ordered dataflow's carry operator is defined in Wavelet ('Let it Flow', arXiv 2608.05451, p3): 'A carry operator (C) acts as a loop variable: it initially forwards its left input'.
sources.relevance: Two rules: a name only needs to be unique within the block that matches it, so tiny local label sets can replace global ids; and never hand the last free resource to a context whose inputs have not all arrived. For disp's copy-ahead duplicators: copying ahead should not take the last free site unless the consumer is already fully supplied.

sources.title: Spatial Computation (Budiu, Venkataramani, Chelcea, Goldstein 2004)
sources.quote: in ASH computation structures are never shared, and each program operation is synthesized as a different functional unit
sources.mechanism: CASH compiles C through the Pegasus IR to asynchronous hardware (ASH) where every operation is its own unit. Semantics is static dataflow, 'each edge can hold a single value at one time' (p3). Pegasus unifies predication and forward speculation (predicate promotion within hyperblocks); MU/ETA handle control; COMBINE joins memory-order tokens. Lenient operations compute early but expect all inputs eventually. Loops pipeline automatically (dataflow software pipelining); FIFOs are inserted to balance strongly connected components (slack matching). 'Recursion is handled in exactly the same way as in software' with stack frames. Limit study vs a 4-way out-of-order SimpleScalar on SpecInt95: 099.go and 132.ijpeg about 25% faster on ASH, the rest 10-40% slower; slowdowns analysed via the dynamic critical path of last-arrival events, where sometimes 'the ack is the last-arrival event' (p4); branch prediction is the main superscalar advantage on control-intensive code.
sources.relevance: Honest measurement of 'never share, always spatial': locality wins on energy, but control and memory-order critical paths dominate time. The last-arrival attribution (data vs ack/backpressure vs distance) is a cheap profiling idea for lattice runs.

sources.title: Why Systolic Architectures? (Kung 1982)
sources.quote: The crux of this approach is to ensure that once a data item is brought out from the memory it can be used effectively at each cell
sources.mechanism: A systolic array pumps data from memory through a regular network of simple cells, each using it as it passes (p3). Convolution designs use a cell like y_out = y_in + w·x_in, passing x on; variants keep weights stationary and move x and y in the same or opposite directions. Some designs (B1, B2) broadcast x and are semi-systolic; 'Pure systolic systems totally avoid long-distance or irregular wires for data communication. The only global communication (besides power and ground) is the system clock' (p8).
sources.relevance: A third option beside copying and sharing: pass-through use, where a value needed k times is threaded past k stationary cells each doing a controlled update and handing the value on. The reversibility of (x, y) -> (x, y + w·x) and the suggested non-destructive triage for tree calculus's S rule are the reviewer's extrapolations, not Kung's claims.

sources.title: Theory of Latency-Insensitive Design (Carloni, McMillan, Sangiovanni-Vincentelli 2001)
sources.quote: a module is a patient process if its behavior does not depend on the latency of the communication channels
sources.mechanism: Systems are built from patient processes whose behaviour does not depend on channel latency. Each stallable module is encapsulated in a shell/wrapper implementing the latency-insensitive protocol; long wires are segmented by relay stations, which the paper shows must be capacity-2 buffers to sustain throughput one (a capacity-1 buffer caps throughput at 0.5). Theorems: composition of patient processes is patient (III.1), latency equivalence is compositional (III.2), and replacing strict processes by patient ones yields a latency-equivalent system (III.3). The only requirement on modules is that they be stallable.
sources.relevance: The correctness contract for wires of arbitrary length: if every agent is patient, adding relay segments changes timing but never results. disp's confluent interaction-net reduction plausibly gives this for free, provided no rule depends on arrival order; that inference is the reviewer's, not the paper's.

sources.title: Synchronous Elastic Circuits with Early Evaluation and Token Counterflow (Cortadella & Kishinevsky 2007)
sources.quote: tokens carrying information move in the forward direction and anti-tokens canceling information move in the backward direction
sources.mechanism: Elastic channels have 'valid, in the forward direction, and stop, in the backward direction' (SELF, DAC 2006, https://www.cs.upc.edu/~jordicf/gavina/BIB/files/dac06_self.pdf#page=2); elastic buffers need C >= Lf + Lb, so 'the minimal possible capacity is C = 2' (dac06 p3). The 2007 paper models early evaluation with dual marked graphs (markings in Z, early-enabling nodes). An early-enabled node, e.g. a multiplexer whose select and chosen input are valid, fires and produces an anti-token on each input it did not wait for. Anti-tokens flow backward on dual wires (V-/S-), and 'When a token and an anti-token are held in dual arcs, they must cancel each other' (p2). Token and anti-token logic is symmetric; anti-token propagation can be stopped (passive anti-tokens). Invariant: a token cannot be killed and stopped at the same time.
sources.relevance: Model for triage and K dropping arms: fire on the selector, send anti-tokens up the unchosen arms to cancel pending tokens. The claim that on a reversible substrate erasure reuses production machinery and costs heat only on unique information is the reviewer's extrapolation.

sources.title: Resource Sharing in Dataflow Circuits (Josipović, Marmet, Guerrieri, Ienne 2022)
sources.quote: The merge and the branch communicate through a FIFO, with as many slots as there are pipeline stages in the unit
sources.mechanism: Dynamatic dataflow circuits use merge, mux, branch, fork (lazy or eager) and join, plus buffers. Deadlock freedom requires that 'each cyclic path must always have at least one empty buffer slot' (p2, from prior work). To share one unit among several operations, a merge picks a request and records which one in a FIFO as long as the unit's pipeline; operand muxes and the output branch consume that record to route the result (p3). Naive sharing 'may cause deadlock' (p1). Fixes: a 1-slot transparent buffer on each branch output, and forcing tokens to enter the unit in order of basic-block execution: 'always sending tokens into the unit in order of BB execution guarantees the absence of deadlock' (p4). Result: up to 81% DSP reduction 'with minimal or no impact on execution time'.
sources.relevance: A concrete template for sharing a sub-net locally without a matching store: merge, a FIFO of route records, branch. The route record is a history that the result consumes on its way out. Reversibility of the merge/branch pair and 'the FIFO becomes a stack for recursion' are the reviewer's extrapolations; the paper handles non-recursive C and its ordering rule is program (BB) order, which a tree-calculus net lacks.

sources.title: The Implementation of Functional Languages Using Custom Hardware (Stoye 1985, Cambridge TR-81)
sources.quote: In case 4, cells 2 and 3 can both be reused, which is very convenient as we were just about to generate two new cells
sources.mechanism: SKIM II is a microcoded combinator reducer on a heap of two-pointer cells, using one-bit reference counts on pointers: an application pointer is mappl (multiple) or uappl, the latter meaning 'there are no other pointers to this cell', so discarding a uappl frees its cell (p37). S a b c has four cases by uniqueness of the two spine pointers; in case 3 one dying cell is reused, in case 4 both are reused and 'no cells generated' (p38). Because S duplicates c, a uappl c must be changed to mappl. Combinators whose freed cells cannot be used immediately put them on the free chain. 'On average, about seventy percent of wasted cells are immediately reclaimed' (p39), with timings on Takeuchi's function and a 2000-element sort.
sources.relevance: In a linear net every wire is unique, so Stoye's best case is the normal case: write rules so dying agents become the fresh agents and ordinary rewrites neither allocate nor free; only copying and erasing touch the resource ledger. The fuel/heat framing is the reviewer's.

key_ideas: There are three ways to run one piece of code for many activations. Copy it: static dataflow, and disp's Dn duplicators (Dennis & Misunas 1975). Name the activations and match tokens by name: tagged-token dataflow, classically with a global match table (Arvind & Nikhil 1990), but made local by small per-block tag spaces (TYR 2024) or per-instruction wave-relative queues (WaveScalar 2003, still tagged). Order the activations: FIFO/ordered dataflow, needing no tag beyond the instruction (TYR p5), or merge-FIFO-branch sharing (Josipović et al. 2022). Copying and ordering are the most local; local naming is the middle ground.

A shared circuit with a local route record: a merge records 'which caller' in a FIFO beside the shared unit, and the branch consumes it to send the result home, so the record is a history used up by the answer. Deadlock needs a transparent one-slot buffer on each branch output and requests entering in program (basic-block) order (Josipović et al. 2022). Reversibility of the pair and a stack for recursion are untested extrapolations.

Backpressure and bounded unfolding: every cycle of a dataflow circuit must keep at least one empty slot (Josipović et al. 2022), and a loop's unfolding is bounded iff its graph is one strongly connected component (Culler 1985). Reading this as tokens-plus-holes conservation is an interpretation that suits a reversible lattice.

Forward progress under bounded resources: never give the last free tag to a context whose inputs have not all arrived (TYR's allocate rule), keep a spare for tail recursion, and a name need only be unique inside the block that matches it, so two tags per block suffice (TYR 2024).

Throttling is a correctness condition, not a tuning knob: unbounded unfolding exhausts storage and deadlocks (Culler 1985, 'just enough parallelism'), yet throttling inserts extra data dependencies and can itself deadlock when a loop is throttled too much (Arvind & Nikhil 1990, p12).

Erasure as anti-tokens: an early-evaluating join (e.g. a multiplexer with its select) fires and sends anti-tokens backward into the inputs it did not wait for, cancelling tokens they meet, with logic symmetric to forward tokens (Cortadella & Kishinevsky 2007). Triage and K map naturally onto this.

Pass-through use instead of copying: in pure systolic designs a value is pumped past k stationary cells, each using it and handing it on, with only nearest-neighbour wires (Kung 1982). The link to the reversible add (a, b) -> (a, a + b) is an interpretation.

Recycle the redex: when the redex's pointers are unique, the dying cells become the new cells, so an S rewrite allocates nothing and about 70% of wasted cells are reclaimed immediately (Stoye 1985). In a linear net this is the normal case, leaving only copying and erasing to touch the resource ledger.

Self-cleaning rendezvous: in Monsoon every frame slot starts empty and returns empty at activation completion, matching costs one slot lookup, but frames are released by an explicit compiled release (Monsoon 1990); TYR detects completion with a compiled free-barrier join over the block (TYR 2024). Using 'all slots empty again' as a local completion test is an open idea, not prior practice.

Latency insensitivity as an invariant: if every module is patient, wire length changes timing but never results, and capacity-2 relay buffers sustain full throughput (Carloni et al. 2001; Cortadella et al. 2006). No rule should depend on arrival timing.

Measure before choosing: attribute each operation's delay to its last-arriving input, which may be data or an acknowledgement (backpressure) (Budiu et al. 2004), and record parallelism profiles (Id World, Arvind & Nikhil 1990 p17). Budiu's limit study also shows pure spatial execution losing to branch prediction on control-heavy code.

Tags are a history: the U-interpreter's tag carried the whole chain of parent contexts (Arvind & Nikhil 1990, p17), the dataflow form of a copy-tag, but used only as a name matched in a table. Storing the same information as local route records along the path keeps it local and lets the result consume it.

field: Distributed algorithms that track copies, sharing and completion with a conserved quantity (deficit, credit, weight, permission) that is split on fork and recombined on join, instead of ids or a global view

sources.title: Termination detection for diffusing computations (EWD 687a; Information Processing Letters 11(1):1-4), Dijkstra and Scholten 1980
sources.quote: each edge will have carried as many messages in the one direction as it has carried signals in the opposite direction
sources.mechanism: Nodes send work messages forward along edges. Every message is eventually answered by exactly one signal sent back along the same edge. Each edge's deficit is messages sent minus signals returned. Each node keeps C (sum of its incoming deficits) and D (sum of its outgoing deficits). Invariant P3: C>0 or D=0, so a node with unanswered children stays engaged. A node may signal only under guard G: C>1 or (C=1 and D=0) (https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~EWD/ewd06xx/EWD687a.PDF#page=6). As first stated, a node keeps a 'bag' of the predecessors it owes signals to, and may answer them in any order. The bag is then replaced by a 'cornet': the oldest element, the sender of the engaging message, has to be answered last ('very first in, very last out', https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~EWD/ewd06xx/EWD687a.PDF#page=7). The paper does NOT require extra messages to be answered at once; answering them immediately is the simplification Tel and Mattern 1993 derive (their p.26: 'Dijkstra and Scholten's scheme allows to delay the sending of a signal, but otherwise their scheme is identical'). With the cornet, the engagement edges form a rooted tree with the environment as root, holding exactly the engaged nodes ('we conclude that the engagement edges form a rooted tree', https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~EWD/ewd06xx/EWD687a.PDF#page=8). Theorem 2: once the environment is back in its neutral state, the computation has terminated. State per node is the counters plus the cornet (the predecessors still owed signals, with the oldest marked). It shrinks to two counters and one parent pointer only if extras are answered at once. There are no ids beyond neighbour names and no global view, and the cost is one signal per message.
sources.relevance: This fits the repo's open item 'The substrate's records as matter' (evaluators/rust-ic-strands/README.md, Open section): a record held by what it made instead of a numbered table. A fired rewrite or duplicator stays as an engaged agent holding a small deficit (which outputs are still out) and a wire to its parent. A return token going back up that wire is the signal. When everything is back, the node collapses, and the root (Out) back at zero deficit knows the net is done. The cornet rule says which records may collapse early and which must wait. Precedent in the repo: the two-way calculus walker's 'Tokens split and come back together' fork, which waited with a hole for each half (README at commit eca0073). That walker lived in walk.rs, removed in 2a32736; iso.rs is still in the tree. The README reports 4-7 tokens at most. The claim that this low count came from forking only at `both`, and not from the split/join law, is the sweep's reading; the README does not say it.

sources.title: Global quiescence detection based on credit distribution and recovery (Information Processing Letters 30(4):195-200), Mattern 1989
sources.quote: If it has recovered the whole sum, the environment announces global quiescence
sources.mechanism: The environment starts with total credit 1, and every active process and every activation message in transit holds a share; the shares always add up to 1. R1: a process going passive sends its credit to the environment. R2: a message arriving at an active process sends its credit to the environment (a variant adds it to the process's own credit instead). R3: a message arriving at a passive process hands its credit to that process. R4: on a send, the sender keeps half and the message takes the other half. Theorem 1 (safety): if the environment has regained the whole sum, the system is quiescent. Only the exponent is stored (share 2^-CREDIT), so a send is CREDIT := CREDIT+1. Optimization: when a message arrives at an active process with CR = CREDIT, the two merge locally ('If CR = CREDIT, it is not necessary to send CR to the environment', CREDIT := CREDIT-1, https://vs.inf.ethz.ch/publ/papers/Credit_TermDet.pdf#page=4). This generalizes to a small local set S of exponents updated by binary addition. The environment keeps the missing credit as a set DEBTS of distinct exponents and updates it by binary subtraction with carries; its size is bounded by the number of outstanding shares (p.5). Variants: a LIMIT on the exponent, beyond which a process returns its credit and gets a fresh credit 0 from the environment (p.8); control messages that trail the activation messages, splitting as needed (p.6); and a symmetric variant with no distinguished environment, where 'any process may initiate the detection algorithm'. In that variant the control messages must carry the initiator's identity (https://vs.inf.ethz.ch/publ/papers/Credit_TermDet.pdf#page=9).
sources.relevance: A lattice form of fuel. Give each agent a credit exponent, and require every local move to conserve the total. The single global ledger (repo open item 'Fuel and heat as fields') then becomes a local law each block can check. The merge rule (k, k -> k-1) is the local refund when two equal shares meet, and LIMIT with fresh credit gives a bounded per-agent state. Credit flowing back to Out until Out holds 1 is completion detection, but every return needs a route to Out. Limit: equal amounts carry no lineage, so credit can do fuel but cannot witness that two copies are twins.

sources.title: The derivation of distributed termination detection algorithms from garbage collection schemes (ACM TOPLAS 15(1)), Tel and Mattern 1993
sources.quote: When a reference is copied, its weight is split among the existing and the new reference
sources.mechanism: Reduction: a virtual object Z is referenced by every active process and every message in transit. Z becomes garbage exactly when the computation has terminated, so a distributed garbage collector gives a termination detector. (a) Weighted reference counting (Bevan; Watson and Watson; attributed to Weng). A copy splits a reference's weight between the old and new reference, and a deletion returns the weight to the object, so no increment messages are needed. Transformed, this gives Mattern's Credit Recovery algorithm. (b) Local reference counting (Ichisugi-Yonezawa; independently Piquer as 'indirect reference counting', and Rudalics). Each node counts the references it holds or passed on (LRC) and remembers FIRST, the node it first got a reference from. A further reference it receives is installed, counted, and immediately answered with a dec. When LRC reaches 0 it sends dec to FIRST. Transformed, this is Dijkstra-Scholten with signals sent eagerly: 'Dijkstra and Scholten's scheme allows to delay the sending of a signal, but otherwise their scheme is identical to our derived algorithm' (https://vs.inf.ethz.ch/publ/papers/TermDet_Garb_coll.pdf#page=26). The paper notes 'each process only needs a pointer (FIRST) and a counter (LRC)' and that the central-controller bottleneck is avoided. Z is still the root, but it is not contacted on every message. (c) Generational reference counting (Goldberg) gives a detector whose central controller Z keeps an ActCount array per generation (p.22), so it is not local. Weight underflow: a minimum weight cannot be split. WRC then makes an indirection object with maximal count and points the reference at it, and Credit Recovery 'negotiates with Z to exchange its (minimal) credit for a new, maximal credit' (https://vs.inf.ethz.ch/publ/papers/TermDet_Garb_coll.pdf#page=21).
sources.relevance: Gives disp's core a design axis. Copy history can live in labels (weights: nothing kept, no lineage) or in topology (local reference counting / Dijkstra-Scholten: a copy tree kept, then collapsed). A hybrid: keep a few credit bits per agent, and when they run out, spawn an indirection node with fresh weight (which acts as a Dijkstra-Scholten node). Topology is then paid for only once per 2^bits copies, keeping agents bounded. It also warns against schemes needing a central per-generation table.

sources.title: Checking interference with fractional permissions (SAS 2003; author preprint via Wayback), Boyland 2003
sources.quote: manufacture arbitrarily many read permissions without copying a permission: we split permissions
sources.mechanism: A type system of linear capabilities ('permissions') over a small imperative language with parallel composition. A permission for a location carries a fraction in (0,1]. Reading needs any positive fraction; writing needs the whole ('reads can be permitted with fractional permissions whereas writes require complete permissions', #page=1). Permissions are never copied: to give many readers access you split one, and since 'each piece has a definite fraction' you can tell when all the pieces have come back. Permissions are threaded through sequential composition, and are split into two for parallel composition and recombined afterwards (https://web.archive.org/web/20160913040235id_/http://www.cs.uwm.edu/~boyland/papers/permissions.pdf#page=10). Theorem 1 (p.14): for a well-typed, permission-checked program, terminating evaluation always leads to an isomorphic store, so the nondeterminism of parallel evaluation cannot affect the result. The check is static.
sources.relevance: Gives a type-level rule for reuse instead of copy. In a reversible update (a, b) -> (a, a+b), a needs only a fraction (it is read, as a control) and b needs the whole (it is written, as the target). Since a and b would need more than 1 in total if aliased, `b += b` cannot type. That is the condition that keeps the update invertible. disp's verifier could check fractions on annotations in `open use`d modules. Erasing would need the whole permission, which marks the only place heat is charged. Dropping a fraction gives it back, which is free because the value lives on in the other holders.

sources.title: Permission accounting in separation logic (POPL 2005), Bornat, Calcagno, O'Hearn and Parkinson
sources.quote: only a source with no split-off children gives total read/write/dispose ownership
sources.mechanism: Fractional points-to: a heap cell held at fraction z in (0,1], which can be split into two smaller fractions and recombined. Only z=1 allows write and dispose, and any fraction below 1 guarantees passivity (the command cannot change the cell, p.5-6). Counting permissions: a source records how many read tokens have been split off from it. Tokens cannot be split further, and only a source with zero outstanding tokens has total ownership (the paper's analogy is flint knapping). It names the hard part: 'How many read permissions make a total permission? Clearly, you need them all' (http://www0.cs.ucl.ac.uk/staff/p.ohearn/papers/permissions_paper.pdf#page=2). It prefers fractions as 'more convenient to use than history-based mechanisms like sets of binary trees' (#page=5).
