It also shows a pitfall: halves of a cell combine whatever their origin, so a tree predicate with fractional permission can describe a heap that 'contains a DAG, not a tree' (http://www0.cs.ucl.ac.uk/staff/p.ohearn/papers/permissions_paper.pdf#page=10, continued on p.11).
sources.relevance: Names the two disciplines disp has to choose between: fractions (anyone can split, to any depth, without the owner) and counting (one source counts anonymous tokens). On a bounded-degree lattice, counting would have to become a tree of fan nodes (Dijkstra-Scholten-like), and fractions become credit exponents; both of these are the sweep's mapping. The DAG pitfall shows why a numeric amount cannot certify that two copies are twins.

sources.title: A fresh look at separation algebras and share accounting (APLAS 2009), Dockins, Hobor and Appel
sources.quote: The disjointness property is that no nonempty share joins with itself
sources.mechanism: Tree shares: 'binary trees with Boolean-valued leaves and unlabeled internal nodes' (https://www.cs.princeton.edu/~appel/papers/fresh-sa.pdf#page=13), kept canonical (a subtree with all leaves equal folds into one leaf). The order and the lattice operations are leaf-wise: least upper bound = pointwise OR, greatest lower bound = pointwise AND, and complement. Two shares join when they are disjoint (their meet is empty), and the result is their union. Split s gives two shares by recursively replacing each full leaf with (full, empty) and (empty, full) respectively (https://www.cs.princeton.edu/~appel/papers/fresh-sa.pdf#page=14). The model satisfies disjointness, cross-split and infinite splittability. Token counting is embedded through (co)finite subsets of N, and equality is decided by structural comparison. The fractional and counting models satisfy positivity but not disjointness (p.10-11). This is a model for program logics (used for static verification), not a runtime protocol.
sources.relevance: Gives a local label that can witness twins. A duplicator splits its share s into split_L(s) and split_R(s). Two agents that meet can test whether their shares are exactly the two halves of their join (compute p = x OR y, split p, compare), which is a bounded label comparison with no table. If so, they may fuse back (un-copy). Disjointness means a duplicated share is invalid as soon as it is combined with its clone. Shares are binary trees, so disp could store them as tree-calculus values. Compared with numeric credit: the same conservation, but with lineage. Labels grow about one level per copy, so they need the underflow trick to stay bounded.

sources.title: Abstract read permissions: fractional permissions without the fractions (VMCAI 2013), Heule, Leino, Mueller and Summers
sources.quote: This allows the caller to regain the same amount of permission that it gave away
sources.mechanism: Specifications write acc(x.f, rd) instead of a concrete fraction. At each call the verifier picks an amount pi_call that is positive and strictly smaller than what the caller holds. It never reveals pi_call: it encodes it symbolically (p.7). The same pi_call interprets rd in both the pre- and postcondition, so the caller gets back exactly what it gave. Forks take strictly smaller amounts in the same way, which makes the parallel recursive evaluation (Listing 3) verifiable. With concrete fractions or counting permissions it is not, because the first fork takes all the permission (https://pm.inf.ethz.ch/publications/HeuleLeinoMuellerSummers13.pdf#page=4). Implemented in Chalice.
sources.relevance: Suggests a borrow need not store amounts at all. A borrow is identified by the wire it went out on, and 'give back what you got' is enforced by returning along that same wire, as with a Dijkstra-Scholten signal. disp annotations could type reuse-instead-of-copy as an abstract read, with no fraction arithmetic. The wire-identity mapping is the sweep's extrapolation; in the paper the call itself plays that role.

sources.title: Iris from the ground up: a modular foundation for higher-order concurrent separation logic (JFP 28), Jung, Krebbers, Jourdan, Bizjak, Birkedal and Dreyer 2018
sources.quote: is to make sure multiple parties can agree upon which value
sources.mechanism: Ghost state is drawn from a user-chosen resource algebra (RA): a commutative composition with a validity predicate and a duplicable 'core'. RAs differ from partial commutative monoids: 'Instead of partiality, RAs use validity to rule out invalid combinations of ownership' (https://people.mpi-sws.org/~dreyer/papers/iris-ground-up/paper.pdf#page=9). A frame-preserving update a ~> b requires that for every frame c, valid(a.c) implies valid(b.c), so 'a frame-preserving update is guaranteed not to invalidate the resources of concurrently running threads' (https://people.mpi-sws.org/~dreyer/papers/iris-ground-up/paper.pdf#page=12). Standard building blocks: exclusive (a single owner); agreement, whose task is 'to make sure multiple parties can agree upon which value' was picked (#page=18), with ag(x).ag(y) valid only if x=y and agreement elements duplicable; fractional permissions obtained as a particular RA (p.60); and authoritative, which ties a full authoritative element to the fragments handed out, 'making sure that the fragments are always a "part" of the authoritative state' (p.48).
sources.relevance: A specification language for the substrate's conservation law. Give each agent an RA element (credit x tree share x agreement on value), and require every interaction rule to be a frame-preserving update. A check like `validate()` in evaluators/rust-ca-lattice/crate/src/rules.rs, which already checks every rule's wiring is a perfect matching, could check this mechanically over the finite agent alphabet. Agreement captures 'copying and un-copying values known equal is free' algebraically, since agreement elements are duplicable. Only exclusive things would cost heat to erase. The heat reading is the sweep's interpretation.

sources.title: Orca: GC and type system co-design for actor languages (PACMPL 1, OOPSLA 2017), Clebsch, Franco, Drossopoulou, Yang, Wrigstad and Vitek
sources.quote: Consistency means that LRC + OMC = FRC + AMC
sources.mechanism: The garbage collector of the Pony runtime. Reference capabilities (iso: writable, other actors may neither read nor write; val: immutable and shareable; tag: opaque, identity only) make programs data-race free, so per-actor tracing and cross-actor counting need no synchronization. Each actor collects its own heap. Objects shared across actors are reference counted: LRC is the owner's count, FRC the sum of the other actors' counts, AMC the application messages from which the object is reachable, and OMC the INC/DEC messages in flight. Invariant: LRC + OMC = FRC + AMC. A sender passing on a remote object it does not own just decrements its own FRC (and AMC rises), with no message to the owner. If its FRC is too small to decrement ('we cannot decrease it to zero'), it inflates FRC by a constant GCINC and sends an acquire message to the owner (https://www.ponylang.io/media/papers/orca_gc_and_type_system_co-design_for_actor_languages.pdf#page=12). There are no stop-the-world steps. Per-actor counts are kept in hash maps (orcs, arcs) keyed by object.
sources.relevance: Shows that capabilities plus split-on-send counts work at scale and remove synchronization. Every tree-calculus value is immutable, so in Pony's terms every disp value is val: borrowing is always safe, and only the decision to erase (am I the last holder?) needs the count. 'Inflate and tell the owner' is the underflow trick running in production. The counts are keyed by object address, so the scheme is not lattice-local as is.

key_ideas: Fuel as a conserved credit carried by agents. Each agent holds a credit exponent k (share 2^-k). A copy splits it (k -> k+1, k+1), and two equal shares that meet can merge (k, k -> k-1). If every local move keeps the total, the global ledger becomes a law each block checks; only completion detection still needs credit routed back to a root. Sources: Mattern 1989 (rules R1-R4 and the CR = CREDIT merge, p.3-4); Tel and Mattern 1993 (weighted reference counting, p.18).

Twins witnessed by tree shares. A duplicator splits its share s into split_L(s) and split_R(s). An un-copy is allowed exactly when two meeting shares are the two halves of their join (x, y = split(x OR y)), a bounded label comparison with no record table. Plain joinability is not enough, because any two disjoint shares join. Disjointness makes a duplicated share invalid once it is combined with its clone. Numeric credit cannot do this, because equal amounts carry no lineage. Sources: Dockins, Hobor and Appel 2009 (p.13-14); Bornat et al. 2005 (DAG pitfall, p.10-11).

Records as physical engaged nodes. The substrate's history becomes a Dijkstra-Scholten engagement tree: each fired duplicator or rewrite stays as an agent holding its outstanding outputs and a parent wire. Return signals climb back, a node collapses when all its outputs are answered (refund), and Out back at neutral means the net is finished, with no observer. If extra engagements are answered at once (the Tel-Mattern / local-reference-counting form), per-agent state is one counter plus one parent pointer. Sources: Dijkstra and Scholten 1980; Tel and Mattern 1993 (local reference counting, p.23-26).

Bounded-state hybrid: history lives in labels until they run out of bits, then in topology. When a credit or share label runs out of bits, spawn an indirection node with fresh credit; kept history then costs one node per 2^b copies. Sources: Tel and Mattern 1993 (weight underflow and indirection object, p.21); Mattern 1989 (LIMIT and fresh credit, p.8); Orca 2017 (GCINC inflate-and-acquire, p.12).

Borrow instead of copy. Reading takes a split of the permission, while writing or erasing needs the whole. Giving a fraction back, or un-copying, is free because the value survives in another holder; erasing at whole permission is where heat would be charged. This is a local, typed form of the repo's 'a copy goes back free' rule. Sources: Boyland 2003; Bornat et al. 2005 (passivity); Orca 2017 (immutable val sharing).

Fractional permissions as the reversible control/target rule. In (a, b) -> (a, a+b), a is borrowed (a control) and b is owned whole (the target), so a and b cannot be aliased, which is what keeps the update invertible. After the add, a's borrow returns and its edge collapses, so the add leaves no history. Sources: Boyland 2003; Dijkstra and Scholten 1980.

Abstract borrows: store no amounts. A borrow is identified by the wire it left on and must come back on the same wire, so neither the agent nor the type needs fraction arithmetic. Sources: Heule et al. 2013 (the same symbolic pi_call returned, p.9); Dijkstra and Scholten 1980.

Frame-preserving updates as the locality check for rules. Give each agent an element of a resource algebra (exclusive x fractional x agreement x tree share) and require each interaction rule to be valid against every frame. A validate()-style check (like the perfect-matching check in evaluators/rust-ca-lattice/crate/src/rules.rs) could verify this over the finite alphabet. Agreement elements are duplicable, so copying and un-copying agreed-equal values is free. Source: Iris 2018 (p.9, 12, 18).

Completion without an observer. Credit (or deficit) flows back to a root, and the root holding all of it (or being neutral again) means nothing is left running. This needs a root, which disp nets have (Out); rootless variants need initiator identities. Sources: Mattern 1989 (Theorem 1; symmetric variant p.9); Dijkstra and Scholten 1980 (Theorem 2).

Termination detection is garbage collection of a virtual object that every active thing references. One mechanism (credit or engagement edges) can therefore answer both 'is this value dead, so erase it with heat' and 'is the computation done'. Source: Tel and Mattern 1993.
